articleTitle: Simultaneous Continuous- and Discrete-Time Unknown Input Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study presents a simultaneous continuous- and discrete-time unknown input filtering for both linear time-invariant continuous- and discrete-time stochastic systems with arbitrary unknown inputs. This new approach proposes a system reformation technique to transform the original linear time-invariant system into one that can reflect all online estimable unknown inputs on the output equation. Using a hybrid unknown input filtering method, the simultaneous estimation of unknown inputs and states for both the continuous- and discrete-time systems can be achieved. The relationship with the existing optimal continuous-time input and state filter is also addressed.

articleTitle: A THz Measurement Technique of Large Aperture Antenna based on Compact Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The measurement of the RF performance for large reflector antennas at THz frequencies becomes a big challenge with the development of THz technology. This article introduced a 40GHz-500GHz THz antenna measurement technique based on dual-reflector compact range. With redesign and optimization of Feed, system RF link, software. The updated THz compact range can achieve measurements of RF performances of 40GHz-500GHz large reflector antennas, such as pattern, beam width, boresight, antenna gain etc.

articleTitle: Research on Document Image Binarization: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the digital age, the majority of paper documents are converted into electronic formats for preservation purposes. However, the conversion process can result in significant degradation of the document images, which can subsequently lead to difficulties in reading, text recognition, and other digitisation processes. Document image binarisation is a crucial pre-processing step for automatic document recognition and data analysis. The effectiveness of this binarisation directly impacts the accuracy of the digitisation operation. This paper presents a summary of the research results based on traditional thresholding methods, image feature methods and some learning methods, as well as the evaluation indexes of binarisation performance. It also discusses the characteristics and limitations of these methods. Finally, it presents a summary of relevant methods for document image binarisation and points out several promising research directions.

articleTitle: Robust DOA Estimation Against Outliers Based on Bias-compensated Adaptive Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation approach utilizing the adaptive nulling array framework has gained widespread attention due to its low complexity. However, in impulsive noise environments, traditional least mean squares (LMS) algorithm may experience a sharp decline in performance or even fail to work properly. To address this challenge, we propose a DOA estimation approach designed for impulsive noise situations based on a robust nonlinear function. In addition, the algorithm can mitigate bias caused by auxiliary array noise and uses the variable step-size strategy to enhance its performance. Furthermore, the mean stability of the proposed approach is also assessed. Simulation results demonstrate its superior performance in impulsive noise environments.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band LiShu Guo-Shaped Patch Antenna for 5G/B5G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a unique LiShu Guo-shaped patch antenna design. The antenna features an L-shaped feeding probe and utilizes characteristic mode analysis to optimize the feeding position, resulting in the creation of an upper band around 3.5 GHz. With dual impedance bandwidths ranging from 2.15 to 2.90 GHz and 3.45 to 3.51 GHz, the antenna exhibits impressive average peak gains of 6.9 dBi and 7.6 dBi, respectively. These findings highlight the antenna's potential for 5G/B5G networks, making it a promising choice for such applications.

articleTitle: A Novelty Signal Reconstruction Method of Millimeter Wave Fuze Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the digitization process of millimeter wave fuze signal processing circuits, the traditional Nyquist sampling theorem requires a high sampling rate, which necessitates the transmission and storage of large data samples at the receiving end, resulting in significant waste of hardware memory space. Therefore, it is urgently needed to change the traditional data acquisition method to alleviate the data storage pressure on the radio fuze receiver. This paper applies compressed sensing technology to millimeter wave fuze systems and proposes a signal sampling and reconstruction method based on compressed sensing. Simulation experiments verify that the proposed method performs well in sampling and reconstructing the original signal, significantly reducing the number of sampling points and the equivalent sampling rate. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the number of samples to alleviate the storage and transmission pressure on the fuze receiver.

articleTitle: Iterative Equal-scale Defocused Frequency Domain Stitching Phase Retrieval Techniques Based on the Phase Transfer Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This article provides an iterative equal-scale defocused Frequency domain stitching phase retrieval technique based on the phase transfer function (IEDFS-PTF). This technique can be utilized for single-beam phase recovery environment of the terahertz compact antenna test range and other phase retrieval scenarios with drastically changing phase distributions. IEDFS-PTF is obtained by combining the equal-scale defocused Frequency domain stitching phase retrieval technique (EDFS-PTF) with the multi-plane angle spectrum iteration technique. In the presence of noise, IEDFS-PTF has a better recovery effect than the traditional multi-plane phase retrieval technology. Compared with EDFS-PTF, angular spectral iterative technique has no approximate and omitted operations, but traditional iterative techniques inevitably converge to a partial minimum. IEDFS-PTF combines angular spectrum iteration and EDFS-PTF to successfully suppress the drawbacks of both. The simulation results show that even when the phase distribution varies drastically, the phase root-mean-square error remains below 0.05 until the noise standard deviation exceeds 0.06.

articleTitle: Cross-Language Code Development with Generative AI: A Source-to-Source Translation Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Since the release of ChatGPT in November 2022, there is growing interest around the world on exploring the capabilities of generative AI tools. In addition to text, image, audio, and video generation, these tools are also able to generate program codes. In this paper, strategies for students, programmers and enthusiasts to understand the prompting methods to generate codes in multiple languages by translating source code written in one language to another target language using generative AI is explored. The prompts are created to test the ability of generative AI to create codes in C, Java, C++, and Python. Some of the methods of generating the complete program using limited original source code statements is presented. In summary, while generating source code in a target language, generative AI tools downplay the significance of accuracy of statements written in original language, syntax, semantics, as well as missing statements in a program. Irrespective of these, generative AI tools are still able to generate complete code in a target language by correcting errors.

articleTitle: Improvement Plan for cyber-security of DCS Control System of Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This article proposes a cyber-security improvement plan for the DCS control system of nuclear power plants. Firstly, a brief introduction was given to the traditional architecture of DCS control systems of nuclear power plants. Secondly, the current cyber-security risks faced by DCS control systems in nuclear power plants were summarized, including identity authentication issues, access control issues, communication protocol issues, and data storage issues. Based on the cyber-security risks faced by the DCS control system in nuclear power plants, an improvement plan has been proposed for the DCS platform without increasing external cyber-security equipment. Firstly, regarding identity authentication, it is proposed that nuclear power plants have a very good physical protection that can effectively protect the operator station. However, for the engineer station, a dual factor identity authentication method needs to be added. Secondly, regarding access control, the shortcomings of role-based access control models were pointed out, and a location-based and task-based access control model was proposed. Then, in terms of security communication networks, the sensitive data range of nuclear power plants was analyzed, and communication was divided into internal communication and external communication. For internal communication, pre-stored keys can be used for encrypted communication. For external communication, certificates should be used for identity authentication, and then encrypted communication should be carried out. Finally, for data integrity, control system configurations can be saved through encryption. For passwords, they can be transmitted and saved through hash values.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Optimization Methodology for 2.5-D Advanced Package Considering Thermal and Power Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a collaborative optimization methodology for 2.5-D advanced package considering thermal and power integrity is proposed. A design flow including thermally-aware placement and decoupling capacitor optimization is driven by an improved adaptive genetic algorithm. In the first stage, the methodology comprehends the critical design indexes such as the area, wirelength and temperature. Based on the determined placement, the on-chip decoupling capacitor optimization task is conducted to suppress the impedance of the cascaded power delivery network. The developed methodology provides a new paradigm of electronic design automation tools for complex 2.5-D integrated microsystem in the future.

articleTitle: High Degree of Freedom Low Coupling Sparse MIMO Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: To achieve high precision direction-of-arrival estimation of MIMO arrays in highly coupled environments, based on the difference and cooperative array principles, the uniform array fitted with 5 base layer array and the uniform array fitted with 6 base layer array were used as transmitting arrays, and with the addition of 1 base layer layer sparse array as receiving array, two sparse multi-in multiple-out arrays were designed for single-base radar, which have the characteristics of low coupling of transmitting array and high freedom of receiving array.

articleTitle: Integrated Method of Deep Learning and Large Language Model in Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This research explores the integration of deep learning and large language models in speech recognition to improve accuracy and handle complex contexts. Deep neural network (DNN), convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory network (LSTM), and Transformer-based large language model are used to build an integrated acoustic and language model framework. Experiments on TIMIT, LibriSpeech, and Common Voice datasets show that the ensemble model significantly improves both word error rate (WER) and real-time factor (RTF) compared to traditional models. The model demonstrates superior performance in adaptability to multiple languages and accent changes. The results suggest that technology integration can effectively enhance the performance of speech recognition systems in complex environments, providing new directions for future development.

articleTitle: An Effective Control Strategy for Propagation Constants of Stub-Loaded Endfire Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper introduces a recently proposed effective control strategy for the propagation constants of endfire leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with two kinds of loading stubs within and at two sides of the coplanar stripline to adjust the phase and attenuation constants separately. The inner stubs can decide the phase constant value of the proposed LWA, while the outer ones are employed to control the attenuation constant in a large range with weak influence on the phase constant value. The designed LWA can also maintain the phase value and slope in the operation range under different attenuation constants. In this way, a specific radiation pattern can be acquired easily in a frequency range by tailoring the current amplitude along the antenna with matched phase. An endfire LWA with low sidelobe pattern is designed and fabricated to verify the effectiveness of provided method in controlling propagation constants separately. The well-matched results between simulation and measurement confirm the predicted radiation properties of the designed LWA, and the proposed strategy can modify the attenuation constants effectively with almost fixed phase results in the endfire operation range.

articleTitle: Study on A Packed Bed Dielectric Barrier Discharge Plasma Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified r-z two-dimensional axisymmetric fluid model of packed bed dielectric barrier discharge is established to simulate the effect of the packed bead with sharp edges on plasma discharge. The results show that due to the polarization effect of the packed bead, the electric field at the sharp edges of the packed bead increases, which has a positive significance for reducing the energy consumption of the DBD reactor. Increasing the dielectric constant of the packed beads will promote the plasma discharge in the reactor and make the plasma generation faster. At the same time, the voltage amplitude has a great influence on the plasma discharge. In a certain range, Increasing the voltage leads to the increase of the electric field in the reactor, and the distortion of the electric field at the sharp edge of the packed bead increases, which promotes the increase of the plasma density. Therefore, this study is of great significance to better understand the plasma characteristic behavior of the ring packed bed DBD reactor.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Microstrip Patch Antenna with the Profile of 1.6 mm Covering 3.14~5.51 GHz for 5G Mobile Terminal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Due to the urgent demand for multi-generation communication technology and multi-band mobile terminal applications, more antennas with diverse functions are needed to cover the frequency bands required by practical applications. However, most of the existing mobile antennas are wire antennas, which are mainly concentrated on the metal bezel of the terminals, making the metal bezel so crowded. To relieve the great pressure of the metal bezel, the ultra-wideband patch antenna with a low profile of 1.6 mm about 0.017 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> refers to the lowest frequency of the operation band) is adopted for covering 3.14~5.51 GHz (including 5G N77/N78/N79) on the back cover and it can reduce the number of the antennas on the metal bezel. The first two characteristic modes of the half-mode patch antenna are used and the magnetic-coupling method is adopted to generate additional resonances to widen the bandwidth. As a result, the proposed patch antenna achieves ultra-wideband and low profile. The measured results show that the proposed mobile patch antenna obtains a bandwidth of 3.14~5.51 GHz (54.8%) with a total efficiency higher than -1.7 dB (67.6%), which has great potential to be applied in 5G mobile terminal devices.

articleTitle: Dependable Pipeline Detection algorithms for GPRs in Obscuration Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: We propose a robust pipeline detection algorithm for obscuration environments, which includes two improvements: a pre-processing method called the Regional Adaptive Thresh-olding Algorithm (RATA) and a novel clustering method based on trend analysis and symmetric matching called as Symmetry Matching Clustering Algorithm (SMCA). This approach is highly effective in extracting targets from low-intensity regions and has been validated through simulation experiments. The gotten results demonstrate significant enhancements in the accuracy and reliability of underground pipeline detection in obscuration environments. Comparative analysis shows that, in some aspects, the proposed method outperforms existing algorithms.

articleTitle: A Study on the Wide-Angle Stability of Programmable Metasurfaces with Rectangular and Triangular Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of different array grid types on the wide-angle characteristics of programmable metasurfaces. Metasurfaces typically employ rectangular grid distributions, however, such metasurfaces often exhibit poor amplitude characteristics at large incident angles. In array antennas, triangular grids alter the spacing between elements, generally providing better coupling characteristics and large-angle scanning capabilities. Therefore, this paper focuses on discussing the impact of these two grid types on the encoding stability of reflective metasurfaces at large incident angles, exploring the potential of triangular grid layouts in the design of wide-angle metasurfaces. Two different types of metasurfaces elements under various grid array configurations have been analyzed. Numerical simulations indicate that, for the same element, triangular grid arrays exhibit better wide-angle stability in encoding characteristics compared to rectangular grid arrays.

articleTitle: Overview of Anti-chaff Interference of Radio Fuze
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Chaff formed by airborne chaff projectiles is a common interference faced by radio fuze of air-to-air missiles and air defense missiles, which seriously affects the effectiveness of missile guidance systems. Anti-chaff interference is an urgent problem for radio fuze. The study of anti-chaff interference of radio fuze can greatly enhance the operational performance of radio fuze. This paper firstly briefly describes the development status of chaff jamming, and then summarizes the research status of anti-chaff jamming methods for radio fuze. Then this paper introduces the anti-chaff jamming methods based on spectral spreading, polarization characteristics, Doppler difference, echo signal characteristics, machine learning and so on. Finally, it summarizes the problems faced by the anti-chaff jamming technology of radio fuze, and gives an outlook on its development prospect.

articleTitle: FEM Simulation of Hybrid-2DLMs-based Plasma Array Structure Used in Confrontation with High-Power Microwave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In recent years, the issue of how to efficiently and accurately confront high-power microwaves (HPM) has increasingly become a hot research topic. This article focuses on the effect of the electric field strength and frequency of HPM and initial electron density of the monolayer cylindrical plasma array on electron avalanche effect of plasma, revealing the general rules of plasma used for confrontation against HPM by finite element method(FEM). In this article, a monolayer plasma shielding structure based on the two-dimensional materials of graphene and black phosphorus is proposed.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale SE-SK Network for Human Falling Detection using IR-UWB Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) radars are increasingly utilized for human fall detection owing to their non-contact, high precision, and high privacy attributes. However, the existing single-branch networks-based methods on falling detection only extract single feature maps, and fail to capture complete fall information. Furthermore, processing multiple spectra without the target unique feature results in feature loss after fusion, leading to decreased accuracy. This paper proposes a novel multi-scale network, which combines squeeze-and-excitation (SE) and selective kernel (SK) (SE-SK) networks, for human falling detection using IR-UWB Radars. Specifically, three features spectra of IR-UWB Radar data, that is, the time-Doppler, range-Doppler, and range-time feature spectra, are firstly obtained through the pre-processing of the radar echoes. Then, a multiscale SE-SK network is developed for human falling detection. Experimental results demonstrate improved performance with detection accuracy of 98.2% compared to the existing singlebranch networks-based method.

articleTitle: Securing Near-Field MIMO Communications via Dynamic Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Secure transmission is challenging for wireless systems because the open nature of wireless channels leads to vulnerability to malicious attacks by eavesdroppers. Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) are promising technologies that have great potential to significantly improve secure communication performance. Therefore, this paper introduce DMA to a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications system with an eavesdropper. Due to the high carrier frequency and large antenna aperture, both the receiver and eavesdropper are located in the near-field region. The formulated nonconvex optimization problem is to jointly design the digital precoding vector and the DMA weight matrix via alternating optimization (AO) algorithm for maximizing the secrecy capacity. In the proposed scheme, a closed-form expression of the optimal digital precoding vector is derived, and the DMA weight matrix is optimized by using successive convex approximation and the Majorization-Minimization (MM) algorithm. Numerical results validate the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Classification Method for Vibration Signals Based on Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Due to the complexity of fiber optic vibration signals, using traditional classification methods to classify signals is inaccurate. Effective fiber optic sensor data classification has become an important research topic. Machine learning methods have been proposed for intelligent signal recognition and classification. This study aims to explore the use of machine learning methods to recognize and classify collected signals intelligently. The vibration signal data collected from the fiber optic sensors is first preprocessed, including removing trend terms and applying smoothing filters. Then, time-domain and frequency-domain features are extracted separately to construct a dataset for training and testing purposes. This paper focuses on the classification results of the Random Forest (RF) classifier and compares it with three other machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Back Propagation Neural Network (BP), and Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBF). The results show that the Random Forest model optimized through feature selection outperforms other models in terms of classification accuracy, recall rate, and F1 score.

articleTitle: A Fuze-oriented Multi-parameter Energy-type Interference Environment Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the modern battlefield, fuzes face complex interference from the high-power microwave electromagnetic environment, which greatly affects the detection effect of radio fuzes. The research of energy-based interference environment modeling technology can provide technical support for fuzes to cope with high-power electromagnetic pulse weapons on the future battlefield. In this study, an energy-based interference environment model was proposed, and the effects of transmit power, antenna beam and placement position on the trajectory environment of the fuze were modeled. By comparing with the measured data, the peak field strength error obtained by the model proposed in this paper is less than 12% for both ultra-broad spectrum and narrow-band high power sources, which has good simulation results and has potential application in the field of fuze electromagnetic protection evaluation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Microfluidic Microwave Sensor Based on Taiji Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Microwave sensor plays an important role in industrial control, medical diagnosis, environmental monitoring and other fields as an important wireless sensing technology. However, traditional microwave sensors have limitations in terms of sensitivity and cost. The aim of this study is to design a microwave sensor based on Taiji resonator using simulation technology to improve its performance index and explore its potential value in practical applications. Through the analysis and evaluation of the simulation results, it is found that the microwave sensor of Taiji resonator has higher sensitivity and stability, and has lower cost and manufacturing complexity, which provides a new idea and possibility for the further development of microwave sensor technology.

articleTitle: Research on Radar Cross Section Measurement Based on Terahertz Radar Near-Field High Resolution Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) measurement is an important way for understanding terahertz scattering characteristics of targets. Terahertz RCS measurement has high requirements for the background environment. This paper proposes a RCS measurement method based on terahertz near-field high resolution imaging system. Firstly, a convolution back projection algorithm model for near-field compensation is proposed to achieve precise imaging of targets with large rotation angle. Then, different window functions in image domain are designed to extract the target’s scattering distribution and filter out the background interference. Finally, the RCS is retrieved through inverse Fourier transform of the extracted scattering distribution. By measurement of several typical targets, it is shown that the proposed measurement method can obtain the RCS of the targets at different angles through a single 360° rotation imaging, and the accuracy of RCS measurement is improved and the dynamic range of measurement is expanded obviously.

articleTitle: Efficient Gas Breakdown Analysis Method for Transient Physical Models Based on Implicit Differencing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The article analyzes gas breakdown phenomenon in high-power microwave devices and establishes a model to describe this transient process. First, the breakdown threshold was calculated using the spectral element in time domain (SETD) method and compared with the SPARK3D software, the results match very well. Then, the spatial discretization is carried out, and then, the implicit difference format is used for the temporal difference. Subsequently, through formula derivation combined with SETD, the transient electron density before and after the gas breakdown is calculated, and an electron density distribution diagram is plotted, which is consistent with the physical significance of gas breakdown.

articleTitle: Design of Narrow-pulse Laser Transmitter Circuit for High-precision Pulse Laser Proximity Fuze System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: To address the problems of low ranging accuracy and high power consumption caused by the long rise time and wide pulse width of the laser transmitter in the pulse laser proximity fuze, we propose a new design of narrow-pulse laser transmitter circuit for high-precision laser proximity fuze. The circuit adopts high-speed logic gate delay for pulse width control, generates pulse signals with short rise time and narrow pulse width, and drives GaN FET through GaN FET driver to control the fast discharging of the energy storage capacitor to the laser, so as to realize the laser transmitter with short rise time and narrow pulse width. Simulation combined with the actual circuit test results demonstrate that the circuit can be stabilized to launch a narrow pulse laser with a rising edge of less than 2ns, a pulse width of less than 10ns, and a peak current of not less than 27A, which can effectively improve the ranging accuracy and reduce the power consumption of the pulse laser proximity fuze system.

articleTitle: A 205 GHz Fully integrated Power Amplifier in 40-nm CMOS at Near-fmax Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a 195-213 GHz power amplifier(PA) is presented, operating at far beyond half of the maximun oscillator frequency(f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>). Adopting unilateral signal feed(USF), the layout of NMOS core has been optimized, which has improved f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>. The power gain of PA is boosted by using the gain-plane approach, in the case of low inherent power gain of the transistor. Based on the above methods, a four-stage pseudo-differential amplifier is designed in 40-nm CMOS technology. The simulation results show that the PA achieves 4 dbm for P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> at 205 GHz, with a maximun power gain of 11.5 dB from 195 to 213 GHz, achieving 82% of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>.

articleTitle: Lung Nodule Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5 Network Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A YOLOV5-based lung nodule detection algorithm is proposed to enhance the detection effect of convolutional neural network for lung nodule detection and lower the risk of misdiagnosis. This solves the issues of low detection accuracy and inaccurate localization of the model prediction frame in the field of lung nodule detection. To increase the model's performance and accuracy, a dense convolutional network (DenseNet) network structure is first suggested based on the YOLOV5 model. This dense convolutional network is employed in place of the original feature extraction network. Second, the original loss function is replaced with the SIOU boundary loss function, which makes the model more cognizant of the target's form and placement and lowers the rate of false positives and leaks. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method's precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP) improve from 81.9% to 87.6%, 77.9% to 81.4%, and 84.2% to 87.7%, respectively, when compared to the original YOLOv5 network on the LUNA16 dataset. These improvements indicate that the improved YOLOv5 network has a stronger feature expression capability and increases the sensitivity of automatic lung nodule detection. The enhanced YOLOv5 network may help diagnose lung nodules more successfully and has better feature expression capabilities and increased automatic detection sensitivity.

articleTitle: RCS Analysis of Offshore Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: with the rapid development of renewable energy sources, wind power has emerged as a significant contributor to clean energy. However, the widespread deployment of wind turbines presents challenges related to their radar cross-section (RCS) characteristics. This paper examines the RCS characteristics of offshore wind turbines. It begins by introducing the basic structure of wind turbines and the theoretical foundation of RCS, followed by a discussion of existing research findings and technical methodologies. Subsequently, RCS simulations are conducted for both a single wind turbine and a wind turbine array. Additionally, a numerical simulation model is developed to analyze the effects of frequency and angle on RCS. Finally, the paper concludes by summarizing the key factors influencing the RCS characteristics of wind turbines.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Parallel Data Acquisition System for Inertial Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Arrays can improve the performance of inertial sensors, but the lack of synchronization in acquisition times among sensors is a significant challenge. To address this issue, a data acquisition system has been developed that uses parallel I2C and SPI buses to enhance measurement precision. This study compares the impact of serial and parallel bus architectures and sensor quantity on the efficacy of inertial sensor arrays. The performance indices used for evaluation include zero bias, zero bias stability, and Allan variance. The experiment indicates that the parallel bus significantly enhances the zero bias stability of the sensors. The incorporation of additional sensors reduces stochastic errors, such as angle random walk, quantization noise, and zero bias. The use of a parallel bus configuration enables easy expansion of the sensor count within the array, thereby significantly enhancing the applicative merit of the inertial sensor array.

articleTitle: A Flexible Resource Allocation Algorithm in Dual-Timescale Beam Hopping Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: How to make full use of limited satellite resources and the spatial flexibility of beams to manage these traffic demands is a critical challenge that must be urgently addressed in beam hopping (BH) satellite systems. In this paper, a dual-timescale BH resource allocation algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed. On the large-timescale, a user clustering method that dynamically updates beam coverage cells is used to optimize resource allocation and reduce spatial interference. On the short-timescale, the proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is used to coordinate BH, reduce inter-beam interference, maintain inter-cell delay fairness, and improve system throughput. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed dual-timescale algorithm significantly outperforms the baseline scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of a High-Precision Cavity Optomechanical Accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of a high-precision cavity optomechanical accelerometer. It is composed of a photonic crystal cavity structure and a straight-beam mechanical oscillator structure that are designed on a silicon on SOI (Silicon-On-Insulator) wafer with a top silicon thickness of 500 nm. The working principle of the cavity optomechanical accelerometer is analyzed, the mechanical modes of the mechanical oscillator and the optical modes of the photonic crystal cavity are simulated, the theoretical detection accuracy of the accelerometer is calculated to be $5.86{\text{ug}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $, and the accelerometer samples are further fabricated by using the micro-nano-machining process. The accelerometer is characterized by high sensitivity and low noise, which can be widely used in the fields of high-precision vibration detection, inertial measurement and inertial navigation.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent Infrared Selective Emitter accompanied by Customizable Digital Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a new type of IR selective emitter(ISE) based on five layers of ITO/ZnS is presented. This paper proposes an ISE with excellent selective emission performance in 5 ~ 8 μm undetectable band and high transmittance in visible spectrum. Moreover, the selected emittance material is put on the microwave absorber as a patch. Based on the size of the patch, the four units are arranged as digital pixels, which makes the target emissivity and background emittance more integrated, which is helpful for microwave absorption. This work not only improves the ability of IR emission and heat dissipation, but also improves the application of IR, visible and microwave compatibility.

articleTitle: Overview of the Research Status of Laser Imaging Fuze
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Laser imaging detection technology is an active detection technology that can precisely and rapidly acquire three-dimensional spatial information of targets. Laser imaging fuze, characterized by high resolution, accuracy, and anti-interference capability, have been widely applied in military, mapping, communication, and other fields. This paper presents an overview of the development, working principles, and key technologies of laser imaging fuze, detailing the key technologies involved in three laser imaging detection processes. Currently, laser imaging fuze technology is still in its developmental stage. Due to its potential to significantly enhance the comprehensive performance of laser fuzes in terms of anti-interference and target recognition capabilities, it holds broad application prospects. It is worthy of in-depth research by relevant research institutions to advance the engineering application process of laser imaging fuze.

articleTitle: A Shared-Aperture Dual-Band Array Antenna Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this letter, a 2×2 shared-aperture dual-band array antenna is presented, which utilizes gap waveguide technology to achieve wide bandwidth. The proposed dual-band radiating element consists of two layers of open radiating cavities and a metal cover plate. The cavities are designed as hexagonal structures of different sizes. The lower and upper radiating cavities operate in X-band and Ku-band, respectively. The upper cavity is placed orthogonally relative to the lower cavity for generating different line polarizations and improving the isolation between them. Each cavity is fed by a separate groove gap waveguide. An array is formed and simulated using the proposed dual-band radiating elements. The simulation results show that the -10.0 dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna are 9.8-11.0 GHz in X-band and 14.7-19.0 GHz in Ku-band, respectively. The realized gains are 14.7 dBi (at 10.0 GHz) and 16.7 dBi (at 15.5 GHz) in two different polarizations.

articleTitle: A Novel Window Function for Memristor Model with Short-Term and Long-Term Memory Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Window functions are commonly used in the state equations of memristor models to restrict the variations of corresponding state variables to the defined regions. In this paper, a novel window function is proposed based on the existing Biolek window function. The interval on which state variable is defined changes from [0, 1] in Biolek window function to an interval with adjustable boundaries, and bounds of this interval can be constants or variables or a combination of both. This window function’s independent variable that is related to the change direction of state variable should be chosen according to the structure of the state equation. This window function is used in the memristor model with short-term and long-term memory behavior. Simulation results indicate that the state variables can be limited in their defined intervals when input voltage is applied to the memristor, and this model can be used to mimic the memory and learning behavior of human being.

articleTitle: Design of Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Rasorber with Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable frequency selective rasorber (FSR) based on the fluidity of liquid metal is proposed. It mainly consists of a lossy impedance layer and lossless frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) with liquid metal. Equivalent circuit models are utilized to explain the working mechanism in different statuses. Based on theoretical analysis, the resonant response of FSS is changed from a transmission state to a partly perfect reflection state by controlling the extraction and the injection of liquid metal in microchannels. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed reconfigurable FSR implements status switching successfully among all-pass (2-18GHz), absorption at S-band (2.6-3.6GHz) and absorption at X-band (9.5-10.5GHz) with the corresponding liquid metal state.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Frequency Characteristics of Coupling Windows in Tunable Cavity Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design and research of recent tunable cavity filters, analyzing the frequency variation characteristics of common coupling windows. Based on the coupling structures, we discussed an in-depth analysis and comparison of their coupling characteristics and explained the reasons about why the value of coupling windows changes when tunning the center frequency. Ultimately, we identified several optimum coupling windows types in a specific frequency range (19-21 GHz) that exhibits minimum variation in the coupling coefficient, demonstrating stable performance verified by full-wave EM simulations. This coupling window can be better applied to the design of tunable filters with excellent return loss and insertion loss, high quality factor, and essentially stable bandwidth for the whole tuning range. This finding holds significant engineering importance for the future design and implementation of high-frequency flexible tunable filters.

articleTitle: Deep unfolding based microwave imaging with spin-decoupled programmable metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, the deep unfolding (DU) based microwave imaging method for near-field objects using 1-bit spin-decoupled programmable metasurface (SPM) is studied. First, a 1-bit SPM operating at 12 GHz is designed. Then, the theoretical imaging model is established using the plane-wave angular spectrum approach. Finally, the imaging methods based on the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA) and the learned ISTA are presented. By comparing the imaging results obtained by different methods, it is verified that the designed SPM equipped with the DU method is a promising technique for microwave imaging with excellent performance.

articleTitle: The Influence of Antenna Frequency and Roadway Cross-sectional Area on Radio Wave Propagation in Mine Roadway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the increasing demand for mineral resources, the frequency of coal mining operations has intensified. Consequently, the development of a highly efficient and reliable underground communication system has become a critical concern. This study aims to investigate the radio wave propagation characteristics in mine tunnels by introducing the Finite-Difference TimeDomain (FDTD) algorithm to construct a 3D tunnel electromagnetic field update equation. This equation facilitates the simulation and analysis of radio wave propagation within the tunnel environment. The study specifically examines the impact of antenna emission frequency and tunnel cross-sectional area on the electromagnetic field strength. The findings provide a foundation for further research in channel modeling, modulation techniques, and signal processing algorithms.

articleTitle: MonoMixNet: Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation with a Mixed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Recently, self-supervised monocular depth estimation has attracted widespread attention. This method does not rely on real depth labels but only requires the use of an RGB camera and corresponding algorithms to obtain depth information. Ensuring the effectiveness of depth estimation networks, fully utilizing semantic information, and accurately capturing local details are crucial for improving prediction accuracy. Although many models have achieved satisfactory results by stacking convolutional neural networks(CNNs) and Vision Transformers(ViTs), the former lacks global information in deep networks, while the latter has higher computational complexity and lacks effective design for the decoding end. This paper proposes a hybrid self-supervised monocular depth estimation network that combines convolutional neural networks with self-attention mechanisms and designs a multi-scale feature fusion module(MSFF) to effectively integrate multi-scale features and highlight key detail information. Meanwhile, a feature enrichment module(FEM) is proposed to expand the receptive field through deep networks to capture richer semantic information. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this model, achieving significant performance on the KITTI test set.

articleTitle: Path planning method for maritime drones based on NSGA II algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, based on graph theory and multi-objective optimization theory, the aircraft trajectory planning problem is studied. Firstly, based on the state model of the aircraft, the possible forms of the trajectory line are analyzed, and the 3D Dubins curve smoothing strategy is proposed. Through geometric derivation, a recursive expression for the length of the trajectory line is established, and then the calculation method of the trajectory length based on the 3D Dubins curve is given, and a mathematical model with the objective of minimizing the trajectory length and the number of corrections is established. After that, the above model is solved based on NSGAII algorithm, and the simulation results show that the method of this paper can quickly search the optimal path for maritime drones.

articleTitle: Compact Lowpass Filter Based on Asymmetric Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a newly spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) with asymmetric structure on both sides of the microstrip line is proposed to constitute a compact lowpass filter. There are no additional elements above and below the microstrip line of the asymmetric SSPPs unit, leading to a compact circuit size. Besides, compared with the commonly used symmetric SSPPs structure, the proposed asymmetric bended rectangular-slit SSPPs unit has lower cutoff frequency. Also, the asymptotic frequency of the presented SSPPs unit can be easily controlled by adjusting the lateral direction length of slit. Finally, a compact lowpass filter with the frequency band of 0-9.26 GHz is designed by the proposed SSPPs structure.

articleTitle: A Sea Clutter Suppression Method based on Neighborhood Self-supervised for Ship Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Ship detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images plays a considerable role in ocean monitoring and maritime management. However, due to the complex distributions of sea clutter and the low signal-to-clutter ratio of targets, high-precision ship detection under strong sea clutters is still challenging. A sea clutter suppression method based on neighborhood pixels self-supervised is proposed in this paper for ship detection in SAR images, which comprises the sea clutter suppression stage and the ship detection stage. In the former stage, a Weibull-distribution-based image pre-processing is initially carried out to achieve zero mean normalization of SAR images. Then, a neighborhood sampler based on adjacent pixels of the sea clutter is designed to obtain independent and identically distributed paired image slices for training. Further, a self-supervised network based on U-Net is established with the sampled paired images as input for sea clutter suppression, which does not require any clean ships. In particular, a hybrid loss function including the reconstruction and regularization terms, is customized to ensure the network’s reconstruction and generalization abilities. In the latter stage, a YOLOv5-based detection network is adopted in sea clutter-suppressed images to improve the detection performance of weak ships under complex backgrounds. Experiments conducted on the Large-Scale SAR Ship Detection Dataset-v1.0 (LS-SSDD-v1.0) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which achieves a 0.7% improvement in detection accuracy compared with typical detection algorithms.

articleTitle: W-band CMOS ×8 Frequency Multiplier With High Harmonic Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents an 88-98.2 GHz frequency octupler (× 8) utilizing 55-nm CMOS technology, designed for W-band wireless communication applications. The proposed octupler consists of three stages of push-push frequency doublers (PPDs) and a single stage of a cascode amplifier, featuring low power consumption, high harmonic suppression, and a compact footprint. The octupler achieves a maximum output power of -4.6 dBm at 90 GHz with an input injection power of 6 dBm. Within the frequency range of 88-98.2 GHz, the harmonic suppression ratio (HRR) is better than 43 dBc. The octupler consumes 8.2 mA from a 1.8V supply voltage and occupies a compact size of 0.48 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Statistical Characteristics Analysis based on a Measured Ku-band Sea Clutter Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The complex characteristics of sea clutter affect the performance of sea surface target detectors. Particularly, the statistical properties constrain the development of adaptive detectors. However, the properties of sea clutter are influenced by complex factors, which lead to different characteristics across different radar working frequency bands and sea conditions. This paper mainly analyzes the amplitude characteristics and spatial-temporal correlations of sea clutter based on the real measured dataset. Experimental Ku-band radar sea clutter results show that the empirical probability density function (PDF) is accurately fitted by the Generalized Pareto intensity distribution. Moreover, the decorrelation time of Ku-band measured data is about 1~3ms which is slightly less than that of the X-band radar sea clutter. The results presented in this article serve as a theoretical reference for the development of future target detection methods.

articleTitle: Transmissive Reconfigurable Metasurface for Near-field Focusing in C-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit transmissive reconfigurable metasurface cell loaded with PIN diodes is designed, which can switch two different states to generate a 180-degree phase difference. The meta-atom has a transmission coefficient of greater than 0.7 in the 5-7 GHz and achieves a relative bandwidth of 17% in the C-band. In addition, near-field focusing with adjustable focus is realized by this metasurface, demonstrating the good reconfigurable properties of the transmissive metasurface.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Filtering Dielectric Resonator Antenna based on SIW Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper proposes a circularly polarized (CP) filtering dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) based on a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. The antenna is fed by a stacked feeding network to excite the dipole and DRs. The current is generated by a pair of dipoles and the equivalent magnetic current is generated by DRs. In one cycle, the current and the equivalent magnetic current operate alternately along the same direction with a phase difference of 90°, resulting in a circularly polarized wave. SIW cavity has high-pass transmission characteristics. The reflection coefficient and gain of the antenna show some sideband selective characteristics, which indicates that the antenna has a filtering function. The antenna obtained a relative impedance bandwidth of 26.51% (5.04-6.58 GHz) and an axial ratio bandwidth of 15.6% (5.26-6.16 GHz). With outstanding CP performance and compact size, the proposed CP filtering DRA is an attractive candidate for satellite communications.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of Channel Similarity in the UMa Scenario for 6G FR3 Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the development of the sixth generation (6G) wireless communication, FR3 (7-24 GHz) has gradually become the focus band due to its advantages of wide coverage and high capacity. However, the span of the FR3 is large, and the channel characteristics within the band have not been fully studied. In this paper, we conduct channel measurements campaigns in Urban Macro (UMa) scenario at FR3 using the channel sounder, and analyse the channel similarity. Firstly, channel measurements are conducted in UMa scenario at 11-15 GHz using a time domain channel measurement platform, with three receiver antennas of different beamwidths. Subsequently, the channel impulse response (CIR) similarity in frequency domain and beam domain is analyzed using pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) and temporal power delay distribution correlation coefficient (TPCC) as metrics. Finally, it is found that as the channel frequency interval increases, there is a trend of decreasing channel similarity. Additionally, great differences in antenna beamwidths also lead to lower channel similarity.

articleTitle: Design of a Ku-band ESS with High Shielding Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a Ku-band energy selective surface (ESS) with high shielding effectiveness (SE) is designed for high-power microwave (HPM) protection. The proposed ESS consists of a cascade ABA three-layer structure. By simulating the transmission characteristics of each layer, it is concluded that the structure uses an electromagnetic tunneling effect to achieve enhanced transmission and thus bandpass response. An equivalent circuit model (ECM) is designed and compared with the full-wave simulation results, which show that the insertion loss (IL) is less than 1 dB from 13.5-17 GHz in the low power state, and the average SE is greater than 40 dB in the range of 12-18 GHz under HPM radiation. In addition, the simulated operation of the ESS in the waveguide further demonstrates the feasibility of the structure.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of An Intelligent Automated System for Industrial Lamp Cup Inspection and Grading based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the manufacturing process of lamp cups, the quality of spot inspection directly affects the lighting effect of the lamp cups. Traditional manual inspection methods are inefficient and susceptible to subjective factors. This paper proposes an intelligent lamp spot inspection and grading system based on You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5). The proposed system integrates Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technology and leverages the efficient target detection capabilities of the YOLOv5 algorithm to construct feature models, achieving intelligent automated detection of spot quality and automated grading of lamp cups. Compared with traditional manual detection methods, the designed system effectively improves production efficiency, reduces manual intervention, and provides technical support for the intelligent and automated production of the lamp manufacturing industry. Test experiments are conducted in actual production lines of lamp cups and have verified the effectiveness and real-time performance of the designed system.

articleTitle: Bilinear Interpolation Algorithm Based on Verilog
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper investigates a Verilog-based implementation of a bilinear interpolation algorithm aimed at solving the problem of pixel computation during image enlargement. The bilinear interpolation algorithm, as an effective image processing method, has a wide range of applications in the fields of image processing and computer vision. This algorithm is implemented through the Verilog programming language and includes key steps such as pixel coordinate conversion, nearest neighbor finding, and linear interpolation operations. On hardware platforms such as FPGAs, the use of fixed-point design optimizes the use of resources, improves computational efficiency, and meets real-time requirements. The correctness and effectiveness of the algorithm are verified through simulation tests. This algorithm implementation is characterized by high accuracy and speed and is suitable for real-time image processing applications. This study provides an effective reference method for the design of Verilog-based image processing algorithms, which is of great significance in promoting the development of image processing technology.

articleTitle: Elimination of Interference Analysis for RIS Element Demage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the ability of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) damaged in multi-user environments to eliminate interference. Our research found that even if the RIS is damaged, interference can still be eliminated in the absence of a direct path and when the number of RIS is sufficient. In order to solve interference cancellation, we adopted the alternating projection algorithm, which ensures local convergence and good convergence speed.

articleTitle: A Novel Design Method for a Miniaturized Vertical Interconnection TSV Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents the RF TSV transmission structure with a diameter of 500 micrometers. Through simulation and optimization, a miniaturized vertically interconnected TSV structure is finally designed. Experiments and simulation results confirm the effectiveness and potential application prospects of the new structure. The novel TSV structure presented in this study demonstrates significant potential for enhancing transmission efficiency and reducing occupied space, promising widespread adoption in various advanced technological applications.

articleTitle: Exploratory Application of Dynamic Incremental-based Graph Attention Networks for Financial Fraud Recognition in Listed Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Financial fraud, involving the fabrication of assets, revenues, and profits by certain listed companies, aims to mislead users of financial statements and infringe upon the rights and interests of investors. Prior research has predominantly concentrated on examining the effect of various financial metrics on the incidence of such fraudulent activities, frequently disregarding the temporal variances in the magnitude of these factors’ impacts. This study introduces a continuous dynamic information gain (IG) model that captures listed company behavior and implements a sophisticated Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Long Short-term Memory (LSTM), termed IG-LSTM-GAT model. The model assesses how incremental corporate behavioral information influences the likelihood of financial fraud across diverse timescales, facilitating the identification and prediction of these events. Initially, the IG is determined for factors correlated with financial fraud occurrences. Then, the LSTM model subsequently extracts features from the incremental behavioral information of companies. Culminating, the GAT algorithm performs multi-layer computations on the incremental behavioral features to predict the risk of corporate financial fraud. Experimental outcomes validate the proposed method’s effectiveness, offering significant guidance for the prevention and control of financial fraud detection within listed companies.

articleTitle: Antenna Stealth Design Based on Polarization Reconfigurable Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper designs a polarization reconfigurable metasurface integrated beneath a microstrip antenna for antenna stealth applications. Based on polarization conversion theory, the metasurface employs "I"-shaped structures and controls the on-off states of four PIN diodes in each unit to change the polarization state. By leveraging the characteristic of the metasurface having the same amplitude but opposite phase in different modes, it polarizes the reflected electromagnetic waves in opposite directions, thereby reducing the antenna's RCS and achieving antenna stealth. Simulation results show that the antenna's gain remains around 16 dB after loading, with negligible impact on its radiation performance. Additionally, under normal incidence of x-polarized electromagnetic waves, the metasurface achieves effective RCS reduction in the 11-17 GHz frequency range, with a maximum reduction of 10.2 dBsm. For y-polarized electromagnetic waves, in the 12.3-17 GHz range, the maximum RCS reduction reaches 17.2 dBsm.

articleTitle: A 2.5V 200mA CMOS Low-Dropout Voltage Regulator with Robust PVT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The paper proposes a high-precision, low-noise, and PVT-robust low-dropout voltage regulator (LDOVR) for systems on chips (SOCs). The LDOVR features a bandgap reference circuit, an error amplifier, a power output stage, and a startup circuit. The error amplifier achieves high gain and stability by employing a Miller capacitor with a zeroing resistor for frequency compensation, ensuring a phase margin above 65° across various process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) conditions. The proposed LDOVR is designed and implemented in a 55nm CMOS process. Simulation results demonstrate that with an input voltage range of 2.6-4V (typically 3.3V), the output voltage is 2.5V with fluctuations within 8.6mV, corresponding to a voltage error of less than 0.25%. The quiescent current is below 120μA, and the LDOVR can drive loads exceeding 200mA. Over a wide temperature range from −55°C to 125°C, the LDOVR shows a temperature coefficient better than 7.38 ppm/°C. When the load current is 200mA, the LDOVR maintains a phase margin above 72.7° and a power supply rejection ratio greater than 42dB at 10KHz. The LDOVR occupies a very compact core size of 0.034 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a total silicon area of 0.14 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including all testing pads.

articleTitle: Compact Tri-band Monopole Antenna for RFID/GPS/WLAN/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a compact tri-band planar printed monopole antenna for the applications of RFID/GPS/WLAN/ WiMAX is proposed. The compact tri-band monopole antenna is composed of a Ψ-type monopole antenna and a circular ring ground with an arc-shaped slot. The Ψ-shaped strip can generate four resonance points to meet the low frequency coverage. An arc-shaped slot in the circular ring ground is loaded to improve high-frequency impedance matching and widen high-frequency bandwidth. The antenna is printed on a 1.6mm-thick FR-4 dielectric substrate, fed by a coaxial cable, and can provide three wide operating bandwidths that cover 0.82–0.98, 1.21–1.61 and 2.35–2.71 GHz for RFID/GPS/WLAN/ WiMAX communication systems, with S11 less than -10 dB. This compact tri-band monopole antenna is fabricated and measured, and typical experimental results such as S11, gains, and radiation patterns are presented. The measured results are dovetail with the simulated results. The advantages of the proposed antenna are compact size, simple structure, high gain and omnidirectional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: A Novel Complex-Valued Network for Phase Preservation Sparse SAR Imaging: Initial Result
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Sparse synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging has demonstrated desirable potential in image quality improvement and unambiguity reconstruction. Nevertheless, conventional sparse SAR recovery algorithms based on regularization require handcrafted parameters and cannot preserve phase information, which limits its application. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel complex-valued network for phase preservation sparse SAR imaging. Specifically, we map a innovative iterative soft thresholding algorithm, named as BiIST, into the deep network form. Then, to enhance the imaging performance of sparse estimation, we designed the symmetric complex-valued convolutional neural network block. In contrast to typical sparse SAR imaging algorithms, the proposed method can achieve not only a higher-quality sparse estimation but also a non-sparse estimation that retains the same phase information as the image recovered using matched filtering (MF). Experimental results based on real scenes verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: A High Gain Omnidirectional Dipole Array Antenna for WiFi-6E
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A high gain vertical polarization omnidirectional antenna is proposed, with overall size of 250mm×16mm×1mm. A double U-shaped symmetrical dipole oscillator is used as radiation oscillator, and then four radiation elements are formed into a series-fed antenna array. Meanwhile, two four-element series-fed arrays are connected in parallel, feeding in the parallel center. All antenna elements are direct connected by microstrip lines. Through adding protrusions or adjusting their widths on microstrip lines, impedance transformation can be achieved, and standing wave and gain can be adjusted.Simulation and physical testing results show that the antenna can effectively cover the WiFi-6E frequency range (5.9GHz-7.125GHz), with |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ -15dB. In the horizontal direction, the antenna exhibits low gain variations (<3dB), showing good omnidirectional radiation characteristics. Vertically, the side lobes are very small, and the radiation energy is mainly concentrated in the main lobe, achieving higher overall gain (8.5-11dBi). The proposed antenna is suitable for short-range wireless communication scenarios with high broadband, high gain, and omnidirectional spatial coverage.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based Polarization Converter Using Smith Chart Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this study, we propose the use of the Smith chart method to analyze the electromagnetic (EM) polarization transformation characteristics of metasurfaces in a visual and graphical manner. This approach allows for the visualization of the impedance transformation phenomenon, as well as the amplitude and phase of the reflection coefficients. Based on the Smith chart analysis, we present the metasurface-based polarization converter with three polarization conversion functions. By integrating the varactor diode into the metasurface, it has the ability to manipulate the polarization state in a dynamic manner, which may find promising applications in wireless communications where binary polarization shift keying is highly demanded. The above concepts are confirmed through the full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A novel 2×6 beamforming network for shaping flat-topped radiation patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Usually, beam-forming network synthesis requires good isolation between antenna elements, otherwise the radiation patterns will become deteriorated. To solve this problem, this paper proposed a novel 2×6 beamforming network topology for shaping flat-topped radiation patterns. Results show that the network can realize the beamforming function by adjusting the design parameters of the numerical method when the isolation between the antenna elements is -20 dB and -15 dB.

articleTitle: A Power Supply Method for Detonation Control Module with Threshold of Opening and Closing Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of power supply circuit composed of energy storage capacitor and ordinary linear voltage regulator, such as slow power down and input voltage fluctuation affecting output voltage, a power supply method for detonation control module with threshold of opening and closing voltage is proposed. In this method, a 3.3V linear regulator with threshold value of opening and closing voltage is introduced, which is realized by combining energy storage capacitor and 5V linear regulator. Set the starting and closing voltage threshold to control the enabling pin of 3.3V linear voltage regulator by using resistance voltage divider. When the input voltage rises to the starting voltage, the regulator will start quickly and keep the output voltage stable. When the input voltage drops to the closing voltage value, the output voltage of the voltage regulator will power down quickly. The 3.3V linear regulator with opening and closing voltage threshold significantly reduces the time that the output voltage follows the input voltage during power on and power off, and effectively reduces the impact of input voltage jitter on the output voltage. The verification results show that the speed of powering on and powering off of the circuit developed by the power supply method can meet the power supply requirements of the detonating control module, and the power supply voltage is stable, which can effectively reduce the risks of program runaway and "crash" during powering on and powering off of the microcontroller.

articleTitle: A 170~260GHz On-wafer Probe Based on High Resistivity Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Measurement of devices in high frequencies is important for characterization, especially for millimeter and submillimeter wave band. As an effective alternative for conventional measurement with fixtures, on-wafer probes are favored for avoiding extra expense and performance deterioration. In this work, a high resistivity silicon based RF probe operating in 170~260GHz is proposed. The simulation exhibits return loss better than 15dB and insertion loss better than 1.6dB.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Low-Profile Circularly-Polarized Filtering Antenna for 5.8GHz WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A single-layer Low-Profile circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna that combines filtering scheme into a antenna for 5.8GHz WLAN applications is presented. To achieve the filtering performance, a radiation patch etching rectangular slot and loading stubs is conducted. Two controlled radiating nulls are created at the edges of the passband. The CP radiation is realized by using a defected ground on the bottom of the substrate. The evaluation results show that the constructed antenna has a matching bandwidth of 3.42% (5.74-5.94GHz) and axial ratio bandwidth is 4.48% (5.67-5.93GHz). Moreover, the peak gain is 4.36dBi at the frequency of 5.8GHz.

articleTitle: Digital Twin System for Reflector Antenna Structure Performance Evaluation Based on Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The digital twin system of the reflector antenna based on the surrogate model is designed in this paper to achieve real-time evaluation of its structural performance during operation. Firstly, the finite element model of the reflector antenna is established, and mechanical performance data samples of the antenna structure are obtained. Secondly, using surrogate model technology, a high-precision Gaussian Process mathematical model is fitted to enable rapid and accurate prediction of the antenna structure's performance. Finally, data communication technology is utilized to connect the physical space of the antenna with its twin space, enabling visualization of its structure's performance and interaction with motion attitude based on the Unity engine. Through testing, it has been demonstrated that this digital twin system can achieve real-time monitoring of high precision and efficiency for the structural performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Fire Detection: Unleashing the Power of YOLOv8 Algorithm for Accurate Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Fire incidents present a significant threat to human safety and property, emphasizing the need for highly effective detection methods. This study introduces a cutting-edge fire image recognition algorithm, leveraging the capabilities of YOLOv8 renowned for its swift and precise target detection. Through rigorous evaluation, YOLOv8 demonstrated an exceptional accuracy rate exceeding 90%, accompanied by remarkable recall and F1 score values. Additionally, the model's performance was thoroughly assessed using mean Average Precision (mAP) at an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.5, outperforming other models across all metrics. This research underscores the immense potential of YOLOv8 in the realm of fire image recognition, showcasing its practicality in real-time fire detection systems to fortify public safety and safeguard property.

articleTitle: Research on FDFD Modeling and Wireless Power Transmission of Near-sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the increase of human marine activities, it is of great significance to realize near-sea-surface microwave wireless power transmission according to the electromagnetic wave transmission characteristics of evaporation duct. In this paper, the finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) is used to construct the model of near-sea-surface evaporation duct and calculate the electromagnetic field distribution of evaporation duct with high accuracy. The FDFD model is used to analyze the difference of TM mode and TE mode propagation, the electric field distribution at different propagation distances, and the influence of the frequency.
