articleTitle: A High Impedance Grounding Fault Location Method for Transmission Lines Based on Electromagnetic Time Reversal and Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of arc grounding faults in high impedance ground faults (HIF) on electromagnetic time reversal (EMTR) localization methods. Firstly, two EMTR methods suitable for HIF were reviewed, noting their varying degrees of positioning accuracy reduction in the presence of arc grounding. Subsequently, a method based on low-order harmonics of HIF was proposed to improve the positioning performance of the EMTR method under arc grounding fault conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that this method can achieve accurate positioning in the presence of arc grounding, with a 90% reduction in the required sampling rate. Even at a low sampling rate of 100 kHz, this method exhibits excellent localization performance. Additionally, it significantly enhances noise resistance, allowing for accurate localization even at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10 dB.

articleTitle: A Decoupling Method Based on Time-modulated Array with Harmonic Characteristic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Mutual coupling is a common error source in antenna arrays that affects the performance of various applications. In this paper, a decoupling method based on time- modulated array (TMA) with harmonic characteristic analysis is proposed. Different from the conventional time-modulated technique which only analyzes the received signal’s harmonics of single antenna, the harmonic theoretical model considering coupling coefficients between adjacent antennas has been established and the corresponding coupling coefficients can be obtained independently. Moreover, several numerical simulations considering amplitude and phase coupling coefficients are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: EMC Data Model Design driven by Graph Database
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) issues are becoming a key challenge. This paper explores the EMC data model design method based on the graph database. First, the graph database intuitively represents the relationship between the devices and the signal transmission path through the nodes and the edges, which can more accurately describe the complex electromagnetic environment. Subsequently, the article introduces the current application status of graph databases in the EMC field, including the key steps, such as demand analysis, graph data model construction, semantic modeling, data integration, management, query, and analysis design. Through the case of ship electromagnetic compatibility analysis, we further demonstrate the advantages of the graph database in identifying and managing EMI paths and explore how to improve EMC performance through path analysis, interference intensity calculation, and optimization iteration.

articleTitle: A Novel DM-RPA-Based Strain Sensor for High-Sensitivity 2-Dimensionsal Strain Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Sensitivity is one of the key parameters for evaluating the performance of strain sensors. This paper presents an innovative design of a high-sensitivity DM-RPA strain sensor for simultaneous 2D strain monitoring. It achieves an ultra-high sensitivity factor of 100 ppm/με and linearity simultaneously by leveraging the admittance of two degenerated orthogonal modes. It is 100 and 50 times more sensitive than LP-patch and metal foil strain gages, respectively, and can detect strains in both x- and y-directions.

articleTitle: A Control Method for Current Sharing in Interleaved LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The LLC resonant converter finds widespread application in several fields. Nevertheless, its power level cannot be efficiently increased due to the limitations of the development of semiconductor and magnetic integrated component materials. One excellent answer is to interleave parallel technology. However, load imbalance originating from manufacturing imperfections in the components happens in the resonance tank when all of the interleaved LLC's modules run at the same switching frequency. This research suggests a load current sharing technique for the mismatch of each phase resonant circuit to address this issue. First, the LLC resonant converter's mathematical model is created using the fundamental analysis approach. Then, in order to offset the gain inaccuracy caused by differences in the resonant element and to distribute the load current equally throughout each module, a controller is built that modifies the resonant frequency by regulating the conduction time of the switch-control capacitor circuit (SCC). The control strategy enhances the system's anti-interference and speed. Finally, using a 300W model in MATLAB/Simulink, the simulation results confirm that the suggested control technique is feasible.

articleTitle: A planar wideband quasi-isotropic antenna based on triple current line sources theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A planar quasi-isotropic antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is analyzed based on the theory of triple current line sources. Quasi-isotropic radiation is produced when three dipoles are arranged in H-shape. The proposed H-shape antenna is compared to the existing U-shape antenna to show its advantages in both impedance bandwidth and 3dB gain variation bandwidth. The use of printed dipoles also reduces the difficulty of feeding. The simulated results show that the antenna provides a 10.2% impedance bandwidth from 2.33 GHz to 2.58 GHz. The peak gain is 0.95 dBi and the gain variation of the entire impedance bandwidth is less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: V-band Transceiver Based on Through Silicon Via (TSV) Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A V-band three-dimensional silicon based transceiver SIP (System in Package) is presented in this paper, which is manufactured using high-precision Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technology and integrates low-loss Through-Silicon Via (TSV) vertical interconnection structures. Mixer, Low Noise Amplifier (LNA), and attenuator are contained in the receiver module while the power amplifier (PA), multiplier and attenuator are contained in the transmitter module. The size of the transmitter and receiver modules are 10×10×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 12×11×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> respectively. Measured results show that both the transmitter and receiver can cover the bandwidth of 59-62GHz with VSWR less than 2.0. The receiver gain can be up to 35dB and the transmitter out put power can be more than 15dBm in the frequency band.

articleTitle: Dual-branch Brain Tumor Classification Based on CNN and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Brain tumors can disrupt the normal functioning of the nervous system, affect brain functions, and may even lead to the patient’s death. Conventional methods for brain tumors are insufficient to achieve accurate identification of tumor types. In our study, we propose a dual-branch residual transformer fusion network (DRTFNet). The network combines a convolution neural network and a Transformer structure. Within the CNN branch, local information features are extracted using residual dual-shuffled attention modules, and spatial relationships are coupled using a residual-connected channel prior to convolutional attention. Meanwhile, the Transformer branch employs the ResNet structure and Swin Transformer to extract global information characteristics. To reduce redundant information in the feature maps and focus on the key feature information, the ResNet structure incorporates a spatial and channel reconstruction convolution block. Additionally, the Swin Transformer module also utilizes a hierarchical structure and a self-attention mechanism to efficiently process datasets and improve the classification accuracy of the model. We conducted a comprehensive study on multislice brain tumor classification using the brain tumor datasets. Our test findings demonstrate that the proposed deep-learning method can significantly improve classification accuracy while confirming the robustness of our model.

articleTitle: Analog Circuit Fault Diagnosis Based on Residual Network and Deep Channel Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Analog circuit faults diagnose using circuit signals has always been a research hotspot which is time-consuming and difficult. An analog circuit fault diagnosis method (RNDCAM) based on fault feature extraction module using Residual Network (RN) and Deep Channel Attention feature enhancement Module (DCAM) is proposed. Firstly, to extract the shallow amplitude variation characteristics of a voltage signal, a fault feature extraction module is constructed based on 1DCNN and residual block. By using convolution kernels with different weights, the sample features are broadened to multi-channels, which can better reflect the local characteristics, periodic characteristics and trend characteristics of a voltage signal. Then, to fully tap the deep characteristics of the signal amplitude change, the DCAM module is constructed. The multiple convolution kernels are used to extract all channels of the feature maps at the same time. To effectively capture the local context information and weight the key features, the feature maps are reweighted by the weight matrix obtained by compressing and restoring the channel. The experimental results show that this method can improve the accuracy of analog circuit fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Circularly-polarized Metasurface antenna Array in Random Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A circularly polarized metasurface antenna array is proposed in this paper. The array is composed of low-profile circularly polarized metasurface antenna units with a size of 0.67λ× 0.67λ× 0.05λ (λ is the wavelength at 5GHz). The antenna unit is used to construct a 4×4 random-arranged array and its radiation performance was simulated. The results shows that the maximum gain of 15 dBic and 3dB beam width of 18.8° were obtained.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Folded Transmitarray Using Dual Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A dual-band dual-circularly polarized double folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) is proposed consisting of a main-reflector (MR), a sub-reflector (SR) and a feeding source. The MR is a frequency-selective metasurfaces designed to achieve transmission and reflection simultaneously. In lower band, it converts y-polarized wave into left circularly polarized (LCP) beam while reflecting x-polarized wave. Similarly in higher band, x-polarized waves are converted into right circularly polarized (RCP) beam while y-polarized wave are reflected. The SR is a reflective metasurface designed to reflect linearly polarized (LP) wave and convert it into its orthogonal counterpart, simultaneously. Our proposed FTA reduces the profile by 3/4 compared to its conventional counterpart centred at 12.1 and 16.7 GHz, which is distinct from previous work. Numerical results show that the proposed antenna in two bands achieves a maximum gain of 23.1 dBic and 23.6 dBic, corresponding to an aperture efficiency of 30.8% and 20.8%. Our dual-band strategy promises promising application in satellite and radar communication systems.

articleTitle: Randomized-enhanced Magnitude Channel Pruning for Radar Jamming Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the rapid development of radar jamming technology, traditional detection techniques face significant limitations in complex electromagnetic environments. Recent interference detection methods based on deep learning struggle with processing speed and real-time performance. To address this, we propose a new pruning technique called randomized-enhanced magnitude channel pruning (RMP) to achieve faster detection speeds and more lightweight models. This study evaluates the performance of RMP compared to random channel pruning and magnitude channel pruning in radar jamming detection. To verify RMP's generalization, we also tested it on the VOC2007 [16] object detection task. Results show that RMP consistently reduces mAP@50 loss more effectively than other methods. In one iteration pruning, RMP reduced mAP@50 loss by an average of 0.8% and 1% in radar jamming detection, and by 0.4% and 3.1% in the VOC2007 dataset, compared to random and magnitude pruning, respectively. In multi-pass pruning, RMP reduced mAP@50 loss by an average of 0.3% in radar jamming detection, and by 0.7% and 1.6% in the VOC2007 dataset, compared to random and magnitude pruning, respectively. These findings confirm RMP's effectiveness in maintaining model accuracy and its practical value in fast-response scenarios like radar jamming detection.

articleTitle: Wide-Stopband HMSIW Filter Using Interdigital-Slot-Loaded Complementary Split-Ring Resonator and Ring-Mushroom-Shaped Slow-Wave Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this letter, a half-mode substrate-integrated waveguide (HMSIW) bandpass filter with compact physical size and wide-stopband is implemented by the ring-mushroom-shaped slow-wave unit cells and the improved complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR). The ring-mushroom-shaped unit cells are periodically etched on the conventional HMSIW to produce slow-wave effect and reduce the cutoff frequency of the dominant transmissible mode in the waveguide. Then, the improved CSRR is mainly constituted by etching multiple interdigital slots on the inner metal surface of the CSRR, which will improve the product of the equivalent inductance and capacitance of the structure effectively, thereby achieve a much lower resonant frequency eventually. Moreover, in the filter design with interdigital-slot-loaded CSRR and ring-mushroom-shaped unit cells, to further improved the higher stopband performance, the source-load-coupling scheme is used to generate additional transmission zero, and the serpentine spurline is loaded on the input and output microstrip lines to suppress higher-order modes as well. To verify the availability of the above concept, a two-pole bandpass filter is realized. The measured results indicate that the operation central frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) is 0.96GHz and the in-band insertion loss is less than 2.3dB. Meanwhile, the stopband can reach to 4.3f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with an out-of-band rejection of 30dB. These results illustrate great potential of the proposed filter in practical microwave applications.

articleTitle: A Wide-band Wide-beam Metal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Vivaldi antenna is widely used in mobile communication because of its good broadband characteristics and high efficiency characteristics. In this paper, a wideband metal Vivaldi antenna is proposed and simulated by using electromagnetic simulation software HFSS. The simulation results show that the antenna has a wide operating bandwidth, the relative bandwidth of standing wave ratio less than 2 is about 20%, the relative bandwidth of normal gain greater than 2dBi is about 14%, the antenna’s 3dB beamwidth is greater than 150°, and the cross-polarization ratio is greater than 30dB. The antenna can achieve good broadband bandwidth beam characteristics and is a high performance and high reliability antenna.

articleTitle: Fast Microwave Near-Field Phase Retrieval Based on Improved Diffraction Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a fast microwave near-field phase retrieval method based on an Improved Diffraction Neural Network (IDNN). The method first modifies the Rayleigh-Sommerfeld (RS) formula using the angular spectrum method to adapt it for the Phase Retrieval (PR) equation. By enhancing the output layer of the DNN to simultaneously provide amplitude and phase information and incorporating a backward phase iteration step, the accuracy of phase retrieval is significantly improved. The optimization process leverages a custom-designed loss function and the Adam optimizer for gradient descent, enabling the retrieval of phase information using only amplitude data from two plane measurements. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of this approach and demonstrate its advantages in speed compared to classical algorithms such as the Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) algorithm and the Truncated Amplitude Flow (TAF) algorithm.

articleTitle: A Transparent Metadevice for Radar-Infrared Compatible Stealth using Dual-Sized Thin ITO meta-films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With increasing demand of multispectral detection in military applications, it is urgent to develop effective compatible stealth techniques. Here, we propose a Radar-Infrared (IR) compatible stealth strategy by elaborately designing different-sized ITO meta-films and arranging the resulting supercells in chessboard configuration. For verification, a transparent metadevice is designed in tri-layer ITO-PVC-ITO scheme, and its top checkerboard pattern consists of dual-sized ITO patch films for radar stealth. Meanwhile, IR stealth is achieved due to the high filling ratio of ITO in basic element. Both numerical and experimental results show that the metadevice exhibits a low emissivity of 0.23 and broadband radar cross-section reduction within 7.5~18 GHz, which setup a novel paradigm for multispectral compatible camouflage applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Algorithm for Multi-objective Driver Chip Cell Layout Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The manufacturability of integrated circuit (IC) design is crucial during the global layout stage. Traditional layout algorithms tend to focus on achieving the optimal placement solution with minimal line length and non-overlapping cells, overlooking line and pin density issues. This often leads to congestion, resource insufficiency, and low manufacturability. To tackle this challenge, this paper presents a deep learning-based, multi-objective-driven layout algorithm built upon the open-source algorithm DREAMPlace. The proposed algorithm incorporates a wire-wrap density function and a pin density function, which account for macro-blocking in the layout and are computed using GPUs. Results on the DAC 2012 test benchmarks demonstrate that the algorithm enhances the overall layout, mitigates excessive density, improves pin density without significantly altering wire length and wire density, and achieves a runtime speedup of approximately 4x-10x.

articleTitle: A Gain-Enhanced 77 GHz Series-fed Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a gain-enhanced 77 GHz series-fed patch antenna with metal fence and strip arrays is designed. The proposed antenna consists of a series-fed antenna with 5 patches, a metal fence around the series-fed patches and three metal strip arrays on the metal fence. The metal fence enhances the gain of the series-fed patch antenna and the metal strips with electromagnetic band gap (EBG) characteristics suppress the surface wave further improving the gain. We compared the radiation characteristics of the three antennas: the series-fed patch antenna, the antenna with metal fence, and the antenna with metal fence and metal strips. Simulation results show that the gain of the series-fed patch antenna is 13.4 dBi. By comparison, the metal fence structure increases the gain by 0.7 dB to 14.1 dBi, and the metal strip structure further increases the gain by 0.8 dB to 14.9 dBi. The proposed antenna can be used in 77 GHz automotive radar.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Transmissive Programmable Metasurface for Dynamic Electromagnetic Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this article, a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) 1bit reconfigurable metasurface transmitarray antenna is proposed. To enhance the bandwidth of the transmitarray, a new method is introduced on the transmissive programmable metasurface. The unit cell in the metasurface is integrated with two PIN diodes, and thus a binary-coded phase is realized for a single polarization. Furthermore, to achieve the low-profile design, a butterfly patch design is utilized throughout the unit. The difference is that a unidirectional arrow patch is used instead of the butterfly body portion of the receiver layer. A 20×20 elements low-profile transmitarray is designed. The simulated peak gain is 22.4dB, and the gain bandwidth is about 50%(from 16.8 to 27.5 GHz). The technology provides a new approach to meet the demand for broadband transmission in wireless communication and radar applications.

articleTitle: Ground-based Radio Navigation Base Station Deployment Method based on Improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The ground-based radio navigation system is an indispensable part of the resilient positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) system, and the configuration of the ground-based radio navigation base station determines the positioning accuracy and system coverage of the ground-based navigation system. To improve the system coverage while reducing the system dilution of precision (DOP) value, this paper proposes a ground-based radio navigation base station deployment method based on an improved multi-objective particle swarm optimization (IMOPSO) algorithm. This method searches for the optimal deployment location of ground-based radio navigation base stations under the constraints of DOP and coverage. Based on the standard multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, this paper improved the population individual initialization method and added position judgment criteria. Finally, simulated experimental results verified that the proposed method could simultaneously optimize coverage and DOP distribution.

articleTitle: Attitude Measurement Based on Differential Array of MEMS Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The Attitude and Heading Reference System (AHRS) provides real-time carrier attitude and heading data. Integration of low-cost, low-power Micro Electromechanical System (MEMS) inertial sensors has expanded application possibilities. To address issues like low accuracy and sensor drift, this paper proposes a sensor redundancy technique. It forms an array of 32 inertial measurement units (IMUs) combining gyroscopes and accelerometers. Through differential and mean fusion, this array is virtualized into a stable, reliable, high-precision IMU. A magnetometer is added to the IMU array, and an IMU attitude measurement board is designed based on established principles. The comparison experiments with other commercial attitude measurement boards showed that the IMU attitude measurement board was more suitable for attitude measurement in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Low Coupling Sparse Array Based on Uniform Linear Array Fitting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that traditional sparse arrays only emphasize high degrees of freedom and ignore low coupling, uniform array fitting method can design arrays with low coupling. However, the existing array coupling based on uniform array fitting method still has room for decline, and the value of weight function is not the minimum, so the performance of array DOA estimation needs to be further optimized. Therefore, based on the uniform matrix fitting method, a uniform matrix fitting 6-base-layer array is designed. By extending the spacing of each subarray of the uniform subarray in the base layer, the number of small array element spacing pairs in the differential cooperative array is reduced, and the coupling between the elements of the whole sparse array is reduced as a whole. The performance of DOA estimation of the designed array is simulated and analyzed by using spatial smoothing multiple signal classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Modulation and Demodulation: A Defense Method Against Weight Bit-Flip Attacks in Floating Point CNN Hardware Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a highly utilized deep learning model in various domains, including computer vision and natural language processing. Disruption of the network structure of CNN might cause significant losses. One often-used and effective attack method is the bit-flip attack. This approach affects the prediction accuracy of CNN models through carefully manipulating bits, and in certain cases, it can entirely disrupt the model’s ability to make accurate predictions, resulting in random guessing. In this work, we propose a defense strategy to counter bit-flip attacks, aiming to improve prediction accuracy in the occurrence of such attacks. This work involves the implementation of Lenet-5 and Lenet-3D on FPGA devices, along with the addition of proposed modulator and demodulator to these two CNN models. The results demonstrate that the prediction accuracy of the CNN structure is effectively improved when the proposed modulator and demodulator are incorporated, even when subjected to the same bit-flip attack injection rate. By flipping 200 bits per layer, our method can significantly enhance the accuracy of the MNIST dataset from 19% to over 90%. Similarly, the accuracy of the CIFAR-10 dataset can be increased from 12% to 52%. Furthermore, in terms of hardware resource consumption, the proposed security unit comprises less than 3% of the overall system.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Altitude Target Intelligent Recognition via Airborne Pulse-Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: For airborne pulse-Doppler (PD) radar, this paper proposes a novel target recognition method for ultra-low altitude targets. The proposed method uses the range-Doppler (RD) image features of targets for detection and then extracts the time-frequency (TF) image features from the radar data cube (i.e., multiple RD images) for recognition. Simulation results show that, by learning the TF image features of different targets via SqueezeNet, high recognition performance can be achieved by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Interference Methods for Interferometer Direction-finding Based on Dual-point Source Co-processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Most interferometer direction-finding (DF) interference techniques are limited by the difficulty of achieving coherent interference, failing to interfere with DF effectively. Interrupted-sampling forwarding jamming (ISJ) technology is widely used to interfere with active detection techniques like monopulse DF. This paper is the first attempt to utilize ISJ technology to interfere with interferometer DF. A method of dual-point source co-processing by ISJ is proposed, its mathematical mechanism is analyzed, and the influence of each parameter is simulated. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is verified by experiments. The simulation and experiment results demonstrate that the proposed technique has the flexibility to produce coherent interference effects with a larger degree of freedom.

articleTitle: Diagnosis Using Equivalent Magnetic Current Method for Transmitarry based CATR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we apply the source reconstruction method to diagnosis of a transmitarray based compact antenna test range (T-CATR), and compare its performance with the spatial deconvolution method. The method utilizes planar near-field data to derive equivalent magnetic current elements on the aperture of the T-CATR to diagnose faulty elements. The near-field data are related to the equivalent magnetic currents by establishing the electric field integral equation (EFIE). The EFIEs are reduced to matrix equations by the method of moments and the singular value decomposition method is used to solve the matrix equations. Our simulation results show that the method based on the equivalent magnetic current method requires less data from near-field sampling points and is more accurate than the method based on spatial deconvolution derived antenna aperture field.

articleTitle: Manufacturing Process and Comparative Analysis of MEMS Accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Accelerometer is the device that can measure the acceleration of an object by transferring acceleration into a electric parameter, such as voltage, current and resistance etc. By applying a mathematical relationship between the electrical parameter and acceleration, the rate of change of speed of the object can be determined. However, conventional accelerometers are large, leading to higher energy consumption and inefficient use of space. Therefore, a miniaturized accelerometer is needed. This article introduces the manufacturing process of an accelerometer using MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) technology. The total size of the proposed system is 68 μm × 51 μm × 30μm.

articleTitle: Classification for Spatial Objects with Micro-motions Based on Dual CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: To enhance the precision of micro-motion objects classification under low signal-to-noise ratio(SNR), this paper introduces a micro-motion classification method for spatial objects based on dual CNN (Convolutional Neural Network). This approach takes the noisy MDS(micro-Doppler signature) image as input and output the category of its micro-motion. Firstly, to suppress the noise while preserving the MDS of weak scattering centers, one denoising CNN is designed. Second, a ShuffleNet-based CNN is developed to undertake the classification task. Finally, experiments are conducted and results demonstrate that even in low SNR conditions, our proposed method outperforms several existing methods.

articleTitle: A Lumped Elements Loaded Over-Hundred-Octave Super-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, an over-hundred-octave super-wideband antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna is composed of the ground plane, coaxial probe, the hollowed-out conical radiator, four short circuit posts and several loaded lumped elements. By properly optimizing the model of the proposed antenna and adjusting the parameters of the lumped elements, the performance of the antenna in the low frequency band has been greatly improved. By numerically optimizing, the simulated results show that the proposed antenna can realize 537:1 -10-dB bandwidth from 0.01GHz-5.37GHz, which is expected to meet the application requirements of integrated and wide spectrum.

articleTitle: Research on the Motion Control Algorithms for Unmanned Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Unmanned ships, as an important marine tool, have broad application prospects in maritime resource exploration, rescue, water quality monitoring and other fields. To better achieve automatic navigation of unmanned ships, we study and verify three motion control algorithms of unmanned ships. The Kalman filter is used to suppress the drift of positioning data, the modified Prim algorithm is used for multi-point route planning, and the Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) algorithm is used for adjusting the heading angle. We construct an IoT unmanned ship as verification platfrom to test the effectiveness of the proposed motion control strategy, providing a solid foundation for further research and application of unmanned ships.

articleTitle: Wideband Self-Phased Dipole Antenna with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A new type of wideband self-phased circularly polarized dipole antenna for Ku and K band with simple structure is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna mainly consists of a metallic radiator and a reflector, which connects the inner and outer conductors of the radiator to form a coaxial balun for impedance matching and balance feeding. Two sets of orthogonal metallic arms with unequal length are sequentially attached to the outer conductor, generating a 90 degree phase shift between adjacent arms, deriving dual self-phased mode to realize CP radiation. Each set of metallic arms, upper and lower, is designed with similar lengths to further improve the antenna bandwidth. Simulation shows that the proposed antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 52% (SWR<2), a wide pattern bandwidth of 50% and a gain of about 6 dB within the bandwidth, which can meet the requirements of different wireless systems.

articleTitle: Space Target Feature Extraction based on Linear Frequency Modulation-Vortex Electromagnetic Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Compared with planar electromagnetic waves, vortex electromagnetic waves carry orbital angular momentum, and thus can be applied in many fields such as imaging and detection. Due to the rich spatial information contained, the parameters of a moving target can be effectively extracted using vortex electromagnetic waves. The paper focuses on the estimation of target structural parameters in the linear frequency modulation -vortex electromagnetic wave (LFM-VEMW) regime. Firstly, a LFM beam is transmitted to form a vortex electromagnetic wave in the single-in-multi-out (SIMO) regime, the target echo model is derived, and the mathematical expression of the one-dimensional distance image of the target is given. Secondly, the method of extracting the non-cooperative target parameters from the one-dimensional distance image is discussed, and the kinematic parameters and geometric features of the target can be effectively estimated by the introduction of multiple viewpoints and the information in the distance image. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Design of a Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In response to the demands of satellite-borne phased array packaged antennas, this paper proposes a broadband circularly polarized magnetoelectric dipole (MED) antenna based on Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) technology. The antenna consists of four horizontally oriented patches and four sets of vertically oriented metal vias. A single series microstrip line is coupled and fed through a cross-slot on the metal ground, and four rotationally symmetric rectangular slots are added on the metal ground to enhance the purity of circular polarization. The results show that the thin antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 38.8% (24.47-36.26 GHz) and a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 33.2% (25.09-35.09 GHz), with stable gain across the operating frequency band. The antenna unit features a low-profile design, broad impedance bandwidth, expansive polarization bandwidth, consistent gain performance, and facilitated integration, which altogether renders it ideally suited for Antenna-in-Package (AiP) applications utilizing LTCC technology.

articleTitle: A TSEM Method for Analysing of Elastic Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The Tetrahedral Spectral Element Method (TSEM) integrates the strengths of spectral methods and finite element methodologies, proving exceptionally effective in addressing partial differential equations, notably in the realms of wave dynamics and the propagation of elastic waves. This manuscript details our advancement: a tetrahedron-centric SEM designed for the replication of elastic wave behavior. We further compare the outcomes of our model against those generated by COMSOL. Central to our model is the utilization of hexahedral elements, upon which a Ricker wavelet is imposed as the stimuli for conducting in-depth examinations and observations.

articleTitle: A Compact Wide Load Rectifier Based on a grounded transmission line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: At present, wireless energy transmission (WPT) has been widely used in various fields. In order to apply rectifiers to various devices and reduce their size, this paper proposes a novel wide load radio frequency (RF) rectifier circuit. The impedance of a rectifying diode is affected by power, and when the load changes, the power of the diode will change, causing fluctuations in the impedance of the diode. In order to reduce the impact of load changes on rectification efficiency, a grounded transmission line is used to compensate for the imaginary part of the rectifying diode. The input impedance of the rectifier can be maintained relatively steadily over a wide load range by this method. According to the measured results, when the input power is 20 dBm, the rectification efficiency of the rectifier exceeds 40% in the impedance range of 800~7000 Ω. The rectifier has a rectification efficiency of over 40% in the input power range of 14~26 dBm under a load of 2000 Ω, with a maximum efficiency of 60.5%. The size of the proposed rectifier is 12 mm×37 mm.

articleTitle: Study on Oracle Bone Image Preprocessing Based on Fusion of Denoising and Enhancement Techniques: Improving Text Detection Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of preprocessing oracle bone script images based on the fusion of denoising and enhancement techniques, aiming to improve text detection accuracy. By integrating multiple denoising techniques, we effectively eliminate speckles and noise from the images, and enhance image quality by adjusting contrast and sharpening, making oracle bone characters clearer. Subsequently, we utilize YOLOv8 object detection technology to detect text regions in oracle bone images, ensuring efficient subsequent text segmentation and analysis. Through this study, we have laid a solid foundation for future research on oracle bone scripts and provided reliable technical solutions to address the challenges posed by complex images. Experimental results show that the Box(P) after preprocessing improves by approximately 2.65% compared to the unprocessed, validating the effectiveness of the fusion preprocessing method proposed in this study in practical applications. We look forward to using this method to explore the deeper meanings of more oracle bone texts, advancing the exploration and understanding of ancient civilizations.

articleTitle: A Wideband Cross-dipole Circularly Polarized Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A wideband cross-dipole circularly polarized phased array antenna is proposed. The phased array antenna can achieve a two-dimensional ±30° phase scanning ability with reflection coefficients below -10 dB at 27-32 GHz. The simulated results of a 5×5 antenna array show that the axial ratios at the main beam scanning range are all less than 4 dB within the 27-32 GHz band. The change of the gain in the scanning is smooth at the range of 18-20 dBic, and it achieves a good circularly polarized scanning characteristic. This proposed antenna can be applied in the field of millimeter wave communication, especially for satellite communication.

articleTitle: Multi-polarized Phase Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces offer an advanced method for precise control of electromagnetic waves. However, current research mainly centers on manipulating either linearly or circularly polarized waves. In this paper, we propose the design of a reconfigurable metasurface capable of manipulating electromagnetic beams of either linear or circular polarization. As proof of concept, we report a programmable metasurface based on single dielectric layer by integrating the biasing network and isolation circuit onto the metasurface design. By adjusting the PIN diode states, stable phase modulation with high reflection efficiency could be achieved for different polarizations. The proposed programmable metasurface paves a way for potential applications in multi-polarized wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna at X-band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, an electronically reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (RRA) that operates in X-band is developed and simulated. Two P-I-N diodes are integrated in each element to obtain 1-bit phase compensation. The proposed element offers a stable angular response and polarization rotation in X-band. The element is applied to a 19×19 RRA for achieving beam scanning. The simulated result of the proposed RRA shows that the proposed RRA can achievea beam scanning ranging from -30° to 30° and a peak gain of 18.12 dBi.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Wideband Pattern Diversity Antenna with a Nonuniform Metasurface for Radio Fuze
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A metamaterial-base low profile wideband pattern diversity antenna is presented in this study. The proposed metasurface is constituted of a 4 × 4 array of patches. Modal behavior of the nonuniform metasurface is analyzed by using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). By changing the patches of the metasurface, the allocation of modes is achieved, which share the same patch resonator. Then, the selected modes are excited using a pair of appropriate feeding structures to achieve omnidirectional and broadside radiation patterns. At last, the overlapped impedance bandwidth is 9.1% (5.566.10GHz). The isolation is better than 30dB. The realized gains are 6.25 and 7.5 dBi, respectively. All the above mentioned performances are achieved within a low-profile design of only 0.068 λ0 (λ0 is the center operating wavelength in free space). The antenna has the potential to be used for radio fuze detection because of the beam-switching characteristics.

articleTitle: A Broadband 1-Bit Reconfigurable Huygens Element for Transmitarray in mmW Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This manuscript presents a broadband reconfigurable transmitarray element based on Huygens’ principle for millimeter-wave applications. The element consists of a pair of gradually varying dipoles printed on both sides of a substrate. The electric response is induced by the same directional currents on two dipoles. The magnetic response is generated by the current loop caused by the opposite directional currents on two dipoles and the coupling between them. By adjusting the size of these two gradually varying dipoles and the thickness of the substrate, the electric and magnetic resonances are balanced, which allows for a reflectionless Huygens resonance. Two p-i-n diodes have been loaded to realize a broadband 1-bit transmission phase compensation. The simulation results indicate that the proposed element can achieve an 11.3 % operating bandwidth from 29.3 GHz to 32.8 GHz with a transmission amplitude within -3.0 dB. Therefore, the proposed broadband 1-bit Huygens element has a good potential for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Safety Helmet Detection Method Based on YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the development of technology, the intelligence of traditional engineering becomes particularly important. Currently, the effects of the CBAM attention mechanism and data augmentation on YOLOv5s-based object detection models are proposed, and they are applied to determine whether safety helmets are worn in engineering land assessment. The experiment uses a safety helmet dataset, and the results show that the CBAM attention mechanism does not substantially improve the optimization of the model, while data augmentation significantly enhances the optimization of the model, with an average precision mean (mAP) reaching 90.2% and a recall rate of 81.5%.

articleTitle: Design of Electromagnetic Transmission/Absorption Structures Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a machine learning method is used to design an electromagnetic Rasorber. The XGBoost and Inception V3 model is used to design a transmission coded metasurface structure, and the full-wave simulation method is used to design a FSS absorbing structure. By combining the two methods, we design and optimize an electromagnetic Rasorber, which can realize microwave transmission around 6.5 GHz while microwave absorption in 8-10 GHz band.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarization Amplitude and Phase Modulated Active Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarization metasurface with adjustable amplitude and phase. The unit structure includes a Jerusalem cross metal patch on the top layer, a PIN diode loaded at the metal gap, a metal ground plate, and an F4B dielectric substrate located between the top layer metal patch and the ground plate. This structure allows for the manipulation of the amplitude and phase of the reflected electromagnetic waves. By changing the bias voltage on the diode, the equivalent resistance of the diode can be altered, thereby adjusting the phase and amplitude of the reflected waves. The phase manipulation bandwidth of the metasurface is 8.2-10.5 GHz, with a phase difference range of 180°±30° and a relative bandwidth of 24.6%. The amplitude manipulation bandwidth is 8.2-15.2 GHz, and the amplitude of the reflected waves within this bandwidth can be reduced to below -10 dB. Compared with a large metal plate of the same size, the array analysis of this unit structure shows an overall RCS reduction of 10 dBsm, with the reduction value at the resonance point even reaching 30 dBsm.

articleTitle: A Fast Stereo Matching Network Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Stereo matching is the most critical component of binocular stereo vision. Achieving an accurate and fast matching process is a key step in applying binocular stereo vision to real-world scenarios. Advanced stereo matching algorithms currently require significant computational resources, making them unsuitable for deployment on edge devices. We propose a fast stereo matching network using multi-scale feature fusion. This network employs a lightweight network to extract features, then performs multi-scale 2D convolution to fuse features and constructs a 4D cost volume. We further enhance our approach by incorporating a 3D multi-scale parallel feature fusion block into 3D U-Net architecture. This improved network enables parallel and skip connection-based feature fusion, followed by stereo disparity regression computation. Extensive experiments conducted on Scene Flow and KITTI 2015 datasets show that our proposed network attains both efficiency and accuracy. It achieves a disparity prediction speed of 19ms on GPU, with a 3-pixel error of 4.51% on KITTI 2015 and an EPE of 1.25px on Scene Flow.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm for Sparse Array with Superior Global Sidelobe Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In order to solve the challenge of sparse array optimization to achieve the global optimal peak sidelobe level, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced. This method is used to optimize a sparse array consisting of 60 antennas and 86 half-wavelength apertures. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional particle swarm optimization and simulated annealing algorithms, the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm has excellent performance in coping with the challenge of sparse array optimization.

articleTitle: Dual-Radiation Mode Leaky-Wave Antenna with Flat-Topped and End-Fire Beams Based on the Composite Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-radiation mode leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with flat-topped and end-fire beams based on the composite structure is proposed. A four-element LWA array using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is designed to generate four -1st space harmonics with different beam pointing angles, which are weighted and superimposed to form a flat-topped and wide-angle beam (including the broadside direction). The structure of printed tapered periodic leaky-wave strips realizes the end-fire directional radiation beam with broadband characteristics. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the dual-radiation mode composite structure proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Dual Broadband Antenna for V2X, LTE, and 5G Vehicular Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel dual broadband antenna tailored for vehicular applications. The antenna design incorporates circular and square patches, metal cylinders, and conductive vias. Our simulated results demonstrate an impressive impedance bandwidth spanning from 3.71 GHz to 3.85 GHz for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|<-10 and from 4.47 GHz to 5.91 GHz for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>|<-10, effectively covering crucial V2X, LTE, and early 5G frequency bands. Moreover, the proposed antenna showcases peak gains ranging from 5.62 dBi to 9.75 dBi, delivering exceptional directionality and wide beamwidth. These characteristics are aimed at ensuring reliable and efficient communication for modern vehicular systems, supporting advanced applications such as autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance system (ADAS).

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Metasurface for Full-space Terahertz Wave Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The utilization of metasurfaces to modulate electromagnetic waves in the terahertz (THz) band, especially the phase modulation of electromagnetic waves has attracted much attention. In this paper, a graphene meta-atom that can simultaneously manipulate the transmitted and reflected waves at the same frequency is designed. Graphene is a two-dimensional material with excellent electrical properties, and its conductivity can be changed by adjusting the applied electric field or voltage, thus realizing the dynamic regulation of electromagnetic wave amplitude and phase. According to the generalized Snell's law, the graphene metasurface array have been designed, which can achieve the full-space modulation of THz waves.

articleTitle: A Fast Analysis Method for Electromagnetic Scattering in Broad Frequency Band and Angular Domains of Periodic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A method is proposed for the rapid analysis of periodic arrays in the combined scenario of broad frequency and two-dimensional angular domains. This method initially extracts the characteristic mode basis functions at multiple frequency points and applies singular value decomposition to obtain a set of reduced basis independent of frequency, resulting in a reduced order equation significantly smaller than the traditional method of moments. Furthermore, to expedite the assembly process of the reduced matrix, the empirical interpolation method is employed to decouple the frequency and position information in the impedance and excitation matrices, as well as the additional incident angle information in the excitation matrix, thereby enabling fast analysis across a wide frequency band and for any incident angle.

articleTitle: An active metasurface for beam manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 2-bit active metasurface, where the resonant characteristics are altered by integrating a PIN diode to achieve beam scanning functionality. As a proof of concept, we fabricate a 20×20 periodic array capable of deflecting the reflected wave by angles of 15°, 30°, 45°, and 60° when subjected to vertically incident x-polarized waves. The suggested active metasurface holds promise for potential applications in wireless communication and imaging technologies.

articleTitle: Probing the Interaction Effect in Moderated Multiple Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The relationship between predictor variables and outcome variable has been the research focus in recent years. Interaction analysis is a form of multiple regression designed to test the effect of association of predictor variables on outcome variables. This research examines how the relationship between tourist experience quality and satisfaction changes with perceived service quality. By applying the simple slope approach and J-N technique, the interaction effect of tourism experience and perceived service quality is tested. The results of the moderation analysis shows that tourist experience has more effect on overall satisfaction on low service quality than high service quality. Based on the results, it is not enough only to focus on the attributes performance, researchers and managers should give more attention to the effect of combination of attributes perform for improving satisfaction.

articleTitle: Kernel Adaptive Filtering with Weibull M-transform Maximum Versoria Criterion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A kernel Weibull M-transform maximum-versoria-criterion (KWMMVC) algorithm is constructed, which is to use for nonlinear system identification. The KWMMVC algorithm ingeniously integrates the Weibull M-transform scheme into the maximum-versoria-criterion to formulate a novel cost function. The ability of KWMMVC algorithm to identify nonlinear channels under various impulse noise environments is tested in the kernel adaptive filters, and the results proved its superior performance.

articleTitle: Research on anti-jamming Antenna Based on Tiantong satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the application of satellite communication, phased array antennas play a role in real-time tracking of satellites. Due to the insufficient real-time performance of complex tracking algorithms, most tracking and anti-jamming algorithms rely on Beidou and inertial navigation to determine satellite direction, which increases the coupling between systems. This article improves the two-dimensional DOA estimation algorithm in phased array antennas without relying on Beidou positioning, and combines it with the baseband signal of Tiantong satellite for jamming identification and suppression. Through engineering implementation, it can achieve good anti-jamming performance.

articleTitle: Stealth Backdoor Attack for Remote Sensing Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Deep neural network models in remote sensing image classification tasks face the threat of backdoor attacks. The models attacked by backdoors can identify the injected trigger sample as the target label designed by the adversary, while the classification results for normal samples (samples without triggers) will not be affected. This paper proposes a stealth backdoor attack for remote sensing image classification. Specifically, we apply the rich geological information in remote sensing images to inject triggers that integrate with the image background, which are not easily noticeable. To improve the effectiveness of the attack, we perform targeted adversarial perturbations on the backdoor samples. During the training phase, both poisoned and clean samples are utilized as data for training the classification model. In the inference phase, the backdoor samples will be classified as the backdoor target category instead of the original category. Experiments on real-world datasets verify that the stealth backdoor attack method has strong attack effectiveness and stealthiness.

articleTitle: An adaptive filter algorithm using Ekblom for noise suppressing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: An advanced signal enhancement methodology, designated as the Ekblom adaptive filter (EAF) algorithm, has been developed. The algorithm is obtained by using the Ekblom norm and gradient descent method. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is better than other similar algorithms in noise suppression.

articleTitle: A Fast Analysis Method of Port Voltage Standing Wave Ratio for Special Cascade Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Based on the scattering matrix characteristics of lossless and reciprocal networks, a numerical solution for the standing wave ratio of port voltage in cascading lossless and reciprocal networks with any network is derived. Finally, the above analysis conclusions were validated through software simulation and actual testing, and the simulation and testing results proved the accuracy of the conclusions.

articleTitle: A Seawater Reconfigurable Antenna Based on 3d Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A seawater frequency reconfigurable antenna is proposed in this paper. A 3D-printed dielectric plate is used and three microfluidic channels are introduced in this patch antenna. By gradually injecting seawater into these channels, the equivalent dielectric constant of the substrate can be changed and the operating band of this antenna is altered. Simulation results show that the operating band of the antenna can be switched between 6.43 GHz-7.41 GHz (state 1), 6.47-7.46 GHz (state 2), 6.22-7.18 GHz (state 3) and 6.19 GHz-7.22 GHz (state 4). After injecting seawater, the S11 reached -33.93 dB, with a slight increase in relative bandwidth. The antenna has a simple design structure, low material cost, and is easy to implement. It has great prospects in the rapidly developing 6G applications in the future.

articleTitle: An Effective Kriging-assisted Water Flow Optimization for Ultra-wideband Monopole Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: An effective Kriging-assisted water flow optimization (KWFO) is proposed to address time-consuming antenna optimization problems. This method combines the outstanding search ability of water flow optimization and prediction capability of the Kriging model, which can significantly reduce the number of expensive fitness evaluations. Furthermore, a novel prescreening method is employed to reduce the risk of premature convergence by incorporating the strengths of expected improvement and lower confidence bound. The effectiveness of the KWFO algorithm is validated by the optimization of an ultra-wideband planar monopole antenna.

articleTitle: An Evanescent Wave Narrow-Band Diplex Filtenna Based on All-Metal Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: To adapt narrow-band diplex communication scenarios with the high-power and high-temperature characteristics, an all-metal diplex evanescent wave filtenna (EWF) is proposed in this work. Based on the principle of evanescent wave coupling and attenuation, the transmission pole (TP) and radiation null (RN) are introduced below the cutoff frequency by appropriately embedding capacitive metasurfaces (CMS) in the open-ended rectangular waveguide. Meanwhile, through the study of key parameters, a systematic design process is summarized that allows for the independent adjustment of TP and RN. Thus, a compact and all-metal diplex EWF with a frequency ratio of only 1.06 and a channel isolation of 31 dB between the two units is developed.

articleTitle: Optimal Arrangement of Time-shiftable Loads for Photovoltaic Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In recent years, with a rapid rise in power generation from distributed photovoltaic stations, there have been situations where the power users in the station area cannot consume photovoltaic power generation completely during the peak period of photovoltaic power generation. On the other hand, the energy storage support for the station areas is developing relatively slowly due to the high cost of energy storage facilities. For station areas with time-shiftable loads available, it is worth studying the optimal arrangement of time-shiftable loads as a low-cost and effective solution. Arranging time-shiftable loads from other periods to the peak period of photovoltaic power generation can effectively reduce the reverse peak power of the station area and the impact on the power grid, while not abandoning the generated photovoltaic energy. This paper finds the optimal arrangement through the greedy search algorithm, which can quickly and effectively solve the optimization. The solution has been proven to be the global optimal solution. Furthermore, by considering the distance between arrangements, the algorithm can be extended to a case evaluating the cost of adjustments. The algorithm was applied to the data from an on-site station area, and the reverse peak power was reduced as expected.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna for applications in microwave medical imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Vivaldi antenna for microwave medical imaging (MWI) constructed on an FR-4 substrate measuring 100 mm × 80 mm × 1.6 mm. By incorporating double elliptical slots on both sides of the traditional Vivaldi antenna and a unique pilot, the relative bandwidth has been expanded from 70% to 126%. Simulation results demonstrate that this ultra-wideband antenna functions within a bandwidth of 1.65-7.88 GHz, achieving a peak gain of 10.1 dBi and a front-to-back ratio exceeding 30 dB. Furthermore, simulation experiments have been conducted for microwave imaging of breast cancer, showcasing the antenna's capability to accurately locate tumors and its potential application in the realm of microwave medical imaging.

articleTitle: Knowledge Reasoning Based on The Knowledge Graph of Frequency Equipment for System-level Electromagnetic Spectrum Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: How to comprehensively, clearly, and accurately obtain the electromagnetic characteristics and relations of planning objects is an important issue in realizing efficient and flexible electromagnetic spectrum planning. In this paper, we use knowledge Graph, an intelligent technology in Semantic Web research, to construct the knowledge graph ontology of frequency equipment. We use the reasoning structure based on OWL + SWRL + Jess, combined with the OWL API to construct reasoning rules and procedures to complete the knowledge service required for system-level electromagnetic spectrum planning by setting up specific scenarios.

articleTitle: Interrupted sampling forwarding jamming parameter estimation based on YOLOv7-tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) is a new type of active coherent jamming technology based on the principle of under-sampling. It mainly uses the Doppler tolerance characteristics of wideband signals to achieve multi-false target jamming. The feasibility of the existing anti-ISRJ methods largely depends on the estimation accuracy of the key parameters of the interference. In order to ensure the accuracy and real-time performance of ISRJ parameter estimation under low jamming-to-noise ratio, this paper proposes a ISRJ feature parameter estimation algorithm based on YOLOv7-tiny object detection model with high precision and lightweight. Through simulation and comparative analysis of different methods, the method proposed in this paper can achieve parameter estimation for ISRJ under low jamming-to-noise ratio, and has high precision and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Fast Measurement of Single-Cut Far-Field Pattern of two-dimensional antenna array at a Quasi-Far-Field Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a method of correcting the single-cut far-field (FF) mode of a two-dimensional antenna array at a quasi-far-field (QFF) range by using separable excitation coefficient variables is presented. The measurement distance required by this method merely needs to meet the FF condition of the antenna element. The measurement process of QFF measurement is similar to FF measurement, which can improve the test efficiency significantly compared with nearfield (NF) measurement. To validate the proposed method, antenna array with different beam shapes were simulated.

articleTitle: Low-scattering Two-dimensional antenna array based on Zero-backtracking Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a two-dimensional antenna array based on zero-backtracking is designed. The array is based on the theory of Van Atta antenna array, by changing the length of transmission line, phase cancellation can be realized. In the simulation, the spherical coordinate system is established with the center of the model as the origin, and the result is compared with the metal plate of the same size. Results show that, when the azimuth angle of the incident wave is φ = 0°, the Radar Cross Section (RCS) is reduced for any pitching angle. When the azimuth angle of the incident wave is φ = 90°and the zenith angle θ is in range of -50°~ 50°, good RCS reduction can be realized and 38dB can be reduced at zero trap position.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Scanning and Backward Scattering-Reduced Phased Array Composed of Dual Anti-Reflection-Phase Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This work presents a planar phased array with wide-angle scanning and low backward scattering features. Two printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW)-fed wide-beam antennas with anti-phase reflection are designed and adopted as the array elements. The two elements are arranged in alternate rows with a same aperture size. Simulated results have validated the good radiation and scattering performance of the hybrid phased array. Detailly, the phased array shows a main-beam scanning range of ±57° with low sidelobe levels at 24.0 GHz. Besides, the array achieves a 10 dB reduction of backward radar cross section (RCS) within its operation band. The proposed phased array can be used for millimeter-wave vehicular radar systems.

articleTitle: A Design on Silicon-Based Millimeter-Wave Low Noise Amplifier Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper investigates the technology of silicon-based millimeter-wave low noise amplifiers (LNA). The LNA consist of two stages of amplifiers connected in cascade. The first stage circuit achieves low noise performance by utilizing minimum noise input matching. The second stage achieves high gain performance by utilizing high gain output matching.. The LNA in this paper achieves a gain S21 of 16 dB at a center frequency of 36 GHz with a noise figure (NF) as small as 5 dB.

articleTitle: A GeTe Phase-change RF Switch Design Based on Microstrip Line Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, an RF switch based on GeTe thermotropic phase transition is designed. In order to reduce the parasitic capacitance present in this switch, the switch adopts a microstrip line as the transmission line structure and a three-dimensional heated structure in the design. After simulation and comparison, the insertion loss of the new structure is less than 0.12 dB in the frequency band of 1-70 GHz. In the design of single-pole-double-throw switches, the size of the switches designed in this paper can be reduced to 300um*300um, and the insertion loss is less than 0.7 dB.

articleTitle: A Design of High-Gain, Polarimetric Conversion Reflection Filter Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: An "I"-shaped polarization conversion unit was developed in this study, capable of functioning at a frequency of 12 GHz. The design involved rotating metal patches on the unit by 90 degrees, resulting in an alternative unit with the same reflection coefficient and a phase difference of 180°. The final step involved incorporating choke rings around the "I"-shape to provide filtering functionality. Based on this, a high-gain filtering reflective array consisting of 20×20 proposed antenna unit was constructed. At 12 GHz, the attained gain was 24.7 dBi, and the radiation patterns for both H-plane and V-plane are demonstrated to be stable enough.

articleTitle: A Planar Dual Circularly Polarized Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A planar dual circularly polarized (dual-CP) wide-angle scanning phased array is proposed, which covers the WiFi communications bands of 5.7-5.9 GHz. The unit cell is composed of the radiation patches, metal cavity, and four L-shape metal walls. The L-shape metal walls and metal cavity are utilized to feed the radiation patch. Simultaneously, the metal cavity is used to suppress surface waves in order to expand the coverage of beam scanning. Sequential rotation is employed to reduce the axial ratio (AR) during scanning while forming the 2x2 subarray, which serves as a building block to build the 8x8 phased array. The phased array can achieve beam scanning from -45° to 45° with AR ≤ 3dB in the operating band (5.7-5.9GHz).

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Silicon Based SIP Design of the Four-Channel Phased Array Radar TR Module for Ka-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional silicon based SIP (System in Package) design of the four-channel phased array radar TR module for Ka-band applications. The SIP is manufactured using high-precision Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technology, and integrates lowloss Through-Silicon Via (TSV) vertical interconnection structures, power dividers, amplitude and phase control multifunctional chips, limiter chips, power amplifier chips, low-noise amplifier chips, and various power management chips. This SIP supports free switching among three different operating modes: transmit, receive, and load. The measured results indicate that all performance indicators meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of UCAA for OAM Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Currently, the uniform concentric circular array (UCCA) antenna has got great popularity and has been widely applied in many fields. However, there is little attention paid to its efficiency. When there is a bigger difference between the inner and outer radius of the UCCA, the synthesis efficiency is reduced gradually. The synthesis efficiency of the UCCA, considering the ratio of inner and outer ring radii, is studied in this paper. The characteristics of the divergence angle of UCCA under different radius ratios are analyzed. The result can be a valuable guidance for the UCCA design.

articleTitle: Automatic Radar Antenna Scan Type Recognition Based on the Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the radar electronic reconnaissance field, radar antenna scanning type recognition helps infer the function, working mode, and scanning pattern of the emitters, which is important for radar radiation source identification and threat level assessment. The recognition rate of the traditional machine learning and radial basis function based methods decreases in complex electromagnetic environments. In order to improve the recognition accuracy and reduce manual intervention, this paper proposes a radar antenna scanning recognition method based on the Residual Network, which enhances the recognition accuracy and efficiency. The simulated results of 7 different scanning modes show that the recognition accuracy can reach about 98.7%.

articleTitle: A Jamming Mitigation Method For Time-Domain Phase Modulation of Electromagnetic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Electromagnetic metasurface modulation, as a new type of flexible and controllable passive jamming technique, severely affects the radar target detection performance. To address this problem, a novel jamming mitigation method is proposed. The algorithm follows three steps. Firstly, the jamming modulation parameters are estimated by analyzing the time and frequency characteristics of metasurface-based jamming. Then, reconstruct the periodic jamming signal using the estimated modulation frequency and duty cycle. Finally, the periodic modulation jamming component be eliminated by multiplying the radar echo with time-delayed reconstructed modulation signal. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm not only effectively mitigates the metasurface periodic phase modulation jamming but also could improve the radar detection performance.

articleTitle: Study on a Dual-Function Thermoelectric Cooler-Thermoelectric Generator System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-function thermoelectric cooler-thermoelectric generator (TEC-TEG) system is investigated. Specifically, the TEC module in this system is utilized for cooling chips, while the TEG module is designed for waste heat recovery. An analytical model is established and validated with the experimental results, and the analytical solution shows good agreement with the actual data. Moreover, the TEC-TEG system is assessed in terms of the cooling capacity, output power, energy recovery efficiency, and coefficient of performance (COP). The system operating in the water-cooling condition performs better than the air-cooling one.
