The results suggest that powered by the input current of 2 A, the system achieves a cooling capacity of 13.93 W, an output power of 1.13 W, an energy recovery efficiency of 5.27%, and a COP close to 0.70.

articleTitle: Aircraft Part Recognition from Drones’ Perspective Based on Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Utilizing drones for aircraft surface inspection is a convenient and efficient approach. However, drones may encounter interference en route to the predetermined starting point of flight, leading to positioning deviations. Therefore, to assist drones in achieving more accurate positioning, this paper proposes an aircraft part recognition method from drones’ perspective based on semantic segmentation. This method aids in drone positioning by identifying parts of the aircraft such as the fuselage, wings, and engines. The YOLOv5-seg semantic segmentation model is employed for target segmentation and recognition. The Criss-Cross Attention module is added to enhance the recognition effect of aircraft parts, and Inner-IoU loss is applied to replace the CIoU loss to accelerate convergence. The results indicate that the method employed in this study achieves a mAP@0.5 of 92%, demonstrating a high level of accuracy in the recognition of aircraft parts, thus possessing significant practical application value.

articleTitle: A Compact Range Quiet Zone Detection Technology for Large Aperture THz Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The compact range provides a good measurement method for large aperture THz antennas, and the quality of their quiet zone performance directly affects the credibility of the measurement results. Compared to traditional compact range quiet zone detection, THz has significantly increased requirements for detection equipments due to its high frequency band and short wavelength. This article proposes a THz quiet zone detection method, which uses two laser trackers to measure the detection position coordinates in real time. The phase information of the quiet zone is corrected through post-processing, and then the amplitude of the quiet zone is separated from phase fluctuations and taper through mathematical fitting. Finally, the compressed field quiet zone index result is obtained.

articleTitle: PAPR Minimization based on Symbol Level Precoding in Multi-Receiver MISO-OFDM Fuze
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In multi-receiver MISO-OFDM fuze, we propose a solution on how to reduce the peak to average power ratio(PAPR). Specifically, due to the implementation of constructive interference (CI) and the PAPR limitation of each antenna, we establish an optimization problem aimed at minimizing the total transmit power. And then we turn the former non-convex issue to a completely equivalent convex issue, which can be sovled directly through off-the-shelf convex optimization toos like CVX. Numerical results verify that the theory has higher performance than existing methods in terms of total transmission power and PAPR.

articleTitle: Exact Observation Based Phase Preservation Bistatic SAR Sparse Imaging: Initial Result
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Due to the capability of acquiring non-backscattering information, bistatic synthetic aperture radar (BiSAR) extends the application scope of synthetic aperture radar (SAR). Sparse SAR imaging has demonstrated remarkable potential in enhancing the recovered image quality. However, traditional regularization reconstruction algorithms for sparse SAR imaging fail to maintain the background distribution of the image and completely disrupt its phase. To address above problem, this paper proposes a phase-preserving BiSAR sparse imaging method. The proposed method firstly constructs an exact observation matrix to achieve deconvolution of the BiSAR echo. Then, it employs an improved iterative soft thresholding (IST) algorithm to solve the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> norm regularization problem for scene recovery. The results of the experiment indicate that the proposed method outperforms traditional regularization reconstruction algorithms by achieving both sparse imaging of the observed scene and maintaining phase information through a non-sparse estimation.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Generation with Millimeter-Wave Radar for UAV Taxiing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The autonomous obstacle avoidance technology for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) taxiing is used to improve efficiency and ensure safety. Many target detection and obstacle avoidance methods based on point cloud have been proposed, which need more point cloud data to evaluate the performance. As a key part, point cloud generation by simulating is more flexible but more complex, especially for scenes with multiple targets. To solve this problem, a point cloud generation method with millimeter-wave radar for UAV taxiing is proposed. Firstly, the coordinates of the targets’ vertex are converted to the radar coordinate, and the edges of the targets are decomposed to detection points. Then, a line-of-sight point cloud is generated by abandoning miss detection edges and points. Finally, the echo signals based on the characteristics of the targets are generated. Experimental results demonstrate that the generated point cloud is in accord with the scene setting and the target features contained in the echo signal are also correct.

articleTitle: Absorbing Boundary Condition for the Hexagonal-Mesh-Based FDTD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Compared with the traditional Yee grid FDTD, the hexagonal grid is more complicated to implement the absorbing boundary. Here, we present an absorbing boundary approach for the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method based on hexagonal mesh. The implementation of the proposed absorbing boundary is introduced. The absorbing efficiency of the boundary is verified by simulating the electromagnetic propagation in the free space.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Bandwidth-Improved Transmitarray Antenna with Phase-Shifting Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a high efficiency and bandwidth-improved transmitarray antenna. The antenna employs a phase-shifting element with three metallic layers. This element is based on the principle of polarization conversion, which enables a phase coverage of approximately 300° by adjusting the relevant parameters in the phase-shift element. This element features a low transmission loss throughout the entire working frequency band. An improved phase compensation scheme is proposed to enhance the efficiency of the array antenna. This scheme incorporates the introduction of a reference phase and a more precise evaluation function to calculate the weighted phase errors corresponding to different schemes. A transmitarray comprising 20 × 20-element is designed with the phase-shifting elements. The simulated results show that the 1-dB and 3-dB bandwidth are 16.8% and 28.8% respectively. Within the 1-dB gain bandwidth, the aperture efficiency is better than 31%, and the peak aperture efficiency and peak gain are 47% and 28.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Helix Antenna Using Parallel Arms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band helix antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of radiation arms, feeding network and parasitic branches. Two sets of radiation arms realize dual-band operation and the feeding network sequentially feeds the arms to provide circular polarization. In order to widen beamwidth of radiation pattern, parasitic branches are loaded around the antenna. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna realizes dual resonant bands, the main beamwidth is greater than 0dB within 120 degree covering dual band.

articleTitle: A Fast Algorithm Based on PMCHW for Solving Composite Metallic and Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A Green’s function interpolation method based on the PMCHW equation is proposed for analyzing electromagnetic problems of objects that including conductive and dielectric parts. This problem is solved using surface integral equations to solve the problem of uniform dielectrics and conductors. In order to improve computational efficiency, the PMCHW equation is combined with the multilevel Green’s function interpolation method. Based on this method, it can support the treatment of metals with limited conductivity and the treatment for the junctions of two different materials. This method is suitable for solving problems such as microstrip antenna arrays, RF and microwave devices. Numerical example demonstrates the accuracy and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Beam-Pattern Synthesis with Consideration of Mutual Coupling by MOEA/D-IWO-AEP Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In order to solve complex beam pattern synthesis problem with consideration of the electromagnetic compatibility problems of array elements, a hybrid method consists of Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm based on Decomposition (MOEA/D), Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO) and Active Element Pattern (AEP) is proposed in this paper. The proposed method is verified effective and meaningful for actual practice by using it to optimize a three-objective synthesis problem.

articleTitle: A Wideband 8-Element Dual-Circularly-Polarization Dielectric Rod Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This article presents an 8-element dual-circularly-polarization dielectric rod array antenna based on 5G millimeter-wave band. Each antenna element consists of a metal waveguide embedded stepped diaphragm and dielectric rod antenna, which is fed by dual port feed. The operational frequency range of each antenna is from 24.25 GHz to 27.5 GHz. In addition, the dielectric filled into the polarizer is adopted to meet the needs of component miniaturization, and the impedance matching between the antenna and the air is improved by extending the dielectric rod antenna, which achieves better input impedance bandwidth and isolation better than 20 dB over the operating band. The simulation results indicate that the antenna element exhibits a return loss with |S11|<-22 dB over the operating band, the axial ratio remains below 0.7 dB, and the realized gain is greater than 6.92 dB. Additionally, the 8-element array exhibits robust beam-scanning capabilities with a maximum beam-scanning angle of 51°. Finally, the peak gain of the antenna array is 15.3dBi.

articleTitle: ISAR Super-Resolution Imaging and Denoising Based on 2D Complex-Value Approximate Message Passing Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging is an important tool for air and surface target detection. Usually, the higher the resolution of an ISAR system, the more target information is contained in its imaging results. ISAR super-resolution imaging algorithms can enhance the resolution of an ISAR system with no change in hardware conditions and are one of the most convenient ways to obtain high-resolution ISAR images. Existing ISAR super-resolution imaging algorithms perform poorly in performing high-magnification super-resolution tasks and are sensitive to noise. To overcome these problems, this work designs a 2D complex-value approximate message passing network (2D-CAMPnet) to simultaneously realize ISAR super-resolution imaging and denoising. Specifically, the low-resolution echoes can be regarded as block samples of the high-resolution echoes. Therefore, we employ the 2D-AMP algorithm to recover the high-resolution 2D spatial distribution of the target from the low-resolution echoes for ISAR super-resolution imaging. Then we unfold the 2D-AMP algorithm into the form of a neural network and optimize the algorithm hyperparameters using network training to make the algorithm capable of denoising. Measured data experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of performance and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficient Solution of Propagation coefficient in Biaxial Anisotropic Media Employing Simplified Transfer Matrix Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we employ the simplified transfer matrix method (STMM) to calculate the propagation coefficient of electromagnetic waves in biaxial anisotropic media. Firstly, starting from the Maxwell’s equation, the Helmholtz’s equation regarding the electric field can be obtained. Subsequently, by simplifying the Helmholtz’s equation, the corresponding 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order partial differential equation for a certain component of the electric field can be given. By analyzing the differential equation, the eigenvalues of biaxial anisotropies at different frequency points can be ensured. Finally, based on the eigenvalues, a matrix of electromagnetic field components is constructed to obtain the specific solution form for reflection and transmission coefficients. To verify the effectiveness of the STMM method, we apply STMM and COMSOL to calculate the reflection and transmission coefficients of single-layered biaxial anisotropic media. The results indicate that STMM has the advantages of accuracy and high efficiency compared to COMSOL software.

articleTitle: A Joint Solution Method of Orthogonal Matching Pursuit and Improved Harris Hawk Optimization for 5G Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The sparse nature of the 5G channel makes the orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm a suitable method for 5G positioning. However, the implementation of positioning in three-dimensional scenes requires a much more complex spatial angle dictionary than that in two-dimensional space, which makes it almost impossible to calculate direction of arrival (DOA) using OMP. Aiming at above problem, joint OMP and improved Harris Hawk Optimization (HHO) method was proposed. This method first calculates the time of arrival (TOA) of the received signal through OMP and performs spatial filtering to reduce the non-line of sight (NLOS) component. Then, the improved HHO algorithm based on information sharing mechanism is used to solve DOA, so as to achieve high-precision 5G positioning using only a single base station. Simulation results show that the proposed method has higher positioning performance than some popular algorithms such as subspace-based method.

articleTitle: A High-gain and Low-sidelobe Directional Radiating Waveguide Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Waveguide slot antenna is widely used in ground, ship and airborne radar because of its compact structure, high radiation efficiency and easy control of sidelobe. In this paper, a high gain and low secondary directional radiative waveguide slot antenna is proposed and simulated by electromagnetic simulation software HFSS. The simulation results show that in the working band of the antenna, the east gain of the directional wave is greater than 20dBi, the subcontrol is greater than 20dB, the beam on the H-plane of the antenna can point to 50°, and beamwidth of the E-plane pattern greater than 15dB is 86°. The antenna can achieve good beam pointing characteristics and high gain of directional beam. It has wide application prospect in satellite communication, mobile communication and shipboard communication. It is a kind of antenna with high performance and high reliability.

articleTitle: Measurement of Sheet Resistance of Heated Coated Glass using Cylindrical Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Coated glass, as a common material for green building facades, may experience temperature change due to sunlight and its physical properties may thus be affected. Considering relation between the physical properties and sheet resistance of coated glass, this paper proposes a measurement method for sheet resistance of coated glass at temperatures higher than room temperature by using a cylindrical cavity resonator working with TE011 mode at around 28 GHz. A heating platform is used to heat the sample (from room temperature to 60°C). To minimize temperature variation of the cavity itself, an air gap, ranging from 0 ~ 2 mm, is introduced between the cavity and the sample. Preliminary results indicates that the sheet resistance of coated glass decreases with temperature which agree with existed publications. Thus, the obtained results verified the feasibility and reliability of this measurement method.

articleTitle: BeautyGuard: Style Transfer-Based Adversarial Beautification for Facial Privacy Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The widespread use of deep face recognition (FR) systems has raised concerns about privacy breaches. Current techniques often use adversarial noise to protect facial privacy, but these methods typically suffer from poor visual quality and low adversarial transferability. To address these challenges, a novel approach called Adversarial Beautification GAN (AB-GAN) is proposed. This approach employs GANs to generate "beautified noise" that protects facial images from being recognized by FR systems. Experiments on the CelebA-HQ and FFHQ datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of AB-GAN. Compared to existing methods, AB-GAN not only provides better privacy protection but also significantly enhances the visual quality of the images.

articleTitle: Testing and Analysis of DC/DC Circuit Boards Based in ESD Interference Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study conducted testing and analysis on ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) interference sources for DC/DC (Direct Current-Direct Current) circuit boards. ESD, as a common electromagnetic interference source, significantly impacts the stability and reliability of electronic devices. By simulating ESD interference sources on DC/DC circuit boards, this research systematically evaluated their effects on circuit board performance. Initially, a standardized ESD testing environment was established by constructing an experimental platform. Subsequently, the study observed the operational status and performance variations of DC/DC circuit boards under ESD interference, analyzing their response characteristics at different interference levels. Experimental results demonstrate that ESD interference sources notably affect the output stability and efficiency of DC/DC circuit boards, with increased interference levels leading to more severe performance degradation. Finally, a series of improvement measures were proposed based on the test results to enhance the anti-interference capability and reliability of DC/DC circuit boards, providing valuable references for the design and application of electronic devices. This research , offering significant insights and guidance , serves as a reliable reference point for understanding and addressing performance issues of DC/DC circuit boards under ESD interference.

articleTitle: Analysis of Low-Altitude UAV-to-Ground Channel Characteristics in Rural Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Understanding the characteristics of UAV-to-ground communication channels is important for the development of future intelligent wireless environments. This paper presents a broadband UAV-to-ground channel measurement campaign at 2.7 GHz, based on which the large scale and the small scale channel characteristics are evaluated for UAV flight altitudes of 300 and 400 meters in a rural environment. For these two altitudes, a Log-distance path loss model is developed and the shadow fading is found to be Log-normal distributed. For the small-scale characteristics, the amplitude of the received signal is compared with a number of different distributions and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test is applied to determine that the Ricean distribution is the best fit among considered theoretical fading distributions. Finally, a distance dependent K factor model is proposed in the paper.

articleTitle: Tensor model built from vector for Angle and Doppler frequency estimation with Expanded Nested Spatial-Temporal Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, the transmit-receive array and delay receive stage of MIMO radar are configured in an expanded nested mode to enhance the estimation of parameters. Initially, the transmit-receive array of MIMO radar is set up as an expanded nested array, and the time intervals for the delay receivers are similarly patterned. Subsequently, we obtain and vectorize the covariance matrix of the received signals to expand the degrees of freedom (DOF) in both the time and spatial domains. After eliminating redundant spatial-temporal DOFs, we directly construct a tensor on the basis of the new single snapshot signals and employ tensor decomposition techniques to extract the angle and Doppler parameters of targets. Compared to traditional methods, this approach reduces the computational burden of solving for the pseudo-covariance matrix by directly constructing tensors from vectors. Additionally, this method also expands the DOF in the time and spatial domains, significantly enhancing the precision of parameter estimation. A series of simulation experiments validate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection of Hardware Attacks in Network on Chip Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Network on Chip (NoC) is commonly used as the interconnection topology in modern multi-core System on Chip (SoC) architecture. The extensive use of NoC and its pervasive integration across the chip render it a primary target for Hardware Trojan (HT) attacks. Modeling and detecting potential attacks are essential for ensuring the security of NoC. This paper proposes a HT detection scheme based on traffic-attacking HT. The Gem5 platform is utilized to establish attack models for extracting features. Then, using a Bayesian model to identify change points and a random forest algorithm to identify abnormal change points. The experimental results show that the average detection accuracy of Trojans can reach 99.43%.

articleTitle: Transparent CPW-fed Antenna Array for 5G Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Transparent antennas represent a novel antenna technology with broad application potential in various fields such as the Internet of Things (IoT), vehicular communication, and displays. With the advancement of 5G communication, the design of traditional mobile phone antennas is increasingly constrained by space limitations. Researchers have proposed integrating antennas into displays to address this challenge. This letter presents the design of a CPW-fed TAA with two units. The operating frequency band of this antenna array is 2.86-4.06 GHz, covering the n78 band used in 5G communications, meeting the design objectives. The CPW fed TAA has a transparency of 92%, a gain of 7.9 dB, and an efficiency of over 85%. This high-gain, high-efficiency, and high-transparency TAA can effectively support 5G communication applications in mobile phones, providing reliable communication performance for modern mobile devices.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based High-Power Microwave Near-Field Reconstruction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Neural Network-Based High-Power Microwave Near-Field Reconstruction Method for assessing and analyzing high-power pulse measurements in electromagnetic engineering. Traditional near-field measurements face challenges with instantaneous high peak power and short pulse widths in high-power pulse signals. The proposed method leverages neural networks to enhance data processing efficiency and analysis, demonstrating effectiveness in reconstructing the entire spatial field. The training process showcases convergence after 1000 iterations, with computational efficiency suitable for real-time applications.

articleTitle: Research on Power Efficiency Optimization of Resonant BD-WPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Compared with the traditional unidirectional wireless power transmission system, Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer (BD-WPT) not only inherits the advantages of easy operation, no contact spark and leakage, and intelligent management, but also realizes the two-way flow of energy. Therefore, energy interconnection between devices can be achieved, which further improves the flexibility, convenience and utilisation of electrical energy use. In the LCC-LCC-type WPT system studied in this paper, there are three phase-shift angles, and the adjustment of the phase-shift angle can not only regulate the power size, but also determine the direction of power flow. Therefore, this paper analyses the influence of the primary side phase shift angle on the output power from the principle of phase shift power regulation, and then analyses the influence of the secondary side phase shift angle on the improvement of the transmission efficiency from the principle of fully controlled rectification. Finally, the impact of three phase shift angles on power efficiency is comprehensively analyzed for the characteristics of BD-WPT system with three phase shift angles. And the BD-WPT system model is established by Simulink for simulation verification.

articleTitle: Auxiliary Classifier GAN-Based Super-resolution Microwave Coincidence Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Microwave coincidence imaging (MCI) has attracted more and more attention, but the number of the low correlated measurement modes is limited leading to a limited imaging performance. The unsupervised data augmentation can be achieved by the Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to address the issue of limited samples. In this paper, an Auxiliary Classifier GAN-based super-resolution imaging method for MCI is proposed. To achieve the classification of ten uniformly distributed target points within the 3dB beamwidth (i.e. 10 times super-resolution imaging), a training dataset is designed based on the spatial correlation characteristics of the reference radiation field in MCI systems. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach can effectively generate high-quality samples to meet classification requirements. Compared with other methods, the accuracy and classification efficiency can be improved.

articleTitle: Integrated Design of X-band Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna and Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A magneto-electric dipole antenna is designed and loaded with a three-branch directional coupler to achieve a dual circularly polarized function, which is fed through an L-shaped probe. A low-profile, low insertion loss sixth-order cavity filter is also designed for left-hand and right-hand circular polarization feeding through two ports, respectively. After connecting the antenna to the filter, the resulting structure has a return loss of less than -10 dB at 7.5-9 GHz, an axial ratio of less than 2 dB, isolation of less than -20 dB at the center frequency, and a realized gain of 5.2 dB at 8.25GHz.

articleTitle: Design Approach of The Wideband Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, in order to feed the phased array antenna, the design method of the two-way, four-way, and eight-way power divider is presented. Firstly, the two-way power divider with wide bandwidth performance is proposed and designed by using the microstrip feeding line with the resister. Based on this method, the four-way and eight-way power dividers have been consequently designed and simulated. According to the simulation results, our designed eight-way power divider exhibits good matching across the operating band from 8 to 12 GHz., herein the value of its S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is kept of below of -12dB at the center frequency, and the VSWR is lower than 1.45 in most frequency. What’s more, the insertion loss of the divider is maintained of less than 0.2 dB, while keeping the desired isolation of above 12dB.

articleTitle: Vehicle Recognition Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study utilizes the YOLOv5 model, a rapid object detection algorithm known for maintaining high accuracy while possessing fast recognition capabilities and covering a wide range of target categories. YOLOv5 is renowned for its fast processing speed, outstanding accuracy, and lightweight model files, making it suitable for lower-configured mobile devices. The focus of this research is on batch detection of various vehicle types. The dataset is subjected to data augmentation, and a small object detection layer is added to the model. The experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an accuracy of 90.9%, with a truck detection accuracy of 95.7% and a recall rate of 89.4%. This study holds practical and generalizable value, providing technical support and references for real-world applications such as road traffic management and parking fee collection.

articleTitle: An Intermodulation Matrix Method for PIM Evaluation of Microstrip Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The intermodulation (IM) matrix was deduced to express the PIM model of the a uniform microstip line, which was further applied to analyze the more complicated PIM product phenomenon of microstrip filter and quadrature hybrid in this paper. The distributed PIM source in microstrip circuit can be modeled as current and voltage sources in the equivalent lumped circuit model, by using which a matrix expression with simple form for the PIM voltage and current in a uniform strip was obtained. If a microstrip circuit can be split into several uniform transmission lines, like quadrature hybrid coupler, its PIM level can be solved by considering the matrix formulas of each split strip line. The calculation result of the quadrature hybrid coupler indicates that the order of the PIM level for the four ports from the largest one to the smallest one is the coupled port, the transmitted port, the input port and the isolated port at the center frequency.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Antenna Array covering the X-band for the Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Many Ultra-Wideband (UWB) antennas have been proposed, but no compact designs have addressed the X-band (8-12 GHz) specifically. This paper introduces a wideband antenna designed for X-band radar applications, featuring an impedance bandwidth of 6.4-13.3 GHz with an S11 less than -10 dB, covering the fully X-band. To validate the design, a prototype was fabricated and its performance was measured. Simulations indicate a maximum gain of 16.3 dB, while the measured maximum gain is 15.6 dB, showing excellent agreement between simulation and measurement results. It is highly likely that this antenna will be widespread used in radar systems.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Cascaded Power Amplifier for Military Individual Radio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a tremendous interest in military individual radio in wireless communication. To obtain sufficient operating distance and long standby time, the output power and efficiency of power amplifiers have become the research focus by some of the research teams. GaN has higher electron mobility and forbidden bandwidth than other materials. Nowadays, GaN has become the mainstream key technology for radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers in 5G communication systems. In this work, a 500MHz~2500MHz GaN-based HEMT wideband cascaded power amplifier was designed. The output power of the driver amplifier is 36.6dBm ± 0.5dB, the input return loss is < -5dB, the drain efficiency is > 20%, the DC power consumption is < 25W, the input power is 5dBm, 1dB compression point is 7.8dBm, 0 dBm signal input and 33dBm signal output. The input power of the output stage is 36dBm; the output power is 44.75dB, the efficiency is more than 30%, and the input return loss < -8dB, small signal gain >10 dB, input voltage standing wave ratio < -10dB, output voltage standing wave ratio < -3dB. The demonstrated high performance of the cascaded power amplifier validates its applications in military wireless communication.

articleTitle: Improving Antenna Isolation for Bistatic In-band Full-duplex Base Station Application with Graphene and DGS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, graphene structures and DGS structures are proposed to improve Tx-Rx port isolation of a bistatic dual-polarization antenna array for in-band full-duplex base station application. Tx to Rx isolation is greater than 66 dB in the working frequency range of 4.8-5GHz, with little deterioration in radiation performance and antenna matching.

articleTitle: Clutter Suppression Based on ICUR-RPCA for Random Missing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The performance of clutter suppression in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems is significantly compromised by random missing data. Typically, traditional methods frequently encounter a balance between accuracy and computational complexity. To address the problem, a clutter suppression method based on inverse CUR-robust principal component analysis (ICUR-RPCA) is proposed for the random missing data. Taking advantage of the low-rank property, key nodes entries are completed with reorganizing the whole echo data, first. Subsequently, RPCA is combined with the recovered key nodes and ICUR decomposition, so that the clutter suppression performance with the completed whole data can be achieved by only completing a portion of the data. Finally, the superiority of our ICUR-RPCA method is shown in numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Low Numerical Dispersion LOD-FDTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This work addresses the significant dispersion error in the locally one-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (LOD-FDTD) method by proposing a novel approach featuring isotropic dispersion, known as ID-LOD-FDTD. This method linearly weights the traditional Yee scheme and the isotropic scheme by using a determined weighting factor. Additionally, a scaling factor is used to further correct the normalized phase velocity, making it approach the exact value. The paper provides the derivation process of the dispersion formula for the new method. During the simulation process, the novel method is benchmarked against the traditional LOD-FDTD method, demonstrating the ID-LOD-FDTD method’s superiority in attaining more isotropic dispersion.

articleTitle: A Serial-Fed Antenna Implementation for 60GHz Millimeter-Wave Radar Altimetry on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology has seen significant advancements, leading to its adoption across various sectors. In this paper, we present a radar antenna system designed around the Calterah-IE chip, which utilizes frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) technology and operates in the carrier frequency range of 61 GHz to 63 GHz. By employing a power divider, we have developed an 8×8 series-fed array antenna composed of eight elements arranged in eight columns, enhanced through specific feeding techniques and array configurations to bolster the antenna's gain and directivity for stable operation at 61 GHz to 63 GHz. Simulations have demonstrated the theoretical capability of an 8×8 Series-Fed Antenna Array system, with its narrow beamwidth, to provide accurate and stable altitude information for UAVs. Moreover, the antenna's compact size and lightweight design make it particularly suitable for integration into small UAV platforms.

articleTitle: Spatial Spectrum Estimation Direction Finding Algorithm of Uniform Linear Array Based on Virtual Array Transformation and Data Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Spatial spectrum direction finding is a kind of radio signal direction finding technology which combines multi-element antenna and multi-channel signal processing. The spatial spectrum estimation technique has been extensively utilized in both military and civilian fields in the process of continuous development of science and technology. As for the applications in military field, it makes a crucial contribution to intelligence reconnaissance and electronic countermeasures as a passive detection technique. However, if there are multiple incident signals simultaneously which are coherent or have a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the direction-finding performance will degrade notably. In this paper, a direction-finding algorithm with spatial spectrum estimation for uniform linear arrays (ULAs) based on virtual arrays and data augmentation was proposed to address this problem. Firstly, a basic signal model for the direction-finding with spatial spectrum estimation was established based on the direction-finding principle; next, the conventional direction-finding algorithm was improved by utilizing the virtual array transformation, forward/backward spatial smoothing (FBSS) and data augmentation; finally, three simulation experiments were carried out for analysis and discussion of the results. The simulation findings herein demonstrated the correctness of the algorithm proposed and its adaptability to multiple coherent signals.

articleTitle: Intelligent Takeaway Delivery Vehicle Based on Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This design proposes an STM32-based delivery vehicle solution for takeaway delivery. The program consists of infrared reflection sensor, pressure detection module, GSM module, MPU6050 module, Bluetooth module, ultrasonic module. Through the path planning algorithm and PID algorithm, it realizes the delivery vehicle low-power takeout delivery and completes the function of intelligent takeout delivery.

articleTitle: A Leaky-Wave Beam Scanning Antenna with PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable digital modulation leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is proposed. This antenna does not require additional ADC/DAC modules and mixing circuits, which simplifies the antenna structure design. By introducing diodes, the proposed antenna realizes digital beam scanning and digital modulation of the leaky-wave. By inputting different digital codes, the multi-beam switching functionality is achieved, thereby realizing the purpose of beam reconfigurability. A low-cost and easy-to-manufacture metasurface radiator is fabricated, which can achieve the leaky-wave radiation effect. In summary, the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for realizing beam reconfigurability in future intelligent wireless communications.

articleTitle: Multi-band Independently Tunable Terahertz Perfect Absorber Based on Graphene Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The paper presents a graphene-based independently tunable multi-band terahertz perfect absorber with polarization-insensitive and incidence angle-insensitive properties. The absorber consists of graphene structures, the dielectric layer and a metallic base plate. The simulation indicates that all three peaks of absorptances reached 99.9% at 2.09 THz, 3.53 THz and 5.91 THz. And the absorber is polarization insensitive and incidence angle insensitive in the operating frequency band of 1THz-6.5THz. In addition, The application of this absorber as a sensor to detect the concentration of glucose solution is investigated. Finally, the independently tunable function of the absorber is also discussed. The absorber proposed in this paper may be potentially applied, such as THz wave sensing, electromagnetic stealth and modulators.

articleTitle: Incident Power Density Evaluation Method Based on Metalens and R-U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Incident power density(IPD) is commonly used to quantify the electromagnetic exposure of human body above 6 GHz. In this paper, a novel method of field reconstruction based on metalens and deep learning is proposed to evaluating IPD. Metalens is used to overcome ill-conditioned problem in the reconstruction process. Inputting focused planar electric field, the neural network model outputs the evaluating planar electric field. This method greatly improves the reconstruction accuracy compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Absorptive-Polarization-Converting Metasurface for Dynamic Wavefront Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable absorptive-polarization-converting metasurface with 1-bit phase response is proposed for dynamic wavefront control. An absorber is cascaded on a reconfigurable polarization-converting metasurface for out-of-band electromagnetic absorption at lower frequency. Simulated results show that a broad -10 dB copolarization suppression bandwidth from 2.6 GHz to 7.7 GHz can be achieved. Meanwhile, the considerable cross-polarization reflection above -3 dB with 1-bit phase difference from 5.4 GHz to 7.8 GHz is supported by ON/OFF switching of PIN diodes. As exemplary verifications, dual beam generation and diffusive scattering are presented, where the simulated beam-steering angles agree with the theoretical ones. With the attractive features of reconfigurability and wide bandwidth, our design shows great potential in wireless information communication and scattering suppression.

articleTitle: Modified Pattern Multiplication Approach for Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: For precise beam analysis of a radiating phased array, it is essential to account for mutual coupling and array edge effect. However, the traditional pattern multiplication principle neglects the mutual coupling effect. By incorporating knowledge of the active element pattern (AEP), we propose a modified pattern multiplication approach that includes compensations for mutual coupling and edge effect. This modified approach enables rapid computation of the radiation characteristics of phased arrays. Numerical example demonstrates the validity and accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: Application of Evolutionary Computing for Optimal Design of Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study outlines the development and refinement of an innovative base station antenna for contemporary wireless communication systems, which operates within the frequency range of 1.9 to 4.9 GHz. The antenna is made of copper and has a radiating patch thickness of 0.2 mm. The ground patch measures 38×38 mm and the total height of the antenna is 16 mm. The performance of the system relies on four reflecting walls that have been carefully carved to reduce out-of-band radiations and minimize interference. The antenna attains a peak gain of 6 dBi throughout the operational range, while keeping the |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| parameters below -10 dBi, ensuring effective signal transmission. The process of optimization involves the utilization of evolutionary computers, more specifically a Genetic Algorithm, to meticulously adjust the design parameters. This approach guarantees that the antenna fulfills the demanding criteria of high gain and wide bandwidth, offering a strong and reliable solution for modern communication requirements.

articleTitle: A ViT Merged Oriented-Detector with Neuron Attention for Ship Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Due to the unique microwave properties of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images and the irregular distribution of vessels, deep learning techniques face significant challenges in the detection of ship targets within SAR imagery. This paper proposes an oriented ship target detection model based on the YOLOv8 algorithm, Neural Swin Transformer-YOLO (NST-YOLO). Experiments conducted on the Rotated Ship Detection Dataset in SAR Images (RSDD-SAR) and the SAR Ship Detection Dataset (SSDD+) and comparisons with the other oriented detection models demonstrate that the proposed NST-YOLO achieves state-of-the-art detection performance.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Independently Modulatable Dual-Frequency Energy-Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This article presents a detailed analysis of energy selective surfaces (ESS) in terms of equivalent circuits and resonant modes. Based on its nonlinear transmission characteristics, it is made to realize adaptive protection at high-power microwave (HPM). With the help of Equivalent Circuit Principle, the ESS is designed and analyzed, the effects of different ECM on the ESS are analyzed and a suitable ECM is optimized, and a dual-frequency energy selective surface is designed based on the ECM. The designed model consists of F R 4 with a dielectric constant of 4.3, capacitor and diode. The physical model is finally fabricated and tested, and the experimental results are consistent with the simulation results. At low-power, the insertion loss (IL) is less than 1 dB at the center frequencies of 2.6 GHz and 5.8 GHz, and at high-power, a shielding performance greater than 20 dB is observed. ESS adaptive shielding is realized.

articleTitle: New Electromagnetic Adjustable Angle Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In order to improve the simulation flexibility of the electromagnetic characteristics of the radar angle reflector, a new design of the radar angle reflector with adjustable electromagnetic characteristics is proposed. The amplitude of the reflection coefficient is changed by introducing a PIN diode whose resistance value varies with voltage. A square three-hedral angular reflector is taken as an example to simulate and verify that the radar cross section (RCS) can be changed by spatial modulation of the amplitude control structure, and the variation range is about 30dBsm. The theoretical analysis results are in good agreement with the full-wave simulation results, which shows the feasibility of the proposed method. This research method applies the spatial modulation theory to the radar angle reflector to simulate the target with variable RCS and variable distance, which provides a broader application idea and background support for its application.

articleTitle: A Microwave Sensor for Detection of Water Adulteration and Spoilage in Milk Based on Split-Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The paper introduces a microwave sensor based on split-ring resonators (SRR) for detecting the moisture content and spoilage of milk. This sensor is characterized by its simple structure and high sensitivity, utilizing SRR to enhance the local electric field intensity of the electromagnetic field. By measuring the transmission characteristics of microwave signals, it can accurately detect the moisture content and spoilage of milk samples. The sensor operates at a frequency of 6 GHz and has dimensions of 30×25×1.6 mm³. The study establishes the relationship between resonance frequency and water content in milk through simulated data, which provides an effective method for monitoring milk quality and holds potential applications in the food industry, contributing significantly to ensuring food safety.

articleTitle: Wideband reconfigurable bow-tie metasurface design for focusing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband reconfigurable metasurface design with operating frequency set at 6 GHz by using PIN diode. When the external voltage control diode is switched on or cut off, the reflection phase of the structure presents a phase difference of 180°, with low reflection loss, and the relative bandwidth can reach 45%, with broadband characteristics. By controlling the reflection phase of different regions of the metasurface, near-field focusing can be achieved, and the focus position can be adjusted.

articleTitle: An Energy Efficient CMA Equalizer based on Approximate Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Constant Modulus Algorithm (CMA) has found extensive application within digital communication systems. Unlike traditional adaptive equalizers, the CMA equalizer leverages its own statistical properties to recover signals from channel interference, obviating the need for training sequences. However, the significant number of multiplier units required by the CMA algorithm can lead to excessive circuit overhead. Approximate computing offers a promising approach to achieving high performance while mitigating circuit complexity. In this study, we propose an approximation scheme tailored specifically for the CMA equalizer. We introduce two approximate multipliers, strategically integrated into different computational modules to ensure mutual compensation for accuracy. Implementation results demonstrate that the proposed approximate CMA system achieves reductions of 40.10% in area and 18.13% in power consumption compared to the precise system.

articleTitle: A Compact Improved Performance Circularly Polarized Rectenna With Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A compact rectenna working at 5.8 GHz is designed for wireless power transmission (WPT) with circular polarization (CP) and harmonic suppression (HS), achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of over 75%. This design effectively addresses the polarization mismatch problem typically encountered in WPT systems. Additionally, it successfully suppresses the occurrence of second harmonic distortion from the diode, obviating the necessity for a low-pass filter network in the rectifier circuit and improving RF-to-DC conversion efficiency. We use a slot antenna as the receiving element for WPT system, which has dimensions of 25 mm × 25 mm (0.48 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.48 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). This antenna can receive energy at 5.8 GHz which working within the ISM bands. Moreover, a rectifier circuit with high efficiency is proposed, which includes a matching network, a rectifier network, a DC-pass filter, and a 1000 Ω load. At an input power of 10 dBm, the designed rectifier achieves an efficiency of 75% at 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: An Artificial Electromagnetic Metasurface For Special Reflective Reconfigurable Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Reflective surface antenna based on artificial electromagnetic metasurface manifests itself an innovative technical scheme, which involves combining the advantages of reconfigurable antenna arrays to control electromagnetic reflection dynamically and precisely. In this way, the antenna can adapt to different environments and requirements, provide new ideas for the tailoring and regulation of electromagnetic propagation. Here, a reconfigurable metasurface reflective antenna array which center frequency is in the X-band was designed. When the frequency of the incident electromagnetic wave is 10GHz, the phase-frequency response of the adjacent structural units to the electromagnetic wave differs by 36°, forming a uniform distribution of phase gradient from 0° to 360°. The linearly polarized electromagnetic wave incident perpendicular to the AEM is modulated, and anomalous reflections along 45° and -45°at 10GHz for the single- and dual-polarization, respectively.

articleTitle: Software Defined Radio-Based Electromagnetic Environment Interference Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the continuous development of electronic communication services, wireless communication services are increasingly affected by electromagnetic signals from other services and equipment, especially radio frequency interference (RFI).Based on this, this article mainly focuses on environments with or without RFI, using software radio as a means to establish a RFI monitoring system, extract the characteristics of signals in different environments, calculate dynamic thresholds, and use signal analysis based on signal spectrum characteristics to analyze several environments. A certain number of signals exceeding the threshold are extracted and saved and an alarm is issued. The results show that the method and algorithm used in this article to incorporate software radio into the alarm system have obvious alarm success rates for RFI in different environments, which is helpful for interference monitoring and alarm in wireless communication, and provides support methods for the use of radio systems.

articleTitle: EFT Immunity Test and Damage Localization of C-Band Limiters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, the EFT immunity experimental platform of the C-band RF limiter is designed, and then the electromagnetic immunity test and device damage analysis are carried out. When the voltage of the EFT interference source exceeds 900V, the device experiences increased insertion loss. When the interference continues to grow to 1000V, the device is damaged. Failure localization is performed for the failed sample by using electromagnetic emission measurement techniques. By analyzing the emitted electromagnetic field map (EMF), we can conclude that the PIN diodes are more susceptible to damage. The device's performance is improved by disassembling it and replacing the PIN diode, proving that we have accurately located the fault point.

articleTitle: Magnetic Core Inductor-Based Resonator for Magnetic Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Induction coil sensors have been widely used in magnetic sensing and communication. However, the basic working principle of Faraday’s law indicates that only the change of magnetic flux could induce detectable output voltage. Therefore, induction type magnetic sensors could only measure AC magnetic fields. Moreover, the complicate equivalent circuit of the sensor results in complicated frequency dependent response. Here we report resonant frequency modulation by incorporation of capacitance with both serial and parallel connections, resulting in tunable magnetic sensing and communication functions.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Absorber Combining Magnetic Material and Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Metasurfaces have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional stealth technology due to its remarkable ability to freely manipulate electromagnetic waves. Herein, we propose an ultra-wideband absorber combining magnetic materials and metasurfaces. The proposed absorber comprises two layers of carbony1 iron powder (CIP), a metasurface lossy layer and a metal ground. The operation mechanism and bandwidth enhancement are analyzed and discussed in terms of the electromagnetic field and power loss distribution at two frequencies of 0.32 GHz and 18 GHz. This reveals the synergistic effect of metasurface structures and magnetic materials. After optimization, the absorber showed more than 90% absorption effect in the range of 0.22 GHz ~ 18 GHz. Furthermore, the performance of the absorber at different incident angles was evaluated, demonstrating its resilience to angular changes. This design has the potential to be applied in military and stealth technology.

articleTitle: Preliminary study on silicon wafer characterization using quasi-optical resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Different from the standard μ-PCD (microwave photoconductive decay) method in which an antenna is used as a transceiver, this work tries to use a two-port quasi-optical resonator for μ-PCD measurement. One of the popular applications of μ-PCD is measurement of minority carrier lifetime of semiconductor or optoelectronic materials. As a preliminary study, effect of vertical position of material under test (e.g., silicon wafer) inside the resonator is studied here by both simulation and experiments. The obtained results reveal that: 1) for silicon wafers with lower conductivity, the resonant frequency of the quasi-optical resonator changes in a periodical way as the vertical position changes; 2) for silicon wafers with relative higher conductivity, the resonant frequency changes in a monotonous way since the wafer behaves like a good conductor. These preliminary results indicates that the vertical position should be considered for future μ-PCD experiments.

articleTitle: Space targets recognition based on micro-doppler representation in frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The micro-Doppler (m-D) effect arises from additional Doppler frequency modulation induced by the motion characteristics of a radar target. Analyzing the radar signal in the frequency domain enables a comprehensive depiction of the m-D frequency variations demonstrated by the target. This paper proposes an intelligent framework based on the frequency domain to recognize the micro-motion types of space targets with similar structures. Firstly, the image representation based on the frequency domain, including time-frequency spectrograms and cadence velocity diagram (CVD), was analyzed. Next, a recognition framework based on deep learning algorithms was proposed. Finally, an electromagnetic (EM) computation dataset was collected to validate the performance of the proposed recognition framework.

articleTitle: Drivable area detection in off-road for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Drivable area segmentation is a prerequisite for safe passage through off-road environments. However, the majority of existing approaches are related to the segmentation of structured roads, with relatively limited research conducted in off-road environments. In this paper, we propose a segmentation network for better detecting the drivable area in off-road environments. In the neck network, we used ASPP model and the gated Depthwise Inception model (DIM), where the DIM regulates the flow of weight information by integrating the gating mechanism. To evaluate the effectiveness of our network, we selected the ORFD dataset to test it, which collects off-road images in different light conditions and locations. In the experimental section, we compare the behavior of our method with other networks on the ORFD dataset, measured in terms of accuracy, IOU, and speed.

articleTitle: A Fine-Grained Clothing Style Image Segmentation Method Based on DeepLab v3+
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Currently, research on artificial intelligence in the field of clothing production and manufacturing is still lacking. To advance the process of AI in clothing production and manufacturing, it is necessary to solve the problem of fine-grained segmentation of clothing style images to extract useful information. This paper first constructs a new dataset based on clothing structure morphology, manufacturing processes, and functional characteristics—the Clothing Structure Attribute (CSA) Dataset. Then, based on the DeepLab v3+ model, we propose a clothing style image segmentation algorithm named Clothing Structure Attribute DeepLab v3+ (CSA-DeepLab v3+). In this algorithm, we add feature extraction layers to the baseline network architecture, modify the ASPP convolutional kernel structure, and use two attention mechanisms: CBAM and ECA. We also conduct comparative and ablation experiments to verify performance of our model on the dataset presented in this paper providing a new approach for the automation of clothing production and manufacturing.

articleTitle: A Low-power 1-Bit Wideband Reflection-Type Phase Shifter for Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper proposes a 1-bit reflection-type phase shifter (RTPS) in S-band featuring wideband and low power consumption. Different from conventional phase-tuning devices used in reconfigurable metasurface, the RTPS is controlled by flipping a single CMOS switch, which is characterized by a low turn-on current. The effectiveness of this design is verified through simulations and measurements. Measurement results show that, over a relative bandwidth of 40.9% from 1.83 to 2.77 GHz, the phase difference is 180°± 20°and reflection loss is below 1.7 dB. Additionally, the overall power consumption is approximately 0.53 mW, which is much lower than those using PIN diodes. This 1-bit RTPS can be potentially applied in wideband and low-power reconfigurable reflective meta-surfaces.

articleTitle: Arbitrary polarization conversion and phase control using full- parameter AA-phase metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Arbitrary polarization states represent the most comprehensive information of electromagnetic (EM) wave, and variable polarization channels of EM waves can be widely utilized in target detection. Here, a novel strategy is proposed for arbitrary polarization generation and wavefront control with Aharonov-Anandan (AA) and Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phases. Based on theoretical analysis, it is indicated that comprehensive Jones matrices of AA phase and PB phase enable precise and flexible control of polarization. To validate the feasibility of this matrix, two cases are considered. In case I, two orthogonal circularly polarized (CP) channels of a single metaatom are utilized to generate an arbitrary linear polarization (LP) state and to manipulate wavefront by combing aforementioned phases. In case II, co- and cross- polarization amplitude terms are decoupled by employing angular difference of two meta-atoms to manipulate ellipticity angle, while corresponding dual-channel phase difference is utilized to control azimuth angle. Consequently, left- or right-handed CP wave can be converted into arbitrary polarized wave with a controllable wavefront, leveraging its amplitude and phase through both co- and cross-polarized channels. For demonstration and potential applications, two meta-devices were realized, and excellent beam deflection and bifocal focusing at arbitrary polarization under illumination of LP and CP waves verifies our concept. Our strategy sets a solid platform in implementing arbitrarily polarized EM devices.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Wideband Antenna Considered Multiple Input Multiple Output Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A dual-port antenna has been designed, which is applied to the ultra-wideband system, together with consideration of multiple input multiple output function. Each antenna element was constructed as a curved edge trapezoidal structure. To increase the impedance bandwidth, we carved an elliptical hole in the radiation patch, and the E- and U-shaped slots on the ground plane formed a defect ground structure. Experiment results show that the operation frequency of antenna covers from 3 to 28 GHz, with mutual coupling less than -15 dB. These designs are suitable for promoting radar communication systems in the X-band and efficient satellite communication, such as exchanging data between relay satellites and space stations, as well as receiving television signals.

articleTitle: Active Compensation of Reflector Antenna Structural Deformation Based on Deep BP-Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The active reflector is a method used to compensate for the surface deformation of the reflector due to gravity and other factors, which will lead to the degradation of the electromagnetic performance of the antenna. The time-invariant surface deformation of large antenna caused by wind cannot be compensated quickly and effectively. A method based on deep BP neural network (DBPNN) is proposed to quickly obtain the adjustment of active reflector actuators. The mapping relationship between the deformation of the primary reflector and the adjustment of thousands of actuators is established. In order to ensure the unity of data dimension, the relation matrix of the actuators and panels is established. By processing the deformation data of the primary reflector, the deformation and position characteristics of the panels are obtained, and the network parameters are trained by the Adam optimizer. The results show that the proposed method can obtain thousands of actuator adjustments at different elevation angles very quickly under the premise of meeting the accuracy requirements. Compared with the traditional numerical algorithm, this method is suitable for compensating the loss performance at all elevation angles, and the time of calculation is reduced significantly.

articleTitle: A Contactless Temperature Measurement and Identity Recognition Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a system for contactless temperature measurement and identification device by using Arduino and Maix Dock M1W Development Board. The system mainly consists of a temperature measurement module and an identity recognition module. The temperature measurement module transmits the collected temperature data to the identity recognition module and the display after temperature compensation, and the identity recognition module carries out identity verification through the collected face information, and the combination of the two can realize the functions of epidemic prevention and control, company attendance, and so on. The device can effectively monitor the health of employees and has good prospects for practical application.

articleTitle: Closed-form Equation for Passive Intermodulation of Microstrip Line due to Resistivity Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Passive intermodulation (PIM) is one of the harmful interferences in the communication systems. In microstrip circuits, multiple factors can affect the PIM product including the conductor and dielectric materials, the strip dimension and structure et.al. In this paper, the resistive nonlinear effect on the PIM phenomenon for the microstrip line was analyzed. The resistivity nonlinearity coefficient was obtained by solving the heat conduction equation, by which the expression for the distributed PIM signal excitation source was derived, and the closed form PIM equation for uniform microstrip line was obtained eventually. Using the derived equations, the effect of the material properties and the dimension on the PIM product for uniform microstrip line due to conductor resistivity nonlinearity can be quantitatively calculated. The analytical PIM model will contribute to investigation of the PIM phenomenon in more complex microstrip circuits.

articleTitle: Broadband extreme scattering reduction in a graphene-based transparent and flexible metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Absorbers are commonly employed for the suppression of scattering field; however, a trade-off exists between the magnitude of scattering reduction and the bandwidth. Consequently, a design criterion of achieving a 90% suppression effect is generally adopted. Striving for higher scattering reduction would inevitably lead to a significant decrease in absorber bandwidth, necessitating the development of a new mechanism to achieve wideband and efficient scattering suppression. This study introduces an innovative graphene-assisted transparent and flexible metasurface that successfully achieves a significant reduction in radar cross-section (RCS) across a wide frequency range through the implementation of multilayer graphene stacking and doping techniques. The design achieves remarkable scattering suppression of over 20 dB from 10.3 GHz to 19.2 GHz by leveraging both phase cancellation and absorption mechanisms. Moreover, the insensitivity of the metasurface to large angle incidence is further confirmed through simulation analysis. This research presents a novel and effective design strategy towards realising flawless electromagnetic stealth.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Polarization Shared Aperture Antenna Based on Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A dual polarization shared aperture array antenna combining frequency selective surface (FSS) structure and cross dipole antenna is proposed in this paper. By loading FSS structures on low-frequency antenna arrays, it is possible to achieve transmission of the 3.3-3.8 GHz bandwidth of the high-frequency array, the FSS structure has a wide bandwidth and does not affect the performance of the low-frequency antenna itself. The shared aperture array antenna designed based on this structure has a wide bandwidth, high gain, and good performance. The array antenna has a low-frequency bandwidth of 1.7-2.7GHz, a maximum gain of 10dBi, a high-frequency bandwidth of 3.3-3.8GHz, and a maximum gain of 10dBi.

articleTitle: Broadband Orthomode Transducer Based on the Boifot Junction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This letter proposes a high-performance wideband double-ridged waveguide orthomode transducer (OMT) designed for the V-band, covering the 40-60 GHz frequency band. The OMT design incorporates a square waveguide as the common port, connecting to two distinct isolated standard rectangular waveguide ports. Vertical polarization (VP) is directly coupled to the standard rectangular waveguide ports via an E-plane bend, while horizontal polarization (HP) is split into two sides and then combined using a Y-combiner. The OMT is composed of three main components, a Boifot junction, an E-plane bend, and a Y-shaped combiner. Each of these has been subjected to rigorous full-wave simulations to optimize the design efficiency. The proposed boifot OMT exhibits a simulated return loss of less than -20 dB and an isolation surpassing 120 dB within the 40-60 GHz bandwidth. After fabrication of prototypes, several tests validate the high-performance within the specified frequency range.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Noncontact Measurement of Mechanical Vibration by Near-field Microwave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this work, noncontact measurement of mechanical vibration is studied with near-field microwave method. Two kinds of microwave sensors are used: complimentary split ring resonator (CSRR) and various planar antennas. For the former sensor, a vibration test platform is used to simulate a vibrating object and a vector network analyzer (VNA) is used to measure the time dependent |S21| of the CSRR. For the latter sensor, a fork with resonance frequency of 129 Hz is used as vibration object. A home-made system is used to measure the time dependent return loss of the antenna sensors. Both methods obtain periodical waveforms with periodicity corresponding to the predefined vibration frequency. Thus, preliminary results verify that the near-field microwave method is suitable for noncontact measurement of mechanical vibration.

articleTitle: A Novel Power Divider With Tunable Power Ratios and Reconfigurable Output Phase Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this letter, a novel power divider with a wide tunable range of power ratios and reconfigurable output phase differences is proposed. The tunable power ratio is implemented by replacing the branch transmission line of the conventional Gysel power divider. The branch transmission line equivalent circuit consists of three short-circuited varactors cascaded through two sections of transmission lines. Moreover, by selecting appropriate capacitances of the varactors, the proposed novel power divider can operate either in an in-phase mode or out-of-phase mode. Finally, the electromagnetic (EM) simulation of six examples was conducted and one experimental circuit of the proposed novel power divider was fabricated. The simulation and measurement results verified the feasibility of the proposed novel power divider.

articleTitle: Research on a Fiber Optic Magnetic Field Sensor Based on Fuze Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: We propose a new effective method for magnetic sensors by incorporating quantum nanosensors into the microstructure on the fiber end face. Specifically, we fabricated polymer micro tip probes containing nanodiamonds using photo induced self-writing waveguide technology. The shape of the microtips can be modulated by the curing parameters and their corresponding influence on embedded optical defects in nanodiamonds has been numerically and experimentally investigated. Based on this waveguide coupled NV fluorescence, we have found a new method for magnetic field measurement. Considering its easy to manufacture and flexible structure, it can be applied on small platforms such as fuze.

articleTitle: An Ultralow-Profile Folded Transmitarray Antenna with Low RCS Based on Metasurface and Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel linearly polarized folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) with low radar cross-section (RCS) and ultralow profile. It is engineered by combining a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) for absorbing out-of-band linearly polarized electromagnetic (EM) waves, a transmission and reflection (T-R) metasurface for independent manipulation of x- and y-polarized incident waves, a polarization conversion (PC) metasurface and a horn antenna for feeding. The antenna operates in two distinct radiation and scatting modes. In radiation mode, the spherical electromagnetic (EM) wave generated by the feed horn is transformed into a high-gain pencil-shaped beam.
