The peak gain of 22.9 dBi at 14.2 GHz and 1-dB gain bandwidth of 5% are obtained. Significantly, the incorporation of triple phase compensations via both T-R and PC metasurfaces further reduces the antenna profile to merely 1/7 of its initial focal length. In scatting mode, in-band RCS reduction is realized through antenna matching and EM scattering effect of the T-R metasurface. Furthermore, a 10-dB out-of-band RCS reduction is achieved within 5.5-12.6 GHz under x and y-polarized incident waves relying on FSR.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Imaging Performance of the Mouth-shape Sparse MIMO Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the development of autonomous driving technology, driving safety has become the most concerned issue for the public. We have previously proposed a novel sparse multiple input multiple output (MIMO) four-dimensional (4D) millimeter wave antenna array with a mouth-shape arrangement. In this paper, we propose an improved Four-dimensional fast Fourier (4D-FFT) imaging algorithm through simplifying the steering snapshot matrix. Then, we have simulated and analyzed the imaging performance of the mouth-shape sparse MIMO array through the improved imaging algorithm. The results show that the proposed imaging algorithm has lower complexity, better detection effect, and has application potential in 4D automotive millimeter wave radar.

articleTitle: A Space-Time Modulated Metasurface Encoding Scheme for Orbital Angular Momentum Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Tackling the issue of separating harmonics in conventional space-time digital metasurfaces, this paper proposes a method for achieving harmonic decoupling through rigorous mathematical derivation. Building upon this approach, a encoding scheme for orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing is designed, capable of generating electromagnetic waves with a topological charge of +1 at the fundamental frequency, as well as electromagnetic waves with a topological charge of +2 at the +1st harmonic.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Maneuver Detection and Motion Mode Recognition Based on Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Traditional bearing-only maneuver detection methods for underwater targets often struggle with distinguishing the specific maneuver mode, are susceptible to observation noise, and show limited accuracy for subtle maneuvers. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes a method for underwater target maneuver detection and motion mode recognition based on a bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) classification neural network. By establishing the nonlinear mapping relationship between bearing and range observations and the motion mode of the target, this method can recognize uniform linear motion and three kinds of maneuver: heading change, velocity change, and a combination of both heading and velocity changes. Then maneuver detection is further realized by analyzing the classification results of the target motion mode. As demonstrated by simulation results, this method maintains high accuracy in maneuver detection and motion mode recognition, even under significant observational noise or when faced with a subtle maneuver.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Multiplexing Metasurface Logic Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a polarization-multiplexing single-layer metasurface logic operator that enables independent logic operations under the illumination of different linearly polarized waves. A meta-atom capable of independently manipulating orthogonal linear polarization states is designed to operate as a polarization-multiplexing neuron. Furthermore, the proposed metasurface can serve as different hidden layers in these two polarization channels, achieving a total of ten distinct logic operations. The simulation results are in well agreement with the design targets, achieving a high accuracy of 100%. This polarization-multiplexing strategy can further enhance the channel capacity of optical computing and is expected to facilitate its application in all- optical computers, intelligent computing, and other fields.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Printed Antenna Design for Bluetooth and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study presents the fabrication process of a printed antenna on a FR-4 substrate with accurate measurements of 25×37×1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna design, known for its simplicity, has four semicircles with four small square patches at each end. In addition, it includes two rectangular patches that are fitted with pin diode switches in order to enable the ability to operate in two different frequency bands. The antenna's ground has a carefully placed opening. The antenna being examined demonstrates resonance at both the frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, with reflection coefficients of -19.6 dB and -16.5 dB correspondingly. The VSWR for both working frequencies is below 2, satisfying the requirements of Bluetooth and WLAN applications. The tiny size and creative design elements of this antenna allow for versatility and adaptation in many wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of an Airport Baggage Soft and Hard Bag Recognition Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In response to the need to distinguish between soft and hard baggage at airports, a soft and hard baggage recognition device and method based on depth cameras and a classification recognition model is proposed. The device uses a pressure sensing module to apply pressure to the baggage and obtain feedback stress. Simultaneously, dual depth cameras capture RGB images and point cloud images of the concave areas. The information collected from the dual cameras is stitched together using point cloud registration methods. A classification recognition model is used to output the softness or hardness level of the luggage. In addition, a similarity algorithm is used to pre-process the collected data and reduce the computational load of the classification recognition model, the device has also been experimentally verified to have high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the Improved Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm for 3D Fitting of Object Scattering Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The aim of this study is to optimize the arrangement of corner reflector arrays using an improved Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm to fit the scattering characteristics of target objects. Corner reflectors, as a classic maritime passive jamming device, have an internal geometric structure that maximizes the capture and reflection of radar waves, thereby achieving a larger radar cross-section (RCS). This paper employs both the original and improved GWO algorithms to optimize the corner reflector arrays. A scattering center synthesis algorithm is used to rapidly fit the RCS of the corner reflector arrays to simulate the scattering characteristics of target objects.Under various elevation and azimuth angles, the study optimizes the number, spacing, size, azimuth, and elevation angles of the corner reflectors within the array to achieve the optimal arrangement. The results indicate that the improved GWO algorithm provides a better fit for the scattering characteristics of objects compared to the original GWO algorithm.

articleTitle: Parallelization Design and Evaluation of MT19937 Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A type of linear feedback shift register random number generator is MT19937. To implement MT19937 in parallel on FPGA, a mixed method is utilized in this paper, and empirical tests are conducted on both serial and parallel random number sequences ranging from 32 to 2048. The results reveal excellent randomness in the sequences generated by the parallel MT19937 system. In this paper, the parallel MT19937 system implemented achieves a throughput of 716.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">^</sup>932-bit random numbers per second, surpassing the throughput of the 624-port parallel MT19937 system by 6 times.

articleTitle: Center-Fed Dual-band Dual-Sense Wide Axial-Ratio Beamwidth Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In global satellite navigation systems, a wide axial-ratio beamwidth is generally required to improve the signal coverage of the wireless system. In this paper, a circularly polarized antenna fed with a central coaxial probe is designed, which has circular slits etched on the two-layer patch, and the antenna generates directional radiation when fed at the centre of the patch. After introducing perturbation structures such as branch and tangent, the far-field orthogonal electric field of the antenna has equal amplitude and a phase difference of 90° over a wide-angle range, and a wide-axis-ratio beam is realised by the positive-negative hybrid perturbation. As the central feed ensures the stability of the antenna phase centre, the axial ratio beamwidth is further increased. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 6.4% (1.47-1.57 GHz) and 3.2% (1.81-1.87 GHz). The axial ratio bandwidths are 1.3% (1.54-1.57 GHz) and 1.1% (1.85-1.87 GHz). The axial beamwidths are 188°/185° and 164 /188° for the two main planes at low and high frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarization Ultra-Wideband Frequency Selective Surface Based On External Dielectric Loading At Large Angle of Incidence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarization ultra-wideband frequency selective surface based on external dielectric loading is designed. The structure consists of three layers of metal patch and two layers of dielectric substrate. Impedance matching between FSS and free space is achieved by the method of external dielectric loading. The results show that the designed structure can achieve the characteristics of dual-polarization, ultra-wideband and in-band flatness at 75-80° range incidence. The relative bandwidth can reach 59.45% under TM polarization and 77.68% under TE polarization. By using the method of external dielectric loading, the filtering characteristics at large angle of incidence are improved.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Game Analysis of the Impact of Digital Merger and Acquisition on the Choice of Radical Innovation Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper constructs an evolutionary game model of digital M&A on the choice of radical innovation mode of enterprises, and analyzes the impact of digital M&A on the radical innovation of enterprises. This paper theoretically explores the impact of digital M&A on radical innovation and its mechanism. The results show that the possibility of radical innovation is higher for firms that engage in digital M&A than for those that do not, that is, digital M&A will promote radical innovation.

articleTitle: A Salient Feature-guided Network Using a Two-stage Transfer Learning Strategy for Few-Shot Aircraft Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Deep learning methods have shown promising potential in target detection, which typically require large amounts of annotated data. However, it is challenging to obtain substantial volumes of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images due to high acquisition costs and time-consuming annotation processes. Moreover, aircrafts in SAR images are often discrete and variable, while the complex scattering mechanisms between targets and background further complicate detection. High-precision target detection with sparse training samples has become one of the bottlenecks that restricts the improvement of detection performance. In this paper, a Salient Feature-guided Network using a two-stage Transfer Learning strategy (SFN-TL) is proposed for few-shot aircraft detection in SAR images. Especially, a Salient Feature Enhancement Module (SFEM) is proposed to improve feature extraction ability with sparse training samples, which is composed of an auxiliary branch using a generator network. Additionally, the issue of sparse target feature representation in SAR images is addressed by introducing a Context-aware Feature Fusion Module (CFFM). Experiments conducted on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method has achieved a novel class Average Precision (nAP) of 20.2%, 40.1%, and 66.4% with 5, 10, and 30 training images per novel class, respectively.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Structures of a kind of Equilibrium Networks in a Cournot Oligopoly
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper investigates how firms establish ties with other firms in a Cournot oligopoly market, and we use a two-stage game model to study the equilibrium network characteristics of Cournot markets. The conclusion is that the final equilibrium network topology is determined by three variables: connection cost, total number of enterprises and group size. Compared with Billand and Bravard (2004), our conclusion relaxes the equilibrium conditions and considers more situations.

articleTitle: Two Wheeled Self Balancing Vehicle Based on Wireless Remote Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A design scheme of a two wheeled self balancing vehicle with wireless remote control is proposed. STC8G2K64S4 is used as the main controller of the system, the angle and acceleration information of the vehicle is obtained by gyroscope and accelerometer, the actual angle of the vehicle is fused by using complementary filtering algorithm, and after being processed by PID algorithm, the microcontroller outputs a PWM control signal to control the motor of the vehicle, so as to make the vehicle keep balance. The experimental results show that the design scheme can keep the vehicle upright and has a certain anti-jamming ability, and can control the motion state of the vehicle in real time through the handheld remote control, stable forward, backward and steering.

articleTitle: Design of a Potter Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Within this paper, a square waveguide Potter horn antenna is designed to excite the higher order modes in the form of a step. The antenna consists of a third-order step and a horn. The higher order modes generated by the step suppress the side lobe in the E-plane, and then the phase between the TE and TM modes is controlled by the length of the horn to realize the rotationally symmetric radiation patterns at apertures. The simulation results show that the antenna has excellent symmetry in the E-plane and H-plane of the radiation patterns in the range of 22-29 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 27.5%. Its side lobe level is less than -20 dB and the peak gain in band is 17.4 dBi.

articleTitle: A Series-fed Frequency-scanning Antenna for UAV's Obstacle Avoidance Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the operational maneuvers of multirotor drones, a common phenomenon encountered is the tendency for the drone's front end to tilt downwards. This inclination hampers the effectiveness of existing obstacle avoidance technologies in monitoring obstructions directly ahead. To address the obstacle avoidance needs during maneuverable flight of multirotor drones, this study proposes a design based on a MIMO series-fed frequency scanning antenna. This design ensures the drone's capability to detect frontal obstacles in any flight attitude, overcoming the issues of stalling in low-altitude flights and collisions with billboards or power lines during high-speed flights due to radar scanning towards the ground at an angle. The designed antenna, with a substrate dimension of 29.09 mm by 12.73 mm and operating in the frequency range of 60 GHz to 64 GHz, achieves a scanning angle range of 0° to 20° within a 4 GHz bandwidth, demonstrating the antenna's high-resolution characteristics. Throughout the entire operating bandwidth, the antenna's S11 parameter remains below -10dB, with an average sidelobe level below -9.96 dB, and a maximum gain reaching 15.3 dBi. These parameters indicate the superior performance of the designed frequency scanning antenna.

articleTitle: Proportionation Enpowered Data-Reusing Ekblom Algorithm for Signal Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: An enhanced signal enhancement algorithm termed as proportionation enpowered data-reusing Ekblom (PEDRE) is constructed, which integrates the Ekblom norm, proportional methods, and affine projection techniques to form an innovative cost function. The cost function utilizes historical errors to accelerate the convergence rate of colored input signals. Simulation results indicate that, compared to other similar algorithms, the PEDRE algorithm exhibits superior performance.

articleTitle: Recognition and Classification of Radar Targets Base on Multiple Features of High-Resolution Range Profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: High-resolution range profiles contain important scattering and structural features of targets and are often used for radar target recognition and classification. Based on the characteristics of the high-resolution range profiles, neural networks and feature-based machine learning could be used as classifiers for radar target classification. The accuracy of feature-based machine learning depends on the quality of the extracted features, while the recognition accuracy based on neural networks depends on the structure of neural networks. This article proposes a set of features suitable for target identification, which has low dimensionality, real-time performance, and without translation sensitivity and amplitude sensitivity. Using features proposed, an intelligent target recognition classifier based on ground target simulation is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Design for an Ultra-Wideband Antenna with Reconfigurable Band-Notch Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In order to suppress interference from narrowband systems such as WiMAX and WLAN within the Ultra-wideband (UWB) frequency range, this article presents a notch UWB antenna that effectively mitigates the interference from the narrowband in the 3-12 GHz frequency range, thereby further improving the utilization efficiency of the UWB spectrum. The radiation patch of the antenna consists of a cut circular patch and two U-shaped slots on the radiation patch introduce two notches. The reconfigurable characteristics of the band-notch are realized by the PIN diodes, achieving three reconfigurable working states. The antenna is printed on an FR-4 substrate with dimensions of 20 x18 x1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the antenna structure is compact. The simulation results show that it has good radiation performance throughout the entire operating frequency band, with a steady gain between 1-5dBi. The antenna has an excellent application scene and can be used for UWB applications that suppress narrowband.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband tightly coupled circular array antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a wideband omnidirectional dipole circular array antenna. The antenna consists of eight curved butterfly dipoles, which utilize the coupling between units to achieve a wideband antenna frequency range. Two impedance matching layers are placed above the dipoles to further increase the overall bandwidth of the array. Due to the strong mutual coupling and impedance matching layers, the proposed omnidirectional antenna exhibits a wide operating frequency band. Additionally, the wideband feeding network based on Chebyshev impedance matching is optimized through differential evolution algorithm simulation. As a result, this antenna has an operating bandwidth of 2.9 GHz–10 GHz and good omnidirectional performance over the bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Framework for Digital Transformation in the Era of Digital Economy: A New Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Nowadays, with the digital transformation of the industrial economy, numerous related concepts emerged from various research purposes and application scenarios have caused great confusion for the public, scientific research, enterprise management, and national policy-making. Based on the initial origin of these concepts — scientific and technological progress, this article develops a new conceptual framework: technological progress → productivity growth → improvement in information transmission → social development. By integrating all related concepts under a unified cognitive logic, the article aims to lay a theoretical foundation for the scientific development of research in this field.

articleTitle: Research on multidimensional reconstruction security billing strategy in cloud native scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper proposes a heterogeneous multi-objective secure billing method based on microservices gateway domain to address the data security issues in transaction security billing mechanisms in the financial and pan financial industries. The monitoring module of Service Mesh is integrated, adapted to the monitoring business system, and the semantic parameters of Service Mesh are flexibly configured. In the data flow preprocessing stage, a custom encryption module is used to encrypt and preset user attributes. At the same time, business indicators are defined, a multi-objective model is constructed, algorithm logic is reconstructed, and the delay and traffic of the entire link are optimized. Furthermore, real-time security quantification standards based on time-series monitoring and multithreading are further implemented.

articleTitle: Design of Performance Testing Method for Track Circuit Products Based on PXI Universal Bus Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In response to the requirements for safety, reliability verification and evaluation of track circuit products, this plan adopts a combination of a universal host control part and equipment operation carrier to test the safety and reliability of track circuit products. This article starts with the design of system hardware and software, and elaborates on the structure and implementation method of the scheme. The scheme has a testing platform technology that supports fault excitation and comprehensive physical environment simulation. Through the testing management platform, the combined excitation and judgment of various testing conditions for track circuit products are achieved, supporting performance testing of different track circuit products.

articleTitle: Novel Integrated Ka-Band Amplitude Limiting Low Noise Amplifier Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Low noise amplifier is a key component of RF receiver front-end. An amplitude limiting low noise amplifier (LNA) based on 0.09 μm GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) technology is designed and implemented in this paper. The amplitude limiting LNA adopts an integrated design and works at frequencies of 34 ~ 37 GHz. The actual measurement results show that the proposed amplitude limiting LNA has a gain of over 23 dB in the working band. Its input and output voltage standing–wave ratio (VSWR) is less than 1.6 and has a noise figure (NF) below 4.2 dB. It can withstand a peak pulse power of 10 W, with a pulse width of 50 µs, a duty cycle of 10%. It has the advantages of broadband, low noise, high power tolerance and small size.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Folded Transmitarray Antenna With Linearly Polarized Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A low-profile, high-gain, wideband circularly polarized folded transmitarray antenna (CPFTA) is proposed, and a polarization-selective linear-to-circular polarization (LP-CP) conversion element is introduced. The CPFTA consists of a linearly polarized (LP) magnetoelectric dipole antenna and a circularly polarized (CP) helical patch antenna. The CPFTA demonstrates excellent performance with a 3dB gain bandwidth of 29.5% and a 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 40.9%.

articleTitle: A Broadband Low-RCS Co-polarized Antenna Array Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, a low-scattering antenna array based on hybrid absorption metasurfaces is proposed. The absorption metasurface consists of a single layer of indium tin oxide (ITO) film and several layers of metal sheets, which are stacked to produce a broadband absorbing effect. Through slot coupling, this hybrid absorption metasurface is excited and forms an antenna array with co-polarized radiation. By adjusting the arrangement of the metal sheets, a high reflective frequency band is reserved at the radiation frequency of the antenna array to ensure the radiation efficiency of the antenna array. The proposed antenna array has the characteristics of co-polarization radiation at 5~6 GHz and low scattering at 2~4.5 GHz and 7.5~11.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Device-free Human Activity Recognition Based on CSI Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In recent years, device-free wireless location and action recognition have increasingly become emerging technology. It does not require carrying any equipment while protects personal privacy, which can enable intelligent perception of human body through shielding effect of the target in wireless network. Since human body has a significant reflection effect on wireless signals, it is possible to estimate a person's position and activities by monitoring changes in the signals. Since wireless signals do not contain annotation information, supervised learning cannot be directly performed on the collected channel state information (CSI). Therefore, we propose a device-free human activity recognition scheme based on CSI characteristic, where we create category labels through One-Hot encoding. Specifically, the CSI amplitude matrix and phase matrix of wireless signals are directly processed to reduce calculation errors and improve classification accuracy. Finally, through experimental comparison, the effectiveness of proposed method in terms of recognition accuracy is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Self-interference Canceller Design Based on Knowledge-driven Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) technology, which enables signal simultaneous transmission and receptions in the same frequency band, has been recognized as a key technology in wireless networks. However, self-interference (SI) is a significant problem that hinders its practical application, and effective SI cancellation techniques should be employed. Traditionally, SI uses a polynomial model with a nonlinear adaptive learning algorithm for reconstruction and cancellation, but the number of parameters that need to be estimated is large and difficult to achieve. Therefore, in order to obtain cancellation algorithms with fewer parameters and low complexity, neural network tools have been noticed. In this paper, we propose a knowledge-driven neural network canceller structure, which significantly reduces the computational complexity compared with the polynomial model. Experimental results show that the proposed structure can reduce the number of real addition and multiplication calculations by about 40-60 and 0-40% while achieving similar nonlinear cancellation performance.

articleTitle: Research on Measurement Method for Secondary Electron Emission Coefficient of Aerospace Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: When charged particles incident on the material surface, they will excite secondary electrons and backscattered electrons from the material surface. For low conductivity dielectric materials, the emission of secondary electrons is one of the important mechanisms that cause the surface charging of the material. As the spacecraft surface contains materials with different secondary electron emission coefficients, there is a risk of electrostatic discharge between materials as a result of differential charging, so it is necessary to study the relationship between secondary electron emission and spacecraft surface charging. This paper introduces a measurement method of secondary electron emission coefficient of dielectric materials, using pulsed electron beam together with ultraviolet lamp to neutralize the charged surface during the measurement, and combines the results of secondary electron emission coefficient of typical aerospace materials (Gold, Aluminum, Single-sided Aluminum Plated Kapton™, Double-sided Aluminum Plated F46, Carburized Kapton™, and Polyester Film) to study the impact of secondary electron emission on the surface charging level of spacecraft, laying the foundation for carrying out spacecraft electrostatic protection.

articleTitle: An ADMM Approache for PAPR Reduction in Multi-Receiver MISO-OFDM Fuze
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper propose a low-complexity solution for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction in multi-receiver MISO-OFDM fuze based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Specifically, we study on an optimization problem aimed at minimizing the total transmit power subject to constructive interference (CI) realization and per-antenna PAPR restriction. To obtain the approximate optimal solution efficiently, a corresponding low-complexity ADMM algorithm is derived. Then we show that, in the proposed ADMM algorithm, the computational complexity in each iteration is roughly on the order of $\mathbb{O}\left({K{N^3} + KMN}\right)$, where K, M, N are the number of receivers, transmit antennas and subcarriers respectively. Numerical results validate that the proposed low-complexity algorithm achieves enhanced performance over the existing methods in terms of total transmit power, PAPR and computation complexity.

articleTitle: Trial Study on Sea Clutter Identification and Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Detecting target in sea clutter is challengeable because sea clutter is nonstationary and hardly modeled by the statistical models. In this paper, we present a distribution-free method of sea clutter identification and target detection, i.e., echoes of radar scanning the monitored sea area, which are grouped into echo matrices corresponding to every scanning azimuth, are taken as a whole object. Each echo matrix is transformed into Range Doppler (RD) matrix S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> with windowed FFT. A submatrix of target features is constructed by applying the approaches of peak finding, subtractive clustering and fuzzy c-means clustering on S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>. The feature matrix T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is formed by cascading the feature submatrices. We again apply the subtractive clustering on T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> to estimate the number of clusters k, and then use the k-means clustering to classify the feature matrix T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> into k clusters. The largest cluster is considered as sea clutter features, and others are target features. By finding the nearest neighbors of centroid matrix of k-means clustering, the targets in sea clutter are detected. The proposed method is validated via the measured sea clutter datasets. The results of trial studies prove the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Joint User Activity Detection and Channel Estimation for Grant-Free Temporal-Correlated Random Access in LEO Satellite Based IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite communication has been regarded as a promising solution for providing ubiquitous Internet of Things (IoT) services, due to its capability of global seamless coverage. In this paper, we focus on resolving the joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) problem for realizing the efficient grant-free random access in LEO satellite based IoT. According to the sporadic user traffic and the temporal correlations over consecutive frames, we formulate the JADCE problem as a dynamic compressive sensing problem. Especially, a probabilistic model is built to represent both the time variation of user activities and the evolution of channel coefficients by steady Markov processes. Furthermore, we develop a correlated information aided hybrid generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) algorithm to solve this problem, which utilizes the GAMP algorithm for detecting active users and estimating channels, and further employs the standard message passing algorithm to update user activity likelihood and channel coefficients. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce user activity detection errors and improve channel estimation performance as compared to the existing benchmark algorithms.

Author Keywords: joint activity detection and channel estimation

articleTitle: Widely Linear Beamforming via Interpolated Difference-Sum Co-Array in Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel widely linear beamforming via interpolated difference-sum co-array (WLB-IDSCA) method in satellite communications. We leverage the augmented covariance matrix of coprime array non-circular signals to generate the difference-sum co-array (DSCA). A novel IDSCA is presented to fully exploit the information within DSCA. A problem of minimizing atomic norm is formed, providing a solution to recover the non-circular signals of IDSCA. Interestingly, the covariance matrix of IDSCA non-circular signals has Toeplitz structure so that we can localize them from the peaks of spatial spectrum. A new joint covariance and pseudo covariance matrices optimization problem is formulated to acquire the powers of noncircular signals. By reconstructing the augmented interference-plus-noise covariance matrix, the augmented weight vector can be computed. Numerical experiments verify that the proposed WLB-IDSCA method can be applicable to coprime array noncircular signals.

articleTitle: A Q-Learning-Based Load Balancing Routing Protocol for Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The problem of load imbalance in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) can cause some nodes to overload, resulting in a decrease in the performance of the entire system. This paper proposes a Q-learning-based load balancing routing (QLBR) protocol. QLBR introduces a load balancing mechanism into the Q-learning-based routing protocols, which predicts the load situation based on the forwarding count of nodes to candidate forwarding nodes, thereby better distributing routing load evenly in the network. By balancing the load, QLBR reduces the risk of node failures caused by overuse and improves the overall efficiency and reliability of data transmission in UWSNs. Simulation results demonstrate that QLBR significantly enhances the transmission efficiency of data packet and performance well in terms of end-to-end delay and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Robust Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control for Uncertain Linear Parameter-Varying Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A novel robust composite event-triggered model predictive control method is proposed for linear parameter-varying systems. The proposed controller integrates the nominal and robust compensation elements for optimal control in terms of the error between the observer state and the nominal. Only when the output of the observer violates the measurement error condition, the controller can be updated during the recalculation process of the optimal problem. The activation strategy effectively reduces the communication and computational burden, and the control design framework combines uncertainties and bounded disturbances into a robust invariant set to guarantee system stability. Finally, the viability of the method is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning for Camouflaged Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) is a challenging problem due to the difficulty of distinguishing objects that blend seamlessly into their surroundings. Traditional methods often struggle in complex environments. In this study, we introduce SSPNet, a novel approach that leverages self-supervised learning to enhance COD by pre-training a Transformer-based neural network. SSPNet is designed to learn robust feature representations without extensive labeled data, facilitating the generation of meaningful embeddings for accurately detecting objects in intricate scenes. We conducted comprehensive experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets: CHAMELEON, CAMO, and COD10K. Rigorous testing and ablation studies demonstrate that SSPNet significantly reduces missed detections and offers superior performance in detecting local details when compared to various state-of-the-art COD methods. Our findings underscore the transformative potential of self-supervised learning in enhancing both the accuracy and efficiency of camouflaged object detection (COD).

articleTitle: A Real-Valued Off-Grid DOA Estimator Via Sparse Bayesian Learning Exploiting Wishart prior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: For sparse Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation problems, sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) has achieved excellent performance. As a combination of observation and priors, SBL-based methods exploit priors as regularization constraint to promote sparsity. Unfortunately, canonical Gaussian priors cannot enhance sparsity well, while hierarchical priors show satisfactory sparsity performance. However, most developed methods based on hierarchical priors use Gamma priors, which cannot model the correlation between different variables to be solved and cannot promote sparsity performance to a high level. On this basis, the paper uses Wishart prior to model the correlation and enhance sparsity further, yielding a novel Bayesian framework. Based on the framework, we rigorously deduce the corresponding SBL iterative algorithm by an expectation-maximization (EM) procedure. Moreover, to avoid the unrobust complex operations and intractable off-grid gaps, a real-valued transformation is adopted and the off-grid compensation is completed. Extensive simulations are presented to illustrate the superiority of the proposed method beyond state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: An Approach to Enhance the Efficiency of RISC-V Verification Using Intelligent Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: As the complexity and scale of processor design increases, the significance of verification in the chip design process also expands. Nevertheless, conventional UVM verification techniques are encountering difficulties in meeting the increasing requirements, leading to extended processing durations, decreased coverage, and possible neglect of design flaws. This work focused on addressing these challenges by specifically examining RISC-V verification and implementing genetic algorithms to enhance the production of test vectors within the current UVM verification environment. Experiments have shown that this approach outperforms limited random verification in terms of speed in achieving the specified coverage targets. Our verification framework successfully achieves the objective coverage while reducing the utilization of test vectors by approximately 30.76%, compared to the random testing verification approach. Hence, this approach has the potential to enhance the efficiency of verification and conserve resources, thus mitigating the aforementioned issues.

articleTitle: A Measuring Circuit for Small Values of Capacitance Based on Capacitance-to-phase Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Existing capacitance-measuring instruments can only reach the range level of a micro-farad; for smaller capacitors, they often fall short of the range requirement. This study provides a method for detecting pill capsule products whose contents are out-of-weight-specifications. A difference in the weight of the capsule stuffing leads to a difference in the capacitance of the capsule. However, the capacitance of a capsule tends to be small, ranging from a few to tens of picofarads, which cannot be measured by general measuring instruments. Based on this fact, this study designs a capacitance-to-phase conversion circuit with a capacitance sensor, consisting of a cylindrical hollow pipe and two half-cylindrical copper electrodes. When the measured capsule passes through the pipe, the capacitance sensor captures its capacitance which is converted into a series of output pulses by the measuring circuit. The pulse width of these pulses represents the difference between the tested capsule and standard reference capacitance. The feasibility of the circuit was verified using LTSpice simulation. The test results show that this design can convert the capacitance value into pulses with a resolution of 7.6us/1pF. The relative error between the pulse width read by the microcontroller and that measured by the oscilloscope is less than 5%.

articleTitle: Two-Stage High Precision Positioning for mm-Wave OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-stage sensing-assisted high-precision positioning scheme utilizing ambient millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signals, assuming known ambient channels to perform positioning of the Intelligent Reflecting Unit (RIU) attached to the target. Initially, the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm is utilized for coarse positioning of the target. Subsequently, precision estimation of the angles of arrival (AOA) and departure (DOA) is achieved through beam-domain received signals utilizing the Simultaneous Weighting Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (SWOMP) algorithm. Finally, simulation results validate that the proposed positioning scheme achieves millimeter-level accuracy. In the precision angle estimation stage, high-precision positioning is accomplished even with a small number of subcarrier pilot signals, thereby reducing pilot overhead. Compared to the initial positioning phase, the pilot overhead of subcarriers is reduced to 25%.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Distributed Strain Sensor Based on φ-OTDR with Ultraweak Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A distributed sensing system was proposed for quantitative of strain measurement based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (φ-OTDR) , The coherent detection principle and I/Q demodulation method are adopted to demodulate the distributed strain. Compared with the traditional φ-OTDR system, this scheme uses ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating (UWFBG) to enhance the reflective Rayleigh scattering signal, which can effectively improve the signal-to-noise ratio. In addition, a polarizer is added to reduce the impact of polarization fading. Using PZT as a strain sensor, the position and phase of the strain signal are successfully demodulated by φ-OTDR. The experiment results show that the demodulated phase difference has a linear response to the strain generated by PZT. Due to the enhanced reflective signal by UWFBG, a high strain sensitivity of 2.11 rad/nε was obtained. This scheme has the advantages of low cost, simple sensing structure, no need for amplifiers, and high sensitivity.

articleTitle: An Iterative Active Constellation Expansion Method for PAPR Reduction in DZT-OTFS System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: DZT-OTFS modulation system based on the discrete Zak transform (DZT) can have lower implementation complexity than the conventional OTFS modulation system that utilizes the two-step approach. However, the DZT-OTFS system will have a higher peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in the case of a large number of Doppler bins. Currently, there are many probability-based methods that can improve the PAPR performance of OTFS systems without sacrificing bit error performance, but few of them address the case where the system has a higher number of Doppler bins. To address this problem, the paper introduces the Iterative Active Constellation Expansion (ACE) method and applies it to the DZT-OTFS system for the first time. By extending specific constellation points to predefined regions, the PAPR of the DZT-OTFS system can be significantly reduced under high Doppler bins without increasing the bit error rate or sending any side information to the receiving end, which is needed in some probabilistic algorithms. Additionally, this method can have lower computational complexity than traditional probabilistic algorithms. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms existing probabilistic approaches for PAPR suppression under high Doppler bins.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflecting Surface Aided Wireless Communication Systems: Joint Location and Passive Beamforming Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) technology has attracted significant attention as a novel approach to enhance wireless communication systems in recent years. By intelligently configuring its reflective elements, IRS can manipulate signal propagation, thereby improving desired signals while mitigating interference among users. In this paper, we study an IRS-aided multi-user wireless communication scenario, where the base station (BS) transmits various signals and each user receives their desired signals. To ensure fairness in wireless communications, the objective is to maximize the minimum user rates, considering the power constraint of the BS and the phase constraint of the IRS. Unlike prior works focusing mainly on optimizing BS and IRS beamforming, this study also addresses IRS location optimization. Since the problem is non-convex, it is decomposed into two subproblems and transformed into lower bound problems. Alternating optimization (AO) and successive convex approximation (SCA) methods are employed to solve these subproblems iteratively, aiming to converge the objective function within an acceptable range. Simulation results validate the convergence of the proposed algorithm and demonstrate performance improvements compared to benchmark schemes in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Research on Satellite Beam Tracking Method Based on Carrier Detection and BP Neural Network Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: A satellite beam tracking method based on carrier signal detection and back propagation (BP) neural network correction for combined navigation errors is proposed to address the issue of precise beam alignment of phased array antennas in broadband satellite communication. The phased array mobile communication antenna uses integrated navigation to obtain positioning and carrier attitude, performs coordinate transformation to calculate the alignment direction of the beam based on the position of the communication satellite. After completing initial alignment with the satellite, the phased array antenna detects the communication carrier wave continuously to find the optimal communication beam direction which is used as the expected output for the training of the BP neural network for combined navigation error suppression. After the training of the BP neural network is completed, the optimal beam direction for satellite communication can be directly obtained based on the combined navigation measurement and the phased array antenna beam can always be in a high gain working state, maintaining high bandwidth communication. Simulation shows that the satellite beam tracking method based on carrier detection and BP neural network correction can effectively suppress integrated navigation errors and improve satellite beam tracking accuracy. The tracking method does not rely on satellite beacon signals, simplifies system design, and reduces the precision requirements for integrated navigation selection.

articleTitle: Influence of AI on Network Security and Its Future Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, network security has become the focus of global attention. Hacking attacks, data leakage, network fraud and other threats emerge in an endless stream, bringing huge risks and losses to individuals, enterprises and countries. AI, as a powerful technical tool, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is gradually integrated into the field of network security, providing new ideas and methods for the defense and attack of network security. AI's learning and reasoning capabilities enable it to quickly identify and respond to complex network attacks, providing unprecedented protection capabilities for network security.

articleTitle: Outlier Detection Based On Heuristic Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Outlier detection is a basic problem in machine learning, which is widely used in industrial anomaly detection, network performance monitoring and activity monitoring. Most of the outlier detection algorithms are not effective in local outlier recognition, and can not distinguish the group points from the inner points in the data set with high outlier proportion. Moreover, the effectiveness of the algorithm is largely affected by the density and shape of the data set. This paper presents an outlier detection method based on heuristic clustering algorithm. The algorithm is divided into three stages. In the first stage, a heuristic clustering algorithm based on centroid learning is used to cluster the original data. In the second stage, the outlier score is calculated by the contraction distance of the target point, and the initial outlier identification is carried out. In the third stage, the "backward" mechanism is used to eliminate the "wrong points". The algorithm iterates through these three stages until the stop condition is met. In short, we propose a new outlier detection algorithm based on the heuristic clustering algorithm framework of centroid learning, and propose a "backward" mechanism to correct the wrong or wrong points. Finally, the validity of the proposed outlier detection algorithm is verified on both synthetic and real data sets.

articleTitle: A Point-interval Prediction Method for Photovoltaic Power Generation Considering Weather Types: a Novel Hybrid Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Temporal convolutional network (TCN) is suitable for photovoltaic power generation (PVPG) forecasting as it is an effective multi-scale feature learning and time series model. However, PVPG is typically influenced by multiple factors, and a single TCN cannot effectively capture complex nonlinear relationships. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-mechanism fusion model using TCN as the backbone network. First, integrating BiGRU into TCN enhances the model's ability to capture long-term dependencies within PV time-series data. Meanwhile, the attention mechanism (AM) is further utilized to assist the model in focusing on important features in PVPG. In addition, the power series are decomposed by variational mode decomposition (VMD) to reduce the fluctuations. Then a novel hybrid model, called VMD-TCN-BiGRU-AM, is developed. Finally, based on point prediction, the interval prediction is further conducted using quantile regression (QR) method. The experimental results indicate that the model proposed in this paper surpasses other models in terms of prediction performance and achieves superior prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the influencing factors of the spread of posts in the field of climate change - Take Sina Weibo as an example
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The challenge of climate change is serious, and China attaches great importance to it and takes measures, the frequent occurrence of meteorological disasters triggers public opinion, so it is necessary to understand the formation principle, evolution process, and influencing factors of public opinion. This paper uses the LDA topic identification method to extract four main discussion topics: economic development, climate change and environment, human impact of extreme climate, and weather, and analyses the differences in discussion hotspots between different cities. The study also found that emotional attitudes towards microblog information related to climate change negatively impact its reposting, the number of words and entries on the microblog had a positive impact on its reposting, and the activity, influence, identity category, and credibility of microblog authors had a positive impact on its reposting. It provides new insights into the government's management and guidance mechanisms.

articleTitle: Micromotion Gesture Recognition Technology Based on Millimeter-wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Different from the traditional FMCW radar signal processing method, this paper mainly explores the application of the time-frequency analysis method of the reflected intermediate frequency of millimeter wave radar in fretting detection. The radar echo data are analyzed by FFT, wavelet transform and Hilbert yellow transform. This topic mainly uses human gesture targets as the micromotion feature to detect. Under the three designed gestures, the time-frequency analysis method proposed in this topic combined with a convolutional neural network achieves a high recognition success rate. The motion detection technology proposed in this paper can be applied to millimeter wave radar under THE FMCW system. It can detect and classify tiny motions under complex backgrounds and show good recognition ability under strong interference. It can be used in medical treatment, automobile and other fields to play the role of accurate identification.

articleTitle: Gridless Parameter Estimation for Integrated Sensing and Communications in Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), positioned as a pivotal candidate technology for the next generation cellular mobile communications, can facilitate a broad spectrum of emerging applications. This paper focuses on studying the gridless target parameter estimation algorithm for ISAC, aimed at enhancing sensing ability and laying a solid foundation for precise environmental perception. Specifically, a novel search-free joint angle and delay estimation (JADE) method is introduced. We first formulate a gridless compressive sensing model with multiple spatial "snapshots", then derive an iterative solution for this atomic norm minimization (ANM) problem, and finally obtain angle and delay estimates via applying the two-dimensional matrix-pencil (MP) algorithm to ANM denoised signal. Numerical simulations are conducted in a typical cellular-signal-based ISAC scenario, demonstrating the superiority of this ANM-MP estimator to benchmark JADE algorithms. Particularly, when compared with the matrix-pencil approach, a reduction of 54% for the 90-th percentile error is achieved at the SNR of -10 dB.

articleTitle: Near-field Source DOA Estimation Algorithm Based on De-impact Function under Impulse Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In addressing the issue of localizing near-field source signals in the presence of impulse noise, this manuscript introduces a novel de-impact function designed for preprocessing received signals to alleviate the interference caused by impulse noise. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed de-impact function in effectively suppressing impulse noise. Furthermore, to augment estimation precision, a novel algorithm for near-field source localization is proposed. Building upon the framework of correlation entropy theory, a new correntropy covariance matrix is formulated to replace the original signal covariance matrix for signal processing. Through a succession of low-bias approximations between near-field and far-field scenarios, the algorithm converts the original 2-D search into 1-D operations. Additionally, the conventional spectral peak search is replaced by polynomial solving to further mitigate the computational complexity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Soft Multipath Information-Based UWB Tracking in Cluttered Scenarios: Preliminaries and Validations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate ultra-wideband (UWB) localization and tracking in cluttered environments. Instead of mitigating the multipath, we exploit the specular reflections to enhance the localizability and improve the positioning accuracy. With the assistance of the multipath, it is also possible to achieve localization purposes using fewer anchors or when the line-of-sight propagations are blocked. Rather than using single-value distance, angle, or Doppler estimates for the localization, we model the likelihoods of both the line-of-sight and specular multipath components, namely soft multipath information, and propose the multipath-assisted probabilistic UWB tracking algorithm. Experimental results in a cluttered industrial scenario show that the proposed algorithm achieves 46.4 cm and 33.1 cm 90th percentile errors in the cases of 3 and 4 anchors, respectively, which outperforms conventional methods with more than 61.8% improvement given fewer anchors and strong multipath effect.

articleTitle: A Dehazing Algorithm for Endoscopic Images Based on Cycle GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper tackles the intricate challenge of smoke elimination and the restoration of visual detail in endoscopic imaging, presenting a novel dehazing algorithm grounded in Cycle Generative Adversarial Networks (Cycle GANs). To meticulously retain image intricacies, our approach employs an encoder that assimilates smoke-laden endoscopic images post-Laplacian Pyramid Transformation and harnesses residual learning for extracting features across multiple scales. Innovatively, we introduce a Dark Channel Loss to augment differentiation between true scene colors and those distorted by fog, complementing the native Cycle GAN loss function. Additionally, we implement a Contrast Loss function to conserve image structural integrity and nuances, ensuring resultant images exhibit both clarity and vibrant, true-to-life colors. The foundation of our experimental dataset rests upon 11,296 laparoscopic images generously supplied by the Hamlyn Center and 544 synthetic smoke-infused test images, along with 238 genuine fog-embedded images sourced from public repositories of DaVinci’s official platform. Empirical assessments affirm that our proposed algorithm excels in efficiently mitigating residual smoke artifacts and enhancing the fineness of detail recovery. Remarkably, it also excels in reverting images to their pristine color fidelity while upholding a high degree of structural resemblance to the target images, thereby significantly advancing the field of endoscopic image dehazing.

articleTitle: YOLO-LRHG: Long Range Hand Gesture detection using YOLO with attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: The interpretation of hand gestures is crucial for effective non-verbal communication, particularly in HumanRobot Interaction (HRI). Despite the importance, existing research has mainly concentrated on short-range gesture recognition, inadequate for safe and effective interactions with mobile robots such as UAVs over longer distances. This study addresses this gap by exploring long-range hand gesture recognition using RGB images captured by webcams. We introduce the LRHG-10m dataset, which extends the original LRHG dataset with images captured at 8 to 10 meters in various indoor and outdoor environments. We evaluated seven attention mechanisms and the Ghost module for their performance in detecting small objects under low-parameter conditions. Our proposed YOLO-LRHG model integrates these mechanisms with an anchor-free approach, achieving an impressive mAP@0.5 of 98.5% with 3M parameters and 97.5% with 1.75M parameters, balancing computational efficiency, detection distance, and precision.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Cybersecurity: Enhancing Threat Detection and Defense in the Digital Age
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Information technology's swift progression has rendered network security a critical component of modern infrastructure. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized network security, particularly in threat detection and defense mechanisms. Leveraging its advanced data processing and pattern recognition capabilities, AI can forecast and counter potential network threats with enhanced precision and efficiency. The burgeoning global AI market reflects its expansive potential in bolstering network security. By emulating the neural networks of the human brain, AI bolsters threat detection rates, dynamically refines security strategies, and enables automated response and recovery from cyber-attacks. Studies suggest that AI's integration can markedly diminish the risk of network breaches and fortify the reliability of security measures.As the cyber landscape grows more intricate and threats evolve, ongoing innovation in AI is imperative for future advancements. The anticipation is that AI will assume an increasingly pivotal role in network security, offering robust defense against the escalating complexity of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Formation fracture pressure prediction with very small actual samples based on BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low prediction accuracy, high cost of obtaining actual measured samples, few actual samples in the traditional prediction process of drilling fracture pressure, a deep fracture pressure prediction method with very small actual samples based on Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) and transfer learning (fine-tuning) is proposed. The original logging data are taken as the features, and the fracture pressure is obtained by the formula method as the label. Thus, the empirical dataset is constructed. Logging features of natural gamma, well diameter and Young ’s modulus are selected by experiments. And then, the pre-training is performed using the empirical dataset. At last, in the fine-tuning stage, three models based on the actual measured data are obtained by the three-fold cross-validation training method, and the model with the best performance is selected to predict the fracture pressure. The experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the accuracy of formation fracture pressure prediction compared with the traditional formula method.

articleTitle: Efficient Multi-UAV Path Planning for Wireless Data Harvesting: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework designed to optimize the path planning of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for wireless data harvesting missions. The proposed approach leverages Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) with State-Action-Reward-State-Action (SARSA) and Q-learning algorithms to improve learning efficiency and overall performance.In our framework, UAVs operate in a decentralized manner, learning their policies independently through interactions with a grid-based environment that includes no-fly zones, buildings, start and landing zones, and sensor locations. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the DDQN-based algorithm significantly outperforms SARSA and Q-learning in terms of maximizing data collection, minimizing collisions, and achieving faster convergence, underscoring its potential to enhance UAV operations in dynamic

articleTitle: Intelligent Perception Method of Shipborne Radar Jamming Signal Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: To improve the jamming signal perception ability and anti-jamming performance of shipborne radar in complex environment, this paper proposes a visual perception method of jamming signal based on YOLOv8n. Firstly, the time-frequency image dataset of jamming signal is constructed, and the noise is suppressed by contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE). Second, the YOLOv8n object detection algorithm is used to realize the recognition and location of jamming signals. Then, combined with the location information of the jamming signal in the time-frequency image, the values of key parameter estimation can be obtained by numerical calculation. Finally, the values of parameter estimation are corrected by the Euclidean distance clustering algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that the jamming signal category perception precision of the proposed method can reach 98.01%, and the parameter estimation error is 2.36%, which is 7.47% lower than that before correction.

articleTitle: A Wideband Anti-Jamming Acquisition Algorithm Based on Fast FRFT for LEO Satellite Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites integrated with 5G/6G can fully leverage the advantages of both satellite and terrestrial communications to achieve global seamless coverage, addressing issues of terrestrial communication disruptions caused by natural disasters and other factors. However, satellite communication is susceptible to interference from natural or malicious high-power sources. Under the influence of jamming, the performance of the communication system can deteriorate significantly, reducing the reliability of signal transmission. To address the issues of low capture probability and large frequency offset estimation error caused by broadband interference in low-orbit satellite communication, a wideband anti-jamming acquisition algorithm based on Fast FRFT is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively suppresses wideband jamming and the acquisition time meets the real-time requirements of the satellite communication system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Channel Assignment for Wireless Mesh Networks Based on Multi-Intelligent Body Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: With the popularity of emerging applications and the diversification of IoT device needs, wireless mesh networks (WMN) have been recognized as an effective way to solve "last mile" coverage. In the scenario where the network environment status is unknown, an adaptive channel allocation algorithm based on multi-agent reinforcement learning is proposed to solve the problem that static channel allocation in wireless mesh network cannot adapt well to traffic changes in the network environment, resulting in the degradation of link communication quality. Map the channel allocation problem as a multi-agent reinforcement learning process. The state space based on multiple factors such as interference and load is established, and the relationship between exploration and utilization in the algorithm is balanced by using the improved greedy action selection mechanism, and the return function based on link satisfaction is designed to guide the channel selection to improve the quality of link communication. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively adapt to the dynamic changes of traffic and source nodes in the network to ensure the quality of user service.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Object Detection Algorithms for Wood Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the performance of YOLOv8, Faster R-CNN, and Mask R-CNN models in wood defect identification. The dataset, collected in collaboration with a timber company, includes 441 images of wood defects such as knots, oil streaks, black dots, and cracks. These images were annotated using the Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT). The study applied the three models to detect and localize wood defects, comparing their accuracy, detection speed, and precision. Faster R-CNN showed the fastest convergence and the best training results within 24 epochs, while YOLOv8 demonstrated robustness in complex backgrounds but slower mAP improvement. The results indicate the strengths and weaknesses of each model, providing insights for selecting the most suitable model based on specific application needs, and contributing to the development of efficient and automated wood defect detection methods.

articleTitle: Chaotic Weighting Random Integration-Based Data Augmentation for Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification With Extremely Small Sample Size
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: As a potential solution to improve wireless security, radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) is a lightweight access authentication technology. However, the existed deep learning (DL)-based RFFI methods are highly dependent on the training sample size. Therefore, serious overfitting problem will occur if the training samples are inadequate, which obstructs their practical applications. To address this issue, we propose an innovative data augmentation method to effectively expand the sample size. In this design, after data preprocessing, a random integration based data augmentation is applied to integrate several initial samples and generate new samples. Furthermore, compared with the existed methods, chaotic sequences are utilized to randomly set the integration weight of each initial sample, and thus enhancing the diversity of augmented samples. The superiority of the proposed chaotic weighting random integration-based (CWRI) data augmentation method in accuracy and generalization ability is validated by the hardware implementation on Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) portable radios.

articleTitle: Bayesian weighted Dynamic Distribution of Samples-based Remote Sensing Feature Selection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Feature selection is basic and important research for extracting valuable information from high-dimensional remote sensing features. However, high-dimensional data contains redundancy and noise that weakens the recognition results. Classical feature selection methods rely on feature discrimination measures and ignore the risk of subsequent recognition errors and waste feature discrimination performance by statically evaluating each feature using all samples. This paper proposes a Bayesian weighted Dynamic Distribution of Samples Feature Selection (DDSFS) algorithm using the Bayesian risk criterion. The algorithm is a forward search that uses the Parzen window to estimate the mutual information between features and categories. Then, the sample distribution is dynamically adjusted according to the recognized risk until the feature subset is selected. Using remote sensing images collected from Google Earth, the experimental results illustrate that the DDSFS has better performance than other typical feature selection algorithms for different classifiers, which illustrates the superiority of the approach.

articleTitle: SSM-YOLO: Lesion Detection Algorithm for Colorectal Polyps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In the medical field, the detection of colorectal polyp lesions via endoscopic images is challenged by complex backgrounds and numerous irrelevant factors, leading to lower detection rates, higher rates of missed diagnoses, and increased misdiagnosis in the early diagnosis of colorectal lesions. To improve diagnostic accuracy, this paper proposes a deep learning-based method named SSM-YOLO for detecting gastrointestinal polyps. This method integrates attention mechanisms, namely Shuffle Attention (SA) in the backbone and Second-Order Channel Attention (SOCA) in the head of the YOLOv7 network architecture. These mechanisms are designed to reduce background interference and minimize the impact of irrelevant factors. By enhancing the model's focus on target regions, they effectively improve the detection performance of the model. Furthermore, by replacing the CIOU loss function with MPDIOU, the enhanced model achieves better predictions of the boundary boxes for gastrointestinal polyps, bringing them closer to the true boxes and thus enhancing the accuracy of model detection. Experimental comparisons conducted on a dataset of augmented colorectal polyps demonstrate that the improved SSM-YOLOv7 model achieves a precision(P) rate of 98.8%, a recall(R) rate of 96.3%, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 98.8%. These results indicate improvements in all three metrics compared to the original model, confirming the effectiveness of the SSM-YOLOv7 model in detecting gastrointestinal polyp lesions.

articleTitle: Radar HRRP Estimation Based on Deep Unfolding Networks under Interrupted Sampling Repeater Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Radar high-resolution range profile (HRRP) estimation under interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) is a challenging task in complicated environments. In this paper, we modify two deep unfolding networks (DUNs), i.e., analytical learned iterative soft thresholding algorithm (ALISTA) and analytical learning proximal operator method (ALePOM), to work under various situations. We first detect and remove the interfered components in the received signal and then employ the modified DUNs to estimate the HRRP of target.
