Specifically, by taking pre-calculated matrices as input data, these two modified DUNs overcome the challenges of parameter tuning for traditional iterative sparse recovery methods and the dependence on specific dictionaries for existing DUNs, enabling their applications to various situations with changing radar parameters and/or jamming parameters. Furthermore, we outline the dataset construction and training schemes to improve the performance and reduce the training difficulty of the proposed methods. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed methods exhibit superior effectiveness and advantages in radar HRRP estimation under ISRJ.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing based CDL Modeling for C-V2X Scenarios with Multiple Roadside Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) communication has provided safer and more convenient interactions between vehicles and surroundings. To support the improvement of intelligent C-V2X communication, it is essential to understand the characteristics of the wireless channel. In this paper, channel measurement is performed in the urban C-V2X scenario at 5.915 GHz. The material electromagnetic (EM) parameters are calibrated based on the measured results, which are used for multipath data obtaining in ray-tracing (RT) simulation. After that, the clustered delay line (CDL) models for the C-V2X scenario are proposed to study the spatial characteristics of the significant multipath components. Related cluster and in-cluster parameters are extracted and analyzed based on CDL modeling. This paper provides useful calibrated EM parameters for extensive simulations. The complex channel data in the C-V2X scenarios with and without multiple roadside vehicles are effectively simulated and studied. The proposed CDL models can offer guidance for channel modeling research in the C-V2X scenario.

articleTitle: A Concatenated Mapping ZC Sequences Based Large-Capacity Grant-Free Random Access Preamble Design Method for Satellite Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: Satellite communication has garnered widespread attention due to its wide coverage and flexible deployment, and is expected to be a promising solution for achieving reliable access of ubiquitous Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Given the efficiency of grant-free random access (GF-RA) in massive machine-type communications, this paper investigates the preamble sequence design and detection issue for GF-RA in satellite-based IoT. Specifically, a concatenated mapping preamble is designed by concatenating orthogonal Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequences and multiple root ZC sequences processed through Kronecker product operations, which can effectively reduce the collision probability of preambles and further improve the detection performance of active users. In particular, the proposed method remarkably expands the capacity of the preamble set, thereby the users colliding in orthogonal sequences can be identified by detecting non-orthogonal sequences. Furthermore, we propose a two-stage multi-user detection method and theoretically derive the success detection probability of active users. Simulation results show that our proposed method can have a notable improved detection performance as compared to the existing ones.

articleTitle: A Novel Robust Adaptive Beamforming Algorithm Based on Steering Vector Estimation and Covariance Matrix Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: In low-orbit satellite communications, the use of adaptive beamforming technology can greatly improve the anti-interference performance of the receiver. Considering that adaptive beamforming is highly sensitive to any form of error, a robust adaptive beamforming technique, predicated on the reconstruction of the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix (INCM) and the estimation of the steering vector (SV), is proposed in this study. The method initially constructs SV error neighborhood tables for the desired and interference signals based on the results of the direction of arrival estimation. The SV that maximizes the multiple signal classification spectrum is then found in the tables as an estimate of the SVs of the desired and interfering signals. Subsequently, the interference covariance matrix is reconstructed based on the estimated interference SVs. Finally, the noise components are separated by projection, thus reconstructing the noise covariance matrix (NCM) and INCM. The proposed method reconstructs a more precise NCM compared with other methods, resulting in enhanced performance. Analysis of simulation results demonstrated that the proposed technique is effective and robust.

articleTitle: Robust Estimation of Lithium-ion Battery State of Health via Improved Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronic Information and Communication Technology (ICEICT)
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation of Lithium-ion battery (LIB) plays a crucial role in ensuring its safe and stable operation. Aiming at the problem of data-driven method that non-Gaussian noise may contained in the labeled values of LIB measurement data because it cannot be measured directly, this paper proposes a robust SOH estimation method combining extreme learning machine (ELM) and mixture generalized correntropy loss (MGCL) theory. Firstly, health factors (HFs) with high correlation with SOH are extracted from the measurement data to prepare the data for SOH estimation. Then the loss function of mean square error in traditional ELM framework is replaced by the MGCL to obtain a novel robust learning model (called ELM-MGCL). Finally, the proposed model is utilized for SOH estimation under three noise conditions, and the estimation results show that the proposed model can achieve acceptable SOH estimation accuracy compared to other models.
